The nearest play is TPC Sawgrass, Sawgrass Country Club, Marsh Landing Country Club and The Plantation, all a short drive east across the Intracoastal in 32082; the King & Bear and Slammer & Squire at World Golf Village and Palencia are south; Jacksonville Golf & Country Club and the Southside private clubs are north. So the pitch writes itself: a Nocatee resident pays club money and drives 15–25 minutes to practise. A one- or two-hole backyard green on a 30-foot yard means he putts before work. Sell the SMALL green here — 200–400 sq ft, two cups, a fringe, a chipping mat — as a realistic product for a builder lot, rather than the 800 sq ft complex that suits Ponte Vedra Beach and Palm Valley acreage.
facts.commercial_targets: SCHOOLS ARE THE STANDOUT AND THEY ARE ALL NEW: Palm Valley Academy, Pine Island Academy and Valley Ridge Academy (K-8) plus Allen D. Nease High School — playground fall zones, PE areas, courtyard surfaces, and Nease's athletic facilities. CDD AMENITY ASSETS: the Splash Water Park and Spray Park surrounds, Crosswater Hall lawns, the dog parks (Nocatee has dedicated dog parks — direct pet-turf targets that the CDD, not a homeowner, pays for), pickleball and tennis surrounds, event lawns and pool decks. That CDD amenity portfolio is one of the largest single-buyer opportunities in the service area and it recurs as new villages come online. DAYCARE AND PRESCHOOL: the childcare centres serving a community with a median age of 40.8 and thousands of young families — franchise and independent preschools around Nocatee Town Center. PET: veterinary and grooming businesses in Nocatee Town Center and along CR 210. HOA COMMON AREAS across ~50 neighbourhoods: entry medians, mail kiosks, amenity lawns. Also the model-home centres — every builder in Nocatee runs models, and a turf install at a model home is seen by every buyer in the community.
facts.landmarks: Splash Water Park and Spray Park — the two amenity centres every resident knows. Nocatee Town Center and Nocatee Station. The Greenway Trails and the kayak launch. Crosswater Hall. The golf-cart culture: Nocatee is a cart-legal community and residents drive carts to the amenity parks, which is a genuinely local detail worth a photo. The Nocatee Farmers Market and seasonal community events. Schools: Palm Valley Academy, Pine Island Academy, Valley Ridge Academy, and Allen D. Nease High School. Nocatee Parkway and the Crosswater Parkway interchange with US 1. Durbin Creek and the Guana River preserve edges. Neighbourhood names a local would use as shorthand: Twenty Mile, Del Webb Ponte Vedra, Coastal Oaks, Willowcove, Greenleaf Village, Austin Park, Daniel Park, Addison Park, Settlers Landing, The Outlook, Seabrook Village, Crosswinds.

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH SALT, WIND, DUNE SAND AND THE EMPTY HOUSE. Vilano Beach is the only place in this batch where grass loses to CHEMISTRY rather than to shade or drought — coquina-rich dune sand with no topsoil, a shallow salt-influenced water table, water that vanishes straight down, and constant onshore salt spray that burns St. Augustine and leaches fertiliser to the inlet within days. And it is the only place where the owner is not there to fix it: 28.7% of the island's 1,687 housing units are vacant, rental vacancy is 16.9%, median age is 58.9 and a third of residents are over 65. So the pitch is not aesthetics, it is ABSENCE — a yard that looks the same when you fly back in November as it did when you left in April, no irrigation controller to fail while nobody is watching, no landscaper to pay for a lawn that is dying anyway, and no sod to lay under a Phase III order that has banned new sod installation county-wide since 11 May 2026. This is a $625,790-median-value island of second homes and short-term rentals, and the highest-leverage customer is not a homeowner at all but the PROPERTY MANAGER holding dozens of units. Three more things make the page genuinely un-templatable: Vilano is a CDP with NO city government, so unlike St. Augustine across the Usina Bridge there is no municipal ordinance — but FDEP's Coastal Construction Control Line and FEMA flood zones DO apply, and saying so signals you have actually worked on the island; the product spec is different, needing UV and salt-resistant backing and infill, wind-uplift edge detail and a plan for blowing sand, plus real work on ELEVATED decks and terraces on piling-built homes where there is no ground-level yard at all; and the commercial list is hospitality — Cap's on the Water, Aunt Kate's, The Reef, Pesca Rooftop at the Hyatt Place — not schools and ballfields. Contrast it in one line: World Golf Village is a putting green, Mill Creek is a batting cage, Julington Creek is a shaded 25-year-old lawn, Switzerland is an acre with a dock, and Vilano Beach is a salt-blasted dune yard on a house that is empty half the year.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: Unincorporated St. Johns County — Vilano Beach is a CDP, not a city, so there is NO municipal ordinance and no city council; the City of St. Augustine's rules stop at the far side of the Usina Bridge and do not apply here. That is a real and checkable point of difference from the St. Augustine page. County-side, the Land Development Code contains no artificial or synthetic turf provision (verified by full-text search of Article V, 11 Aug 2025, and Article VI, 12 Jan 2026); the residential constraints are the Table 6.01 70% impervious surface ratio and district setbacks. LDC Sec. 6.06.02.A.5 bars artificial plants from satisfying required landscaping on permitted development, which matters for condo and hotel projects on the island but not for a homeowner. THE ISLAND-SPECIFIC LAYER NOBODY ELSE HAS: Florida's Coastal Construction Control Line. FDEP's CCCL programme regulates structures and activities seaward of the line that can cause beach erosion, destabilise dunes, damage upland property or interfere with public access, and CCCL permits also protect sea turtles and dune plants; the rules are at Chapter 62B-33 F.A.C., contact CCCL@FloridaDEP.gov or 850-245-8570. Any oceanfront job near the dune should be checked against the CCCL before a quote is signed — FDEP does not publish a plain-language landscaping answer, so confirm case by case rather than asserting. Add FEMA flood-zone status and, in the town centre, condo association approval. County fertilizer rule still applies: 5 lbs N per 1,000 sf per year, none under storm watch/warning — a rule that argues for itself on an island draining straight to the inlet.
facts.water_and_rules: Provider: JEA. JEA supplies water from Ponte Vedra south to Vilano Beach along A1A, through the Ponte Vedra and Ponce de Leon grids and the Palm Valley system via an interconnection with the St. Johns County Utility Department — so Vilano is on JEA's coastal grid, not the county's inland system. Status at 2026-09-07: SJRWMD Phase III Extreme Water Shortage, declared 11 May 2026 and still in force across St. Johns County. One irrigation day per week — odd or no address Saturday, even Sunday, nonresidential Tuesday — nothing between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m., 3/4 inch and one hour per zone maximum, and NEW SOD INSTALLATION AND NEW PLANTINGS PROHIBITED, along with aesthetic water uses, street and pressure washing. Standard schedule when it lifts: DST odd Wed+Sat / even Thu+Sun / nonres Tue+Fri; EST odd Sat / even Sun / nonres Tue; never 10 a.m.-4 p.m. County reclaimed water does not reach the island — only Twin Creeks and SilverLeaf have it. No artificial turf rebate found in St. Johns County. The restriction that actually bites hardest here is not legal but practical: a one-day-a-week schedule assumes somebody is home to notice a broken head or a controller that reset, and on an island where 28.7% of units are vacant, nobody is.
facts.soil_and_yard: Completely different ground from the other four, and this is where the page earns its keep. Vilano is a barrier island, so the profile is marine dune and beach sand — coquina-rich shelly sand rather than the inland Myakka flatwoods spodosol — with a shallow, salt-influenced water table and essentially no organic topsoil. Water disappears straight down, which means natural turf needs constant irrigation just to survive and fertiliser leaches immediately. Salt spray and onshore wind burn St. Augustine and kill anything not salt-tolerant. Much of Vilano sits in a FEMA FLOOD ZONE, lender-mandated flood insurance is normal, elevation drives both cost and resilience, and newer homes are built on pilings — so a meaningful share of usable outdoor space is elevated deck, terrace or under-house area rather than ground-level yard. Shade is minimal: no live oak canopy problem here, the opposite — full sun, full wind, full salt. Practical install consequences: specify UV and salt-resistant backing and infill, plan for wind uplift at edges and on elevated decks, expect sand migration and blowing sand fouling, and treat the base as free-draining from the start. Beach driving is permitted seasonally in places, and the shoreline is actively managed, so anything near the dune line needs care.
facts.housing_stock: A barrier-island CDP on the southern tip of San Pablo Island, directly north of the St. Augustine Inlet, with the Atlantic on one side and the Tolomato/Matanzas River on the other. 1.80 sq mi total, 1.77 sq mi of land. Population 2,514 at the 2020 census — DOWN from 2,678 in 2010 — and 2,512 as of 1 July 2024. This is by far the smallest place in the batch and the only one shrinking. 1,687 housing units, and the number that should shape the whole page: 28.7% VACANT, with a 16.9% rental vacancy rate. That is a second-home and vacation-rental island, not a commuter suburb. Housing runs from modest 1970s concrete-block beach cottages through condos and townhomes to piling-elevated modern coastal custom homes and large oceanfront estates. Four distinct pockets: PORPOISE POINT at the southern inlet end, with deep-water lots and boat access, home to the priciest waterfront in the area; the VILANO TOWN CENTER, walkable around the pier and boardwalk, with a mix of condos and townhomes and vintage hotel buildings; the A1A OCEANFRONT CORRIDOR of single-family homes and condos; and SOUTH PONTE VEDRA BEACH running north, larger oceanfront estates with a remote, low-density feel. Estimated median house or condo value $625,790 (2023) — the highest per-square-foot ground in this batch. Lots are narrow and deep in the classic barrier-island pattern, so usable rear yards are often small, walled or decked, and many are elevated above the ground plane on pilings. HOA presence is patchy: condo and townhome associations in the town centre, some covenants in newer subdivisions, and plenty of older cottage lots with none.
facts.who_lives_there: The demographic outlier of the batch, and the page must reflect it. Median age 58.9 at the 2020 census. Only 11.1% of residents are under 18; 32.7% are 65 or older. 56.0% married-couple households. 91.4% White, 4.9% Hispanic or Latino. Most residents own. Areavibes describes it as a sparse suburban feel with an average age around 44 across all residents, but the census age structure is the reliable figure. Combine that with 28.7% vacancy and the picture is clear: retirees and near-retirees who own outright, plus a large float of second-home owners and short-term-rental investors who are not on the island most of the year. School zoning confirms the low child count — Keterlinus Elementary, Sebastian Middle and St. Augustine High School, all on the mainland in St. Augustine, not on the island. ZIP 32095 median household income is $128,915 (Dec 2025), third-highest in St. Johns County, though that ZIP reaches well inland to Palencia and should not be presented as Vilano's own figure.
facts.golf: There is no golf course in Vilano Beach — the island is 1.8 square miles wide and there is no room for one. Say it plainly. The nearest real golf is THE PALENCIA CLUB, 600 Palencia Club Dr, St. Augustine 32095, a 7,071-yard Arthur Hills design under mature live oaks running down to the Intracoastal, in the same ZIP code and a short drive west over the Usina Bridge or up US 1. Beyond that, King & Bear and Slammer & Squire at World Golf Village (32092) and St. Johns Golf & Country Club (205 St Johns Golf Dr) are 20-30 minutes inland. For this page golf is a SECONDARY pitch — a compact backyard or rooftop-terrace green for a retiree or a second-home owner who plays at Palencia, not a championship-course identity. Do not lead with it.
facts.commercial_targets: Hospitality first — this is a lodging and restaurant economy, not a school-and-ballfield one. HYATT PLACE VILANO BEACH (and Pesca Rooftop, a rooftop terrace that is a natural synthetic-turf application). HOLIDAY INN EXPRESS & SUITES. OCEANVIEW LODGE. CAP'S ON THE WATER, AUNT KATE'S and THE REEF — all outdoor-seating waterfront restaurants where salt, sand and foot traffic destroy grass. The Publix-anchored town centre. Condo and townhome associations around the pier and boardwalk for pool decks, courtyards and dog relief areas. The Vilano Beach Pier and boardwalk area. Vacation-rental and property-management companies — on an island with 28.7% vacancy and 16.9% rental vacancy, the property manager who maintains dozens of units is a single relationship worth more than any homeowner. Pet businesses and dog-friendly rentals: Vilano welcomes leashed dogs, which makes pet turf a genuine repeat product here. Schools are OFF-island in St. Augustine — Keterlinus Elementary, Sebastian Middle, St. Augustine High — so treat them as St. Augustine targets, not Vilano ones.
facts.landmarks: The FRANCIS AND MARY USINA BRIDGE carrying A1A over the inlet to the St. Augustine historic district, with a roughly 0.2-mile boardwalk beneath it through the salt marsh linking the residential side to the town centre. The VILANO BEACH PIER on the river side of the Matanzas, free for sightseeing and fishing, with sculptures along it including the blue bird of happiness, and the best vantage point for sunset over downtown St. Augustine. PORPOISE POINT at the southern end, for fishing and launching jet skis. CAP'S ON THE WATER. AUNT KATE'S, next to the Usina boat ramp, tracing to 1900 when Henry Flagler asked the Usina family for fresh oysters. THE REEF. PESCA ROOFTOP at the Hyatt Place. The Publix-anchored town centre and its vintage hotel buildings. Hyatt Place Vilano Beach, Holiday Inn Express & Suites, Oceanview Lodge. The Dolphin Bay Scenic Shuttle to downtown. Seasonal four-wheel-drive beach access. Annual events a local would name: the Florida Skimboarding Pro/Am in August, the Vilano Bridge Run 5K/10K in spring, the Whiskey Wine & Wildlife Festival, June kingfish tournaments.

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH THE SLOPE AND THE SAND ON A $1M LAKE LOT, NOT WITH THE MILITARY BASE. The page's headline should be the one problem no other town in this service area has: a lot on Trail Ridge that runs downhill into the clearest lake in northeast Florida, on deep droughty dune sand that will not hold grass on a grade, in a district where the sprinkler is now legally limited to one day a week. Everything else follows from that. The washout between the house and the dock, sand tracking onto steps and shoreline, the bare patches that come back every spring, and the fact that a properly based, pinned, edge-restrained turf slope fixes it permanently. Bolt on the water-quality argument, which is genuinely persuasive to this specific buyer and unavailable anywhere else: Kingsley is oligotrophic with 7.2 feet of visibility, and turf means zero fertilizer and zero herbicide draining off your lot into it. That is a different lead from every neighbor. Middleburg is rural acreage. Clay Hill is dog runs and pasture. Keystone Heights is a small lake town. Kingsley Lake is a tiny, geographically gated ring of $1M-$2.4M waterfront homes with a slope-erosion problem and an environmental conscience, where inventory almost never comes up and the competitive field is empty because nobody drives out SR 16. This is the one page in the western half of the territory that can legitimately carry $10-12 per square foot pricing, and it should be written as a premium waterfront page, not a rural one. Treat Camp Blanding as the page's second half and its credibility engine: name the museum, the WWII history and the 73,000 acres because every local knows them, use the installation as the commercial and government-contracting pitch, and be explicit that a 3,000-bunk tent-and-barracks training post is not a family housing market. HONESTY NOTE for the parent agent: this is a very small residential universe, likely a few hundred homes. It deserves a short, sharp, high-ticket page rather than a long one, and its real job is to be the highest-margin lead-per-visit page on the site, not a traffic page.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: Three separate regimes and they should not be blurred. (1) Private Kingsley Lake homes sit in unincorporated Clay County with no HOA or CDD of consequence, meaning no architectural review, but shoreline and near-water work may trigger county environmental setbacks or SJRWMD permitting given proximity to the lake. VERIFY before promising a permit-free install on a waterfront lot. (2) Any work on Camp Blanding is state or federal contracting through the Florida National Guard / Florida Department of Military Affairs, not a residential sale and not a county permit; it needs base access, registration and a procurement pathway, and the page should treat that as a business-development note rather than a call-to-action. (3) I could not access the Clay County Land Development Code (Municode 403, county site unreachable), so I found no evidence for or against a synthetic turf provision; confirm with Clay County Development Services. Statewide and confirmed: Florida Statute 373.185 stops deed restrictions and local ordinances from prohibiting Florida-Friendly Landscaping but does not explicitly mention or protect artificial turf, so do not claim state-law protection for turf.
facts.water_and_rules: Private wells, no municipal utility, and the same regulatory lever as everywhere else in the district but with sharper teeth here. The St. Johns River Water Management District's Phase III Extreme Water Shortage order was still in effect as of July 2026 and explicitly applies to ground and surface water and to private wells and pumps. Under Phase III: irrigation is limited to one day a week (odd or no address Saturday, even Sunday, nonresidential Tuesday), prohibited 8 a.m. to 6 p.m., capped at three-quarters of an inch and one hour per zone, with only a tapering establishment window for new sod (daily 15 days, three days a week for 30, two days a week for 15). Clay and Bradford counties are both named. SJRWMD leadership stated the area needs roughly three feet of rain over three months to return to normal, and the most severe shortage zones are in the western and northwestern district, which is exactly this location. Golf course fairway irrigation is also cut to one day a week under the order, which is a useful talking point for any club conversation. Rebates: none found from SJRWMD or Clay County Utility Authority that would cover artificial turf. Do not imply one. Camp Blanding operates its own installation systems; any work there goes through state military channels, not a county utility.
facts.soil_and_yard: This is the technically distinctive field for this page and it is genuinely unlike anywhere else in the service area. Kingsley Lake sits on Trail Ridge, a relict sand ridge that is one of Florida's highest natural elevations, and Camp Blanding contains Clay County's highest point at 259 feet against a county average of 95 feet. The soil is deep, droughty, fast-draining relict dune sand, not the flatwoods hardpan found across the rest of Clay County. So the failure mode is inverted: this is not a standing-water problem, it is a nothing-holds-water problem. Grass on these lots goes droughty and thin, and the sand simply will not carry turfgrass on a slope. Every lakefront lot pitches downhill toward the water, so the recurring homeowner complaint is bare patches, washouts and gullies between the house and the dock, and sand migrating onto steps, walkways and the shoreline. That makes properly based, edge-restrained, pinned turf on a slope the actual product being sold here, not a decorative lawn. Second technical hook: the lake is oligotrophic, very low nutrient, high clarity, with a 2024 Secchi depth of 7.2 feet, pH about 5.9, dissolved oxygen 8.5 mg/L, and its sandy bottom slopes gently before dropping sharply into the central basin. Owners are protective of that clarity. Eliminating fertilizer and herbicide from a lot that drains straight into Kingsley is an environmental argument that is real here and impossible to make in a Nocatee subdivision.
facts.housing_stock: Two completely different markets sharing one map pin, and the page must separate them or it will read as nonsense. (1) CAMP BLANDING JOINT TRAINING CENTER is a roughly 73,000-acre Florida National Guard installation in Clay County near Starke that physically includes Kingsley Lake. It is not a residential base. Housing capacity is about 3,000 military personnel at a time and accommodations are tents and barracks-type buildings for temporary training; there is no permanent family housing community to sell to. It is about 8 miles from Starke and 36 miles southeast of Jacksonville, with a Starke 32091 mailing address despite sitting in Clay County. (2) KINGSLEY LAKE is the residential opportunity: a nearly circular 2,000-acre sinkhole lake nicknamed the Silver Dollar Lake, max depth 82 ft, average about 40 ft, surface elevation 174 ft, sitting on Trail Ridge. Roughly half the shoreline lies inside Camp Blanding; the rest is private residences. There are no public boat ramps and no public beach, so the ring of private homes is small, tightly held and effectively gated by geography. Live inventory bears that out: 7 listings totaling $5.5M, ranging from $175,000 vacant lots to a $2,390,000 waterfront home, with 3-6 bedroom houses on parcels up to 4.42 acres, described as a very tight, low-inventory market. Housing type is old multi-generational lake camps and cottages passed down within Jacksonville and north Florida families, mixed with newer large custom builds. Lots are deep and run downhill to the water. No HOA of consequence, no CDD.
facts.who_lives_there: On the installation itself: essentially a transient training population, not residents. Around the lake: two groups. First, legacy lakefront families, often second- or third-generation owners of camps used as weekend and summer houses by Jacksonville households, which is why inventory almost never turns over. Second, newer high-net-worth owners building or buying at the $1-2.4M end. Ambient ZIP data is misleading and should NOT be used as the customer profile: ZCTA 32091 (Starke) has 14,719 people over 152.1 sq mi, median household income $62,852, median home value $206,200, poverty 16.6%, bachelor's degrees only 18.1%, veterans 7.9% (about 25% above the national rate, reflecting Camp Blanding). Kingsley Lake is the wealthy outlier inside a poor ZIP; a $2.39M lakefront listing sits in a ZIP whose median home is $206,200. Say that plainly in internal notes so nobody prices this page off the ZIP median. Nearby Keystone Heights, the closest incorporated town to the south on SR 21, had 1,446 residents in 2020, 83.7% non-Hispanic white, median age 38.1.
facts.golf: Confirmed finding: there is no golf course on Kingsley Lake and none on Camp Blanding that I could verify. The nearest Clay County clubs are 20-40 minutes away in the Green Cove Springs, Middleburg and Oakleaf corridor. VERIFICATION WARNING: I could not confirm any course names from a live source this session (golflink, golfpass, exploreclay and the club sites returned 403/DNS errors and the search budget was exhausted). The names to check before publishing are Magnolia Point Golf and Country Club in Green Cove Springs, The Ravines Golf Club in Middleburg, and Eagle Landing Golf Club at Oakleaf. Also worth verifying: whether Camp Blanding retains any golf facility from its WWII era, which I could not confirm either way. The commercial reading is the same as Clay Hill but with a much better wallet behind it: a Kingsley Lake owner with a $1M+ lake house is 30-45 minutes from the nearest course, which is exactly the profile that buys a real backyard practice green rather than a novelty one.
facts.commercial_targets: The best commercial list of any small place in this service area, because the installation itself is the target. On or tied to Camp Blanding: parade and ceremony ground surfacing, PT and unit fitness areas, indoor training and gym spaces, troop billeting common areas, the Camp Blanding Museum and Memorial Park grounds (currently renovating Cooper Hall and actively fundraising for expansion, which is a live opening), and the K-9 and working-dog areas associated with the Multijurisdictional Counterdrug Task Force Training and the Combating Transnational Organized Crime Center of Excellence. Off-installation: Keystone Heights schools and the city's recreation facilities, Keystone Heights Airport (42J) terminal grounds, Starke-area daycares, kennels and veterinary practices, and lakefront homeowners' shared docks, steps and beach approaches. Camp Immokalee's waterfront and field areas are a strong prospect if confirmed. Be clear internally that government work here means procurement and base access, not a driveway estimate.
facts.landmarks: Camp Blanding Museum and Memorial Park, 5629 SR 16 West, Building 3040, Starke FL 32091, phone (904) 682-3196, established 1990, sitting outside the main entrance with WWII-era buildings, vehicles, aircraft and unit memorials. The SR 16 main gate. Kingsley Lake itself, the Silver Dollar Lake, with no public ramp or beach. Trail Ridge and the 259-foot Clay County high point on the installation. SR 21 (Blanding Boulevard) running north to Middleburg and Orange Park. Starke about 8 miles west, Jacksonville about 36 miles northwest, Keystone Heights just south. Keystone Heights Airport (FAA 42J), a public general aviation field 3 miles north of Keystone Heights. The Keystone Heights Moon Tree, an Apollo 14 sycamore planted at the library in 1984. The WWII history is unusually strong recognition material: more than 800,000 soldiers trained at Blanding, nine infantry divisions between 1940 and 1943, and a POW camp holding German prisoners from 1942-46. Current tenants include the 53rd Infantry Brigade Combat Team, 3rd Battalion 20th Special Forces Group, the 125th Regional Support Group and the 202nd RED HORSE Squadron. VERIFY before publishing: Camp Immokalee (Boy Scout camp said to be on Kingsley Lake) and Mike Roess Gold Head Branch State Park near Keystone Heights; both are very likely correct but I could not confirm them from a live source this session.

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH THE PUTTING GREEN, BUILT TO A STANDARD THE CUSTOMER CAN MEASURE AGAINST TPC SAWGRASS. Nowhere else in the service area can you say: your neighbour works at the PGA TOUR, you play a course Pete Dye built, and THE PLAYERS is in your ZIP code every March. That means this page must NOT sell 'artificial grass' — it must sell a short-game facility, quoted the way a club project is quoted: stimp-rated nylon putting surface, specified undulation and contour, cut cups, fringe collar, a chipping pad at a stated distance, sand-set bunker integration, and a base spec you publish. Price it at $10–12/sq ft and up and let the spec justify it; this is the single best town in the whole four-county area for that price point. Then the second layer, which is genuinely local and not a template: SALT AND SHADE AND A DROUGHT ORDER. Onshore salt aerosol burns St. Augustine along Ponte Vedra Boulevard, the live oaks over those streets deny it the sun it needs, the boulevard's shallow irrigation wells can run brackish, and since 11 May 2026 St. Johns County has been under a Phase III order that limits everyone to one watering day a week and PROHIBITS NEW SOD OUTRIGHT. A homeowner whose lawn died this summer legally cannot replace it with grass right now. Third differentiator to state explicitly, because it separates this page from Nocatee's: on the boulevard corridor there is often no HOA — your approval runs through St. Johns County and the Ponte Vedra Zoning and Adjustment Board, which meets the first Monday of the month. Say you handle that submittal. HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM THE TOWN NEXT DOOR: Ponte Vedra Beach is the ocean side, the old money, the clubs and the 30%-over-65 retiree with a handicap. Palm Valley, a mile west across the same ZIP, is the marsh side and the drainage job. Ponte Vedra 32081 is new-build small lots. Do not let these three pages share a paragraph.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: THIS IS THE MOST DISTINCTIVE REGULATORY SITUATION IN THE BATCH AND IT IS A GENUINE PAGE DIFFERENTIATOR. Ponte Vedra Beach is unincorporated — there is no city hall — but it has something no other unincorporated place here has: the PONTE VEDRA ZONING DISTRICT, governed by the Ponte Vedra Zoning District Regulations (Ordinance No. 2020-38) and administered by the PONTE VEDRA ZONING AND ADJUSTMENT BOARD (PVZAB), a board appointed by the St. Johns County Board of County Commissioners that meets the first Monday of each month at 3:00 p.m. in the County Auditorium, 500 San Sebastian View, St. Augustine. PVZAB reviews and takes final action on building height and size, intensity of land use, area of yards and open space around buildings, and the location of buildings designed for specified uses within the district. The zoning regulations date to 1965 and the overlay district was added in 1997 as a guideline for the coastal corridor. Practical translation for the page: on the Ponte Vedra Boulevard corridor your approval path runs through the county and PVZAB, not an HOA — while inside Sawgrass Players Club, Sawgrass Country Club, Marsh Landing and The Plantation you go through a private ARC. Countywide, the St. Johns County LDC requires Florida-Friendly landscaping on new development with at least half of planted species native and at least half the irrigated area on low-volume irrigation, and caps Impervious Surface Ratio per the Comprehensive Plan — note that ISR counts 'compacted materials', so document your base permeability rather than assume turf is automatically pervious. Overriding all of it: Fla. Stat. § 125.572 (HB 683, ch. 2025-140, effective 1 July 2025) bars the county from prohibiting DEP-compliant synthetic turf on single-family residential parcels of one acre or less — but it does not override private covenants, so Marsh Landing's ARC still gets a submittal.
facts.water_and_rules: Potable water is St. Johns County Utility Department; a meaningful number of the older oceanfront and boulevard properties also irrigate from PRIVATE SHALLOW WELLS, which are still subject to the shortage order. St. Johns County is under PHASE III EXTREME WATER SHORTAGE declared 11 May 2026 — Extreme Drought (D3), the highest classification recorded in Florida since 2000. Rules: irrigation ONE DAY PER WEEK only; nothing between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m.; odd or no address SATURDAY, even address SUNDAY, non-residential TUESDAY; maximum 3/4 inch and one hour per zone; NO NEW SOD INSTALLATION AND NO NEW PLANTINGS; aesthetic water uses prohibited; street and pressure washing restricted; and it applies to private wells and pumps as well as utility water. Reclaimed water is exempt from the one-day limit. Micro-spray, micro-jet, drip and bubbler are allowed anytime. Normal schedule when no shortage is declared: odd Wed/Sat, even Thu/Sun, non-residential Tue/Fri during daylight saving, dropping to one day in Eastern Standard Time, avoiding 10 a.m.–4 p.m., one hour per zone. New landscaping normally gets a 30-day unrestricted establishment window then alternating days for a further 30 — but Phase III has suspended new sod entirely. County fertilizer rule: max 5 lb nitrogen per 1,000 sq ft per year, nothing within 10 feet of surface water. Enforcement: St. Johns County Code Enforcement (904) 209-0734, or report via the SJC Connect app. NO TURF REBATE EXISTS — verify before making any claim.
facts.soil_and_yard: San Pablo Island is a barrier-island landform: deep, fine, near-white quartz sand with almost no organic content and effectively no water-holding capacity on the ocean side, grading to a high water table and salt-marsh organic muck as you move west toward the Intracoastal. (Landform and setting are sourced; specific soil series are installer field knowledge — confirm per-parcel via USDA Web Soil Survey.) Three field problems define the work here. SALT: onshore aerosol burns St. Augustine and Zoysia along the boulevard corridor, and irrigation drawn from shallow coastal wells can be brackish enough to make it worse — turf is immune to both. SHADE: mature live oaks and cabbage palms canopy much of the boulevard corridor and the older Sawgrass streets, so the same 4–6 hour sun problem as Riverside applies here, just under more expensive houses. DRAINAGE PARADOX: the sand drains too fast on the dune side (irrigation runs straight through, which is why these yards need so much water) and too slowly on the marsh side. Slope is minimal; dune-face lots have real grade change. On golf-frontage lots the yard usually falls toward the course or a lagoon, which is an asset if you build the base to use it.
facts.housing_stock: Unincorporated, on San Pablo Island, about 18 miles southeast of downtown Jacksonville, in what is Florida's wealthiest county. ZIP 32082 holds roughly 31,861–36,683 people depending on source and vintage. Median home value $792,600 in the ZIP-level data, with average sale prices around $898,000 as of April 2024 — home values in the ZIP are up about 68% (+$322,000) since 2011. Four distinct sub-stocks, and they are four different jobs: (1) THE PONTE VEDRA BOULEVARD CORRIDOR — 1930s–1950s original oceanfront and second-row cottages and estates, many since torn down and rebuilt at 6,000–12,000 sq ft; big irregular lots, dune frontage, mature live oaks and cabbage palms, no HOA in the conventional sense but county overlay review; (2) SAWGRASS PLAYERS CLUB and SAWGRASS COUNTRY CLUB — 1970s–1980s gated golf-course homes, villas and patio homes on tight golf-frontage lots with strong associations; (3) MARSH LANDING COUNTRY CLUB — 1980s–1990s gated, ICW and marsh-front, half-acre-plus, heavy covenant control; (4) THE PLANTATION AT PONTE VEDRA BEACH — 1990s–2000s low-density gated golf. Add continuous teardown/rebuild infill throughout. HOA prevalence is very high inside the gates and effectively zero on parts of Ponte Vedra Boulevard, which is a real sales-cycle difference. This is historic-plus-luxury-rebuild, not new-build suburbia.
facts.who_lives_there: Median household income $138,877 in the ZIP-level data and $150,646 in the community-level figure; per capita income $88,539 against a US figure of $44,673; only 4.4% below the poverty line. THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT DEMOGRAPHIC FACT: 30.1% of residents are over 65, against just 16.4% under 18. This is a retiree and semi-retiree market with time, discretionary income and a golf habit — not a young-family market. Median age 53.1. 70.6% hold a college degree, 39.7% a STEM degree, and only 3.0% stopped at high school. Employment skews professional/scientific/technical services 14.3%, healthcare 13.8%, finance and insurance 11.5%. Unemployment 1.9%. 87.7% white non-Hispanic. These are people who buy on craftsmanship, references and finish quality, and who will absolutely notice a bad seam or a wrong shade of green — but who are not price-shopping three quotes on Facebook. This is the $10–12/sq ft customer the client wants.
facts.golf: The best golf address in Florida outside of a handful, and the reason this page exists. TPC SAWGRASS — home of THE PLAYERS Championship, permanent host since 1982, played in March; two Pete Dye championship courses, THE PLAYERS Stadium Course with the par-3 17th island green (the most photographed hole in American golf) and Dye's Valley Course. THE PGA TOUR'S WORLD HEADQUARTERS is in Ponte Vedra Beach; so is the ATP Tour's headquarters. SAWGRASS COUNTRY CLUB — private, member-owned, established 1974; the Ed Seay course hosted THE PLAYERS from 1977 to 1981. PONTE VEDRA INN & CLUB — the original 1928 resort, Ocean Course and Lagoon Course, both reworked by resident architect Bobby Weed; plus The Lodge & Club. MARSH LANDING COUNTRY CLUB — private championship 18 through Intracoastal marsh, tidal creeks and lagoons, with 10 lighted Har-Tru courts and a resort pool. THE PLANTATION AT PONTE VEDRA — 18 holes, par 72, 7,141 yards. SAWGRASS MARRIOTT GOLF RESORT & SPA. Jacksonville Beach Golf Club is minutes north. No other town in the batch is remotely close to this concentration, and the page must trade on it explicitly and by name.
facts.commercial_targets: GOLF FIRST: TPC Sawgrass practice areas and clubhouse landscape, Sawgrass Country Club, Marsh Landing Country Club, The Plantation, Ponte Vedra Inn & Club and The Lodge & Club, Sawgrass Marriott — tee-line surfaces, chipping and putting practice areas, cart-path aprons, pool decks, terrace and event lawns, and club fitness-centre flooring. HOSPITALITY: Ponte Vedra Inn & Club, The Lodge & Club, Sawgrass Marriott, the Ponte Vedra Concert Hall grounds, Sawgrass Village retail courtyards. CORPORATE: PGA TOUR headquarters campus and ATP Tour headquarters — the highest-prestige logo either of them could ever put on a portfolio, and both are golf/tennis organisations that understand playing surfaces. SCHOOLS: Ponte Vedra High School, Landrum Middle School, Ocean Palms Elementary, plus private options. HOA COMMON AREAS: the gated communities' entry medians, amenity centres, pickleball surrounds and pool decks are recurring accounts. PET: veterinary practices and boarding along A1A and JTB, plus resort-property pet relief areas. MEDICAL: Baptist Medical Center Beaches and Mayo Clinic Florida are just north — courtyard and therapy-garden surfaces.
facts.landmarks: The 17th island green at TPC Sawgrass. THE PLAYERS Championship in March. The PGA TOUR world headquarters campus. The ATP Tour headquarters on ATP Tour Boulevard. The Ponte Vedra Inn & Club and The Lodge & Club, the 1928 resort that started the town. Mickler's Landing beach access at the south end. The Guana Tolomato Matanzas National Estuarine Research Reserve and the Guana Dam. Ponte Vedra Concert Hall. Sawgrass Village and the Sawgrass Marriott. The Ponte Vedra Recorder, the local paper. The town's origin story is worth a line: it began as MINERAL CITY, a titanium and mineral sands mining settlement after the 1914 discovery, and was renamed Ponte Vedra by the National Lead Company in 1929 after a Spanish coastal town — the beach people play golf on is literally an old strip mine.

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH THE SOIL, BY NAME: "There is a USDA soil series called Mandarin. It was established in 1977, its type location is in Duval County, and it is the reason your lawn keeps failing." No competitor in northeast Florida will run that line, it is completely verifiable, and it is the rare hyper-local fact that is also the technical truth — Mandarin-series fine sand holds nothing in the dry season and perches a water table 18 to 42 inches down from June through December, so the same yard scorches in April and bogs in September. Wrap the neighborhood's own identity around it: the moss-draped ancient live oaks of Mandarin Road that everyone loves are also casting the shade and running the surface roots that finish the grass off. Then close on the economics, because Mandarin's buyer profile is the best in the batch for premium work: median household income $95,347 and median home value $409,900 in 32223 (both about 20% above metro), median age 47.1, 45% college-educated, 12% veterans, and only 9.1% moved house in the past year. These are people who are STAYING — exactly who buys a 15-year product with a real warranty instead of the cheapest bid, and exactly who refers neighbours they have known twenty years. Fundamentally different from every neighbour: San Jose leads on a Donald Ross golf address, Beauclerc on young families and pet-and-play, San Marco on preservation taste and riverfront drainage, Miramar on century-old shade over tiny bungalow yards. Mandarin leads on SOIL SCIENCE AND PERMANENCE — the biggest, flattest, most private backyards in the batch, on the worst-behaving ground, owned by the people least likely to move. Secondary hook worth its own section: no country club inside Mandarin, so build the green at home.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: Duval is a consolidated city-county — Jacksonville's single code, no separate Mandarin municipality, no town council, no local architectural board. I could NOT reach Municode (403) to verify an express artificial-turf provision in Chapter 656 Part 12 landscape regulations — verify before asserting anything about the code. The governing layer in Mandarin is HOA AND CDD COVENANTS, and it varies sharply by housing layer: historic Mandarin Road and riverfront parcels are essentially unassociated; the 1970s–90s wave is mixed; the 1990s–2000s subdivisions in the 32257/32258 spillover carry active associations and, in newer Bartram/Greenland product, CDD-governed common areas. Give homeowners the real legal position: FLORIDA STATUTE 373.185 BARS LOCAL GOVERNMENTS AND DEED RESTRICTIONS FROM PROHIBITING FLORIDA-FRIENDLY LANDSCAPING, AND REQUIRES ORDINANCES TO ADDRESS TURF SELECTION AND MAXIMUM PERCENTAGES OF IRRIGATED TURF AND IMPERVIOUS SURFACE — BUT ITS DEFINITION IS BUILT AROUND PLANT SELECTION, EFFICIENT WATERING, FERTILISATION, MULCHING, WILDLIFE, PEST MANAGEMENT AND STORMWATER, AND NEVER NAMES SYNTHETIC TURF. So a covenant against artificial turf stands. Offer ARB submittal preparation as a service. Jacksonville tree protection is genuinely live in Mandarin given the heritage oaks — say on the page that you install around root zones without trenching through them.
facts.water_and_rules: Provider: JEA. Regulator: SJRWMD. Standard: two irrigation days/week under Daylight Saving Time, ONE day/week under Eastern Standard Time; odd or no address = Wednesday/Saturday, even = Thursday/Sunday, non-residential = Tuesday/Friday; not 10 a.m.–4 p.m. AS OF 2026-09-07 A PHASE III EXTREME WATER SHORTAGE ORDER IS ACTIVE across parts of Duval and ten other counties: ONE day per week (odd = Saturday, even = Sunday, non-residential = Tuesday), NO irrigation 8 a.m.–6 p.m., a hard three-quarters of an inch and one hour per zone, golf fairway irrigation also cut to one day a week, decorative fountains prohibited, non-essential commercial use suspended, tightened new-planting establishment rules. Exemptions: micro-irrigation and hand-held hose with shut-off nozzle anytime; new landscape 30 days unrestricted then every-other-day for 30 more. This hits Mandarin hardest of the five because Mandarin has the biggest lawns and the most irrigation zones — a 90x100 backyard on a one-day, 45-minute-per-zone allowance simply cannot be kept green. Quantify that on the page. NO artificial-turf rebate is documented in SJRWMD material; JEA's conservation and rebate pages are CAPTCHA-blocked and unverified — confirm with JEA before putting any rebate claim in writing.
facts.soil_and_yard: THE SOIL SERIES IS LITERALLY NAMED AFTER THIS NEIGHBORHOOD, and this is the best single fact on any of these five pages. The USDA MANDARIN SOIL SERIES was established in 1977 with its TYPE LOCATION IN DUVAL COUNTY (0.7 miles west of Girvin Road), formerly mapped as a thermic variant of the Cassia series. It is fine sand, sand, loamy sand or loamy fine sand throughout every horizon, formed in marine sediments, classified SOMEWHAT POORLY DRAINED, with internal free water occurring moderately deep and common, and a SEASONAL HIGH WATER TABLE AT 18 TO 42 INCHES BELOW THE SURFACE, present June through December or November through April. It occurs across northern peninsular Florida, Georgia and North Carolina. Translated for a homeowner: Mandarin sits on sand that will not hold water or nutrients in the dry months, then perches water within a foot and a half of the surface for half the year. That is why fertiliser leaches straight through, why the low corner is boggy from June onward, and why the same lawn is scorched by April. Layer on the neighborhood's other signature — ANCIENT LIVE OAKS DRAPED IN SPANISH MOSS along Mandarin Road and the river bank, the trees the place is known for — and you get deep shade plus root competition plus leaf drop on top of a bad soil profile. Flat topography (unlike contoured San Jose) means little natural fall, so drainage must be engineered rather than borrowed from grade. Installation implication: deep, properly graded aggregate base, perforated collection tied to daylight or a dry well, permeable backing, and a written explanation of how the system behaves when the water table rises in the wet season.
facts.housing_stock: An old riverside farming village that became a suburb: the British established plantations here in the 1760s (Francis Levett Sr.'s 10,000 acres), Spain redeveloped after 1783, Calvin Reed named it "Mandarin" in 1830 after the mandarin orange, and it shipped oranges, grapefruit and lemons by St. Johns River steamship until an 1890s freeze destroyed the groves. It merged into Jacksonville in the 1968 consolidation and then exploded after the 1970 BUCKMAN BRIDGE opened, becoming "one of Jacksonville's fastest growing neighborhoods." That history produces the most STRATIFIED housing stock in the batch; sell to three distinct layers. (1) HISTORIC MANDARIN ROAD / RIVERFRONT — a handful of pre-1900 and early-1900s cottages and large wooded riverfront parcels along the old village road and the river bank, acre-plus lots under enormous ancient oaks. (2) THE 1970s–1990s SUBURBAN WAVE off San Jose Boulevard and Loretto Road — ranch and two-storey traditional houses on quarter- to third-acre lots with backyards typically 60x70 to 90x100 ft (roughly 4,000–9,000 sq ft), many with pools and screen enclosures, mixed HOA. (3) 1990s–2000s HOA/CDD SUBDIVISIONS in the 32257/32258 spillover toward Greenland and Bartram — smaller lots, tighter covenants, active architectural review. Boundaries: Beauclerc north, Julington Creek south, the St. Johns River west (across from Orange Park). The historic core itself is small — about 9,000 residents and 3,800 households as of 2020 — while the 32223/32257/32258 catchment is far larger. CHECK DATE 2026-09-07.
facts.who_lives_there: ZIP 32223, the Mandarin core (ACS 2024 5-yr): 26,160 people over 11.5 sq mi, MEDIAN HOUSEHOLD INCOME $95,347 and per-capita $50,329 — both about 20% above region and nation, the highest in this batch. MEDIAN HOME VALUE $409,900, about 20% above the Jacksonville metro's $343,400. MEDIAN AGE 47.1, roughly 20% older than the metro's 39.3. 45% hold a bachelor's or higher. Poverty just 6.3%, about half Florida's 12.6%. VETERANS 12% of the population (2,491), nearly double the national 6.2%. And the number that should shape the whole page: ONLY 9.1% MOVED IN THE PAST YEAR, far below national rates — Mandarin residents STAY. Contrast the 32258 spillover: 40,408 people, median household income $102,204, median age 36.2, median home value $370,700, 47% bachelor's-plus, 7.9% poverty, 11.6% veterans. So the page addresses two buyers: an established, affluent, older, deeply rooted 32223 homeowner improving a house they intend to die in — the best long-warranty, premium-product, referral-generating customer in the batch — and a younger, even higher-earning 32258 family in newer HOA product. High age plus high income plus low mobility is exactly who buys a 15-year product instead of the cheapest bid.
facts.golf: BE HONEST: MANDARIN HAS NO COUNTRY CLUB OF ITS OWN, and that absence is commercially useful rather than a weakness. Mandarin residents drive to play. Nearest club identities: San Jose Country Club (the Donald Ross course, north up San Jose Boulevard past Beauclerc), Epping Forest Yacht & Country Club (the duPont estate, also north on San Jose Blvd), Deerwood Country Club and Jacksonville Golf & Country Club east, Bent Creek Golf Course, Timuquana Country Club across the river in Ortega, and the St. Johns County clubs south past Julington Creek — Julington Creek Plantation, Cimarrone, St Johns Golf & Country Club — with PGA TOUR headquarters and TPC Sawgrass at Ponte Vedra Beach about 40 minutes east. So the Mandarin golf pitch is precisely NOT "practice for the course down the road" (that is San Jose's). It is: "you have the biggest, flattest, most private backyards in the batch on a 47-year-old, $95k-income, stay-put block — build the green at home because the club is a drive away." These are the 800–1,500 sq ft multi-hole green jobs with fringe, bunker and chipping approach on 1970s–90s quarter- and third-acre lots. Highest average job value in the batch after San Jose's estate work.
facts.commercial_targets: MANDARIN HIGH SCHOOL, 4831 Greenland Road, 32258 — opened 1990, approximately 2,398 students (2023-24), with a football stadium and an outdoor pool that Jacksonville Parks & Recreation runs as a community pool in summer. The largest single institutional prospect in the batch by enrolment; verify field surface before pitching, and pitch practice fields and sideline/end-zone areas even if the stadium field is already synthetic. Mandarin Middle School. Mandarin Oaks Elementary, Crown Point Elementary, Loretto Elementary, Greenland Pines Elementary, Bartram Springs Elementary and Twin Lakes Academy Middle across the 32223/32257/32258 catchment — a dense set of playground and courtyard opportunities. Losco Regional Park sports fields. Walter Jones Historical Park (heritage-appropriate ground surfacing around historic structures). The 32223/32258 HOA and CDD common areas, entry monuments, amenity centers and dog parks — the newer Bartram and Greenland communities are the CDD work. Veterinary hospitals, groomers, boarding kennels and doggy daycares along San Jose Boulevard, the corridor for all of them. Churches with children's ministries. Assisted living and senior communities — relevant given the 47.1 median age and 12% veteran share: low-maintenance, wheelchair-firm, non-slip courtyard surfaces are a real and underserved niche.
facts.landmarks: HARRIET BEECHER STOWE — she bought a Mandarin cottage in 1867 and wintered here for seventeen years, publishing Palmetto Leaves in 1872, "the first unsolicited promotional writing to interest northern tourists in Florida"; a chapel here honours her. The Mandarin Museum & Historical Society (founded 1989), preserving the historic post office, general store and the 1898 ST. JOSEPH'S MISSION SCHOOLHOUSE (a Black-heritage site opened to the public in 2016). WALTER JONES HISTORICAL PARK (opened 2000). Losco Regional Park. Julington-Durbin Creek Preserve. Mandarin South Library Park. Historic cemeteries with graves dating to the 1800s. Julington Creek, the southern boundary. The Buckman Bridge (1970), the infrastructure that created modern Mandarin. Mandarin Road with its moss-draped oak tunnel. Marinas and river views on the St. Johns, across from Orange Park. Notable residents: U.S. Congresswoman Val Demings and Lynyrd Skynyrd guitarist Allen Collins.

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH THE PARADOX: the town is named for golf, and the golf shrine left. The Hall of Fame closed its World Golf Village campus in 2023 and went back to Pinehurst, the IMAX closed in 2024, Caddyshack closed in June 2026, and the county is still shopping the empty site. What did NOT leave is the golf — King & Bear, the only Nicklaus-Palmer co-design, freshly restored for $2.5 million, and Slammer & Squire, both still here, both 4.5 stars. So the honest, unrepeatable line for this page is: the museum moved out, the game stayed, and the way people play it here has moved into the backyard. This is THE putting green town in northeast Florida, and it should read that way from the first sentence — not as generic suburban landscape turf with a golf photo. Nothing next door can claim it: World Golf Village is the only community in the service area literally built by the PGA TOUR, on 6,300 acres, with two championship courses at its centre and a population that more than doubled from 12,310 to over 26,000 in a decade at $117,212 median household income. Second differentiator, and it is a commercial one: WGV has more institutional turf buyers per square mile than anywhere else in the batch — Tocoi Creek High with 2,375 students and 16 sports on a 68.79-acre campus, Mill Creek Academy, Pacetti Bay Middle, the Turnbull Creek CDD amenity centre at 101 Positano, two golf operations and a convention resort — so the page should carry a real commercial section, not a token one, and should quote the nonresidential Tuesday-only irrigation rule at those buyers directly. Third, the drought close: WGV is on St. Johns County potable water and is NOT on the reclaimed system (only Twin Creeks and SilverLeaf are), so under the Phase III order in force since 11 May 2026 these homeowners get one watering day a week and cannot legally lay new sod at all. Distinguish it in one line from its neighbours: Mill Creek is the ballfields and the new-build frontier, Julington Creek is the shaded 25-year-old lawn, World Golf Village is the putting green.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: Unincorporated St. Johns County — no municipal ordinance layer. The county Land Development Code has NO artificial or synthetic turf provision: verified by full-text search of Article V (11 Aug 2025) and Article VI (12 Jan 2026). Residential constraints are the Table 6.01 numbers: 70% impervious surface ratio in every residential district, 10 ft minimum rear yard in RS-1/RS-2/RS-3. THE COMMERCIAL TRAP, and it matters more in WGV than anywhere else because of the volume of CDD and HOA common area: LDC Sec. 6.06.02.A.5 allows non-living ground cover such as rock, gravel and mulch in combination with living plant material but states 'The use of artificial plants shall not be permitted to meet any of the landscaping requirements' — and Sec. 6.06.02.A.6 requires all plantings to follow Florida-Friendly principles, exempting only golf courses, sports fields, agriculture and silviculture. Those rules attach to development needing a Development Permit (Sec. 6.06.01), so an amenity-centre or clubhouse landscape plan cannot count synthetic turf toward required landscaping — a homeowner's backyard is untouched. Governance layer: multiple CDDs and HOAs. Turnbull Creek CDD (established 2004, managed by Rizzetta & Company, HOA management by Freedom Community Management) governs Murabella, amenity centre at 101 Positano Avenue, St. Augustine 32092. Assume an ARB submittal on every residential install. FS 373.185 blocks deed restrictions from prohibiting Florida-Friendly Landscaping but its definition does not name synthetic turf, so it is not a reliable HOA override. Fertilizer: 5 lbs N per 1,000 sf per year max, none under storm watch/warning.
facts.water_and_rules: Provider: St. Johns County Utility Department (904-209-2700, utilbill@sjcfl.us), not JEA — JEA's St. Johns service is the northwest corner and the Ponte Vedra/A1A coastal grids, not the SR 16 / International Golf Parkway corridor. Status at 2026-09-07: SJRWMD PHASE III EXTREME WATER SHORTAGE, declared 11 May 2026 and still in force. Irrigation is ONE DAY PER WEEK — odd-numbered or no address Saturday, even-numbered Sunday, NONRESIDENTIAL TUESDAY — with no irrigation 8 a.m. to 6 p.m., 3/4 inch per zone maximum and one hour per zone. NEW SOD INSTALLATION AND NEW PLANTINGS ARE PROHIBITED, as are aesthetic water uses, street washing and pressure washing. That nonresidential Tuesday line matters here because WGV is thick with CDD and HOA amenity common areas. Standard schedule when the order lifts: DST odd Wed+Sat / even Thu+Sun / nonres Tue+Fri; EST odd Sat / even Sun / nonres Tue; never 10 a.m.-4 p.m.; micro-irrigation and hand-held hose with shutoff nozzle exempt from timing. New landscaping may be watered daily for 30 days after installation, then alternate days for a further 30. Reclaimed water is exempt from the one-day rule, but St. Johns County reclaimed service currently covers only TWIN CREEKS and SILVERLEAF — World Golf Village is NOT on reclaimed, so its residents are on the one-day potable schedule. No artificial turf rebate found anywhere in St. Johns County. Enforcement: SJC Code Enforcement 904-209-0734 or the SJC Connect app.
facts.soil_and_yard: Flatwoods sand — the Myakka-type spodosol profile: dark gray sand at the surface, gray sand to about 26 inches, an organic-stained spodic hardpan to roughly 60 inches, grayish brown sand below. Rapid infiltration through the top, only moderate through the subsoil, with the natural water table within 10 inches of the surface for one to five months a year and past 40 inches in dry spells. WGV sits inland at low relief with heavy stormwater pond and wetland infrastructure threaded through the plats, so a large share of lots back onto a retention pond, a wet preserve or a golf course drainage swale — the classic result is a soggy rear corner that stays wet after storms and bakes bare in drought. Two distinct shade regimes: the older resort-core and King & Bear lots sit under retained mature live oak and pine (the Palencia course nearby is explicitly described as oak-shaded), while Murabella and the newer production sections are open, sun-blasted and irrigation-dependent. Both fail St. Augustine, for opposite reasons. Golf-frontage lots add a third problem: overspray, cart traffic at the property line and the homeowner's own short-game wear pattern.
facts.housing_stock: A 6,300-acre resort community created by the PGA TOUR and established in 1998, now a census-designated place covering roughly 26.86 sq mi between Jacksonville and St. Augustine, off I-95 and International Golf Parkway in ZIP 32092. This is the widest ERA SPREAD of any place in the batch: original 1998-2005 resort-era product around the courses and the village core, a large 2004-2015 middle layer (Murabella, Heritage Landing, Samara Lakes, Las Calinas, Glen St. Johns, South Hampton, Cascades 55+), and active new construction still going. Population went from 12,310 in 2010 to 22,117 in 2020 to 26,077 (2020-2024 ACS 5-year) and a reported 30,556 as of 1 July 2025 — it more than doubled in a decade. 10,222 housing units, 81.3% owner-occupied, 9.0% vacancy, 2.79 persons per household, 85.5% family households, median property value $477,000. Lot pattern is genuinely mixed and the page should acknowledge it: golf-frontage and estate lots in King & Bear, standard 50-75 ft production lots in Murabella and Samara Lakes, villa and townhome product, and 55+ patio homes in Cascades. Baseline county dimensional standards (LDC Art. VI Table 6.01, 12 Jan 2026) run RS-3 7,500 sf / RS-2 10,000 sf / RS-1 13,200 sf with 10 ft rear yards and a 70% impervious cap, but nearly all of WGV is PUD/CDD-governed with its own plat standards. Practical backyard range: roughly 1,200 sf on a production lot to several thousand on golf frontage. HOA and CDD coverage is close to universal.
facts.who_lives_there: Median household income $117,212 (2020-2024 ACS 5-year, +6.82% YoY), per capita income $51,060, poverty 5.35%, homeownership 89.4%. Median age 42.9 (42.3 male, 44.1 female) — older than Nocatee, younger than Vilano Beach. 31% of households report income above $150,000; only 3% below $25,000. Race/ethnicity roughly 74.5% White, 9.0% Black, 8.3% Hispanic (a separate source reports 88.8% White / 11.9% Hispanic — figures vary by vintage, so cite one and move on). Top employment sectors: health care and social assistance (2,247), professional/scientific/technical services (1,649), retail trade (1,343). Average commute 33.7 minutes, 65.2% drive alone, 2 cars per household — this is a commuter community split between Jacksonville jobs and St. Augustine. ZIP 32092 median household income is $126,947 (Dec 2025), fifth-highest in the county. WGV ranks #105 of 956 Florida places for median household income, 89th percentile statewide.
facts.golf: The densest and most on-brand golf story in the batch. TWO championship courses, both at the community's core: KING & BEAR, 1 King and Bear Dr, St. Augustine 32092 — the only Jack Nicklaus / Arnold Palmer co-design, with Bobby Weed, par 72 at 7,279 yards, fully restored in a five-month, $2.5 million project. SLAMMER & SQUIRE, 2 World Golf Pl, 32092 — Bobby Weed with Sam Snead ('the Slammer') and Gene Sarazen ('the Squire'), par 72 at 6,939 yards, recently renovated. Both hold 4.5-star Golf Digest ratings. Adjacent and same customer base: The Golf Club at South Hampton, 315 South Hampton Club Way, 32092; St. Johns Golf & Country Club, 205 St Johns Golf Dr, 32092 (18 holes, six tee sets, 5,286-7,236 yards, under 20 minutes away); The Palencia Club, 600 Palencia Club Dr, 32095 — a 7,071-yard Arthur Hills design under live oaks running to the Intracoastal. THE CRITICAL FACT: the World Golf Hall of Fame, which opened here in May 1998, CLOSED its WGV campus in 2023 and relocated back to Pinehurst, North Carolina. The IMAX Theater closed in 2024, and Murray Brothers Caddyshack closed 27 June 2026. As of September 2025 St. Johns County was evaluating redevelopment proposals for the vacant Hall of Fame site.
facts.commercial_targets: TOCOI CREEK HIGH SCHOOL, 11200 St. Johns Pkwy — opened for 2021-22, roughly 2,375 students, 68.79-acre campus, 16 sports, Toros, burnt orange and gunmetal gray; zoned for World Golf Village and SilverLeaf. MILL CREEK ACADEMY, 3750 International Golf Parkway (K-8, 904-547-3720). PACETTI BAY MIDDLE SCHOOL. Magnolia Oaks Academy, coming online as a Tocoi Creek feeder by 2028-29. TURNBULL CREEK CDD / MURABELLA amenity centre, 101 Positano Ave — pool, fitness, tennis courts and athletic fields, with a district manager (Rizzetta & Company) and an HOA manager (Freedom Community Management) as two separate procurement doors. Golf operations: King & Bear and Slammer & Squire for practice greens, tee lines, range mats and clubhouse surrounds; South Hampton, St. Johns Golf & CC and Palencia within reach. The Renaissance Resort and the St. Johns County Convention Center for event lawns and rooftop/terrace installs. The vacant Hall of Fame redevelopment site as a watch item for a future amenity bid. Daycares, vets and pet businesses along International Golf Parkway and SR 16.
facts.landmarks: King & Bear (1 King and Bear Dr) and Slammer & Squire (2 World Golf Pl). The VACANT World Golf Hall of Fame site — closed 2023, collection moved to Pinehurst; the county has been evaluating redevelopment proposals since September 2025. The former IMAX Theater (closed 2024). The former Murray Brothers Caddyshack (closed 27 June 2026). The Renaissance Resort at World Golf Village. International Golf Parkway and the I-95 Exit 323 interchange. Tocoi Creek High School, 11200 St. Johns Parkway — 68.79 acres, built on land formerly owned by the Pacetti family. Mill Creek Academy, 3750 International Golf Parkway. The Murabella amenity centre at 101 Positano Ave. St. Johns County Convention Center at the Renaissance.

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH SPORTS SURFACES AND NEW CONSTRUCTION — this is the ballfield-and-batting-cage page, and it is the one town in the batch where the commercial job should come BEFORE the backyard. St. Johns County put $12 million into Mill Creek Park at 4881 SR 16 and opened it on 1 March 2025 with two baseball fields, two softball fields, four batting cages and a multipurpose field, its second major athletic park in ten years, built with the Villages Baseball Association. Tocoi Creek High sits up the road with 2,375 students and 16 sports on 68.79 acres, fed by Mill Creek Academy and Pacetti Bay Middle. Youth sports gravity in western St. Johns County now sits here, and the county's own Land Development Code exempts sports fields from its Florida-Friendly planting rules — so the page can talk cages, bullpens, hitting tunnels and dugout aprons with real authority. The residential half is the other genuine difference: Mill Creek is the county's new-construction FRONTIER, where Pacetti-family farm and timber ground is turning into SilverLeaf, Grand Oaks, TrailMark and Mill Creek Forest. That means builder-graded, machine-compacted fill that looks like perfect sand and drains like a pan — a base-prep story, not a shade story — plus brand-new HOAs whose ARBs are still writing their turf standards. Two more things nobody nearby can say: SilverLeaf is one of only TWO communities in all of St. Johns County with reclaimed water, so its residents dodge the one-day-a-week potable rule and must be sold on wear, heat, mud and pets rather than drought, while everyone else on the corridor is capped at one watering day and legally barred from installing new sod under the 11 May 2026 Phase III order. And the town has a genuinely old, checkable identity — a school with an unbroken line back to an 1879 log building, one teacher who served 46 years, no electricity until 1948, an 18th-century mill dam still on the archaeological register — which lets the page sound local rather than templated. Be honest in the copy that Mill Creek is a corridor and a name rather than a bounded town, and cross-link it to World Golf Village instead of competing with it.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: Unincorporated St. Johns County — no municipal layer. No artificial or synthetic turf provision anywhere in the county Land Development Code (verified by full-text search of Article V, 11 Aug 2025, and Article VI, 12 Jan 2026). Residential limits are Table 6.01: 70% impervious surface ratio in every residential district, Open Rural at 1 acre minimum with 25/10/10 ft yards and 35% lot coverage, RS-E at 1 acre with 30/20/20 ft yards, RS-3 at 7,500 sf with a 10 ft rear yard. LDC Sec. 6.06.02.A.5 bars artificial plants from meeting any required landscaping, and Sec. 6.06.02.A.6 requires Florida-Friendly planting principles while EXPRESSLY EXEMPTING GOLF COURSES, SPORTS FIELDS, AGRICULTURE AND SILVICULTURE — a genuinely useful exemption to know when quoting an athletic-field job on this corridor. Those rules apply to development requiring a Development Permit, not to a homeowner's backyard. The governance split is the thing to get right: new SilverLeaf, Grand Oaks, TrailMark and Mill Creek Forest addresses sit inside young HOAs and CDDs with active, strict architectural review boards, while the surviving rural acreage typically has no HOA at all. Qualify every lead on that one question. FS 373.185 protects Florida-Friendly Landscaping from deed restrictions but its definition does not name synthetic turf. Fertilizer: 5 lbs N per 1,000 sf per year, none under storm watch/warning.
facts.water_and_rules: Provider: St. Johns County Utility Department (904-209-2700) on the served side, private wells on the rural acreage. Status at 2026-09-07: SJRWMD Phase III Extreme Water Shortage, declared 11 May 2026, still in effect — irrigation ONE day a week (odd or no address Saturday, even Sunday, nonresidential Tuesday), none between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m., 3/4 inch and one hour per zone maximum, and NEW SOD INSTALLATION AND NEW PLANTINGS PROHIBITED. The order explicitly covers private wells and pumps as well as utilities. Standard schedule on lift: DST odd Wed+Sat / even Thu+Sun / nonres Tue+Fri; EST odd Sat / even Sun / nonres Tue; never 10 a.m.-4 p.m. THE ONE PIECE OF LOCAL LEVERAGE UNIQUE TO THIS CORRIDOR: reclaimed water is exempt from the one-day rule, and SILVERLEAF is one of only TWO communities in all of St. Johns County with county reclaimed irrigation (the other is Twin Creeks). Reclaimed runs in purple pipe (Pantone Purple 522C, labelled Do Not Drink) and may irrigate lawns, gardens, trees and shrubs but may NOT wash vehicles, structures or driveways, fill pools or hot tubs, or connect to potable or A/C lines. So a SilverLeaf homeowner has a watering advantage his neighbour on the next road does not — sell turf there on heat, wear, pet damage and mud, not on the drought. Everyone else on the corridor is on the one-day potable schedule. No turf rebate found in St. Johns County. Code Enforcement 904-209-0734 / SJC Connect app.
facts.soil_and_yard: Flatwoods sand over the Myakka-type spodosol profile — dark gray surface sand, gray to roughly 26 inches, an organic-stained hardpan to about 60 inches, water table within 10 inches of the surface for one to five months a year and past 40 inches in drought. Two Mill-Creek-specific complications. First, this corridor is actively being converted from timber and farmland, so builder lots are heavily fill-graded and machine-compacted: the sand looks like a perfect base and is not — it is a compacted pan over a natural pan, and it holds water at the surface after a storm. Base prep and a deliberate drainage plane earn their money here more than in any established neighbourhood. Second, the creek itself: Mill Creek is a real watercourse, and archaeological site 8SJ2458, the Historic Mill Site west of SR 13, survives as an earthen dam thought to date to the late 18th or early 19th century — evidence that this corridor's low ground has been wet and impounded for two centuries. Rural parcels carry the opposite problem: retained live oak and pine canopy, root mats and leaf litter over never-cleared ground, so scope grubbing and root work, not sod stripping.
facts.housing_stock: HONEST CAVEAT UP FRONT: results for Mill Creek are genuinely thin and the page should be scoped accordingly. Mill Creek is a historic place name for the rural corridor of western St. Johns County around SR 16, CR 13A / Pacetti Road and International Golf Parkway, west of St. Augustine. It is NOT a census-designated place, has no Wikipedia article, no population count, no median income and no housing table of its own — it does not even appear in Wikipedia's list of 14 unincorporated communities in St. Johns County. Its identity is carried by two institutions and a road: Mill Creek Academy, Mill Creek Park, and SR 16. Mill Creek also OVERLAPS World Golf Village heavily — Mill Creek Academy sits at 3750 International Golf Parkway inside the WGV area — so treat the two pages as neighbours that must not duplicate each other. Housing here is a seam, not a single stock: old Pacetti-family farm and timber parcels and scattered rural homesteads on acreage (county Open Rural zoning, 1-acre minimum, 100 ft width, 35% lot coverage, 70% impervious cap; RS-E at 1 acre / 150 ft width where platted) sitting directly against the county's most aggressive new-construction frontier — SilverLeaf, Grand Oaks, TrailMark, Mill Creek Forest by Toll Brothers, Mill Creek Landing, Arbor Mill. So a Mill Creek lead is either a builder-fresh 2020s production backyard with bare compacted sand and a brand-new HOA, or an acre-plus rural parcel with no HOA at all. Almost nothing in between, and almost nothing historic in the built fabric.
facts.who_lives_there: No place-level data exists — say so rather than padding. The defensible frame is the surrounding ZIP 32092, whose median household income is $126,947 as of December 2025, fifth-highest in St. Johns County behind Fruit Cove 32259 ($149,213), Nocatee 32081 ($132,087), 32095 ($128,915) and Ponte Vedra Beach 32082 ($127,105). Countywide median is $108,800, up 55% since 2015 and nearly triple 2005. World Golf Village CDP, which encompasses much of this corridor, reports $117,212 median household income, 89.4% homeownership, $477,000 median property value and median age 42.9. Character: young to middle-aged families buying new construction for the schools, plus a thinning population of long-tenured rural landowners — the Pacetti family name runs through the whole area, from Pacetti Road to the land Tocoi Creek High was built on to Mrs. Pacetti, who taught at the Mill Creek school from 1926 to 1975.
facts.golf: Nothing named 'Mill Creek' in golf — do not invent one. The relevant courses are all a short drive on International Golf Parkway or SR 16: King & Bear, 1 King and Bear Dr, St. Augustine 32092 (Nicklaus/Palmer/Weed, par 72, 7,279 yards, restored for $2.5m) and Slammer & Squire, 2 World Golf Pl, 32092 (Weed with Snead and Sarazen, par 72, 6,939 yards) at World Golf Village; The Golf Club at South Hampton, 315 South Hampton Club Way, 32092; St. Johns Golf & Country Club, 205 St Johns Golf Dr, 32092. The Palencia Club, 600 Palencia Club Dr, 32095, is further east. For a Mill Creek page the golf story is proximity, not identity — the stronger sports story here is baseball and softball, not golf, which is exactly what makes this page different from World Golf Village's.
facts.commercial_targets: MILL CREEK PARK, 4881 SR 16 — the single best commercial target in the batch and the reason this page exists: two baseball fields, two softball fields, FOUR BATTING CAGES, a multipurpose field, concession stand and restrooms, $12m, opened 1 March 2025, run with the Villages Baseball Association. Batting cage floors, bullpen mounds, cage tunnels, dugout aprons and worn infield transitions are exactly the recurring, referable work an installer wants, and the county's own LDC exempts sports fields from Florida-Friendly planting requirements. MILL CREEK ACADEMY, 3750 International Golf Pkwy (K-8) — play areas, courtyards and PE surfaces. TOCOI CREEK HIGH SCHOOL, 11200 St. Johns Pkwy — 2,375 students, 16 sports, 68.79 acres, fed by Pacetti Bay Middle and Mill Creek Academy. PACETTI BAY MIDDLE SCHOOL. Magnolia Oaks Academy, opening as a Tocoi Creek feeder by 2028-29. The SilverLeaf, Grand Oaks and TrailMark amenity centres — young CDD/HOA common areas with dog parks, playgrounds and pool decks, all still specifying. The Villages Baseball Association itself as a relationship, not just a venue.
facts.landmarks: MILL CREEK PARK, 4881 SR 16, St. Augustine — a $12 million county athletic park that opened 1 March 2025, the county's second major athletic park in a decade, developed in partnership with the Villages Baseball Association. MILL CREEK ACADEMY, 3750 International Golf Parkway (904-547-3720) — a K-8 whose lineage runs back to an 1879 log schoolhouse with a fireplace; rebuilt in 1893 after a fire, again as a one-room school with a wood stove in 1914, as a six-classroom building with an auditorium in 1928, and in its current form from 1991-92 with additions in 2000 and 2011-12. The area did not get electricity until 1948. Mrs. Pacetti taught here from 1926 to 1975. Pacetti Road (CR 13A). The SR 16 / CR 13A / International Golf Parkway junction. The historic Mill Creek dam site, 8SJ2458, west of SR 13. Tocoi Creek High School on former Pacetti family land. The CR 2209 corridor and its $32.5 million widening project.

name: Asbury Lake / Lake Asbury

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH ACREAGE, WELLS, SLOPE AND A BRAND-NEW EXPRESSWAY. The opening line writes itself and no competitor is saying it: you own two acres, you irrigate from your own well, and as of the Phase III order the water district has cut you to ONE DAY A WEEK — your well included. Then two facts that make Timeless sound like the only outfit in the county that has read the code. FIRST: Lake Asbury sits inside the county's own GREATER LAKE ASBURY DISTRICT (Clay County Code Sec. 18.5-52(24)), where the landscaping article reaches RESIDENTIAL buildings, synthetic turf cannot count toward plant requirements, and — critically on wooded acreage — Secs. 18.5-27 to 18.5-32 require an approved TREE PRESERVATION PLAN before anyone disturbs a protected tree's roots or even prunes it. A crew that trenches a base edge near a protected oak without that plan is creating a code violation for the homeowner. SECOND: Lake Asbury is the ONLY place in this batch with genuine slope — USDA maps Blanton, Penney, Ortega and Ridgewood fine sands at 5 to 8 percent above Black Creek — so erosion control, base stability and edge anchoring are real engineering here, not boilerplate, and the county's own code names erosion as the failure mode. Then sell what the demographics actually support: median household income $100,949, per capita $62,221, poverty 2.2%, two gross acres per household, and NO GOLF COURSE INSIDE THE COMMUNITY. That is the batch's best market for PRIVATE BACKYARD PUTTING GREENS with real square footage, full-yard conversions, pool surrounds, and shaded areas under mature oaks where acreage owners have given up on grass. Big jobs, high ticket, $10-12/sq ft defensible. Finally, TIME THE CAMPAIGN: the First Coast Expressway's final phase-two segment opened 29 June 2026 and the population is up 34.3% since 2020 — a wave of new high-income arrivals with raw yards is landing right now. WHY DIFFERENT FROM NEXT DOOR: Oakleaf, six miles north, is 600 square feet of fenced HOA yard on flat C/D flatwoods; Bellair is a mall parking lot; Lakeside is old shaded subdivision; Doctors Inlet is a rural corridor with no census identity and no overlay. Lake Asbury is the one with two acres, a private well, actual topography, six-figure income — and a county overlay district named after it.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: THE SECOND OVERLAY DISTRICT, AND IT IS NAMED AFTER THIS PLACE. Clay County Code Sec. 18.5-52(24) defines the GREATER LAKE ASBURY DISTRICT by metes and bounds: beginning at the northerly right-of-way of STATE ROAD 16 and the easterly line of SOUTH FORK BLACK CREEK, north along South Fork Black Creek to BLACK CREEK, east along Black Creek to PETERS CREEK, southwest along Peters Creek back to SR 16, then west along SR 16 to the point of beginning, excluding the Town of Penney Farms limits. INSIDE THAT DISTRICT, Sec. 18.5-51 extends the county landscaping article to ALL RESIDENTIAL BUILDINGS, not just nonresidential ones — and Sec. 18.5-53(4)(h) states: 'Synthetic lawns: Synthetic or artificial turf shall not be used in lieu of plant requirements in this section' (with (i) doing the same for synthetic trees, shrubs, ground covers and vines). Sec. 18-5.54 also requires a wider 10-foot landscaped yard along rights-of-way inside the district. AND — the constraint that really bites on wooded acreage — Secs. 18.5-27 through 18.5-32 make it unlawful inside the Greater Lake Asbury District to cut, remove, damage, destroy, ROOT-DISTURB, TRIM or PRUNE a protected tree without an APPROVED TREE PRESERVATION PLAN, with work required to follow National Arborist Association pruning standards and ANSI Z133.1. On a two-acre lot full of mature oaks, a turf crew trenching a base edge is exactly the activity that rule contemplates. These overlays came in via Ords. 99-13, 99-23, 99-38 and 99-39 (1999); the Code is codified through Ord. 2026-12 of 14 April 2026 (Supp. 86). HOA prevalence is LOW on the older acreage and HIGH in the newer subdivisions — a genuinely split market. Fla. Stat. 373.185 and 720.3075(4) bar HOAs from prohibiting Florida-Friendly Landscaping or imposing rules that conflict with a water shortage order, but artificial turf is not among the UF/IFAS Florida-Friendly nine principles and gets no statutory protection; do not overclaim.
facts.water_and_rules: Clay County Utility Authority where mains reach, but PRIVATE WELLS on much of the acreage — and that is the hook.
