SJRWMD Phase III Extreme Water Shortage Order 2026-017 was in force at the 2026-09-07 check and it applies to ALL WATER SOURCES INCLUDING PRIVATE WELLS AND PUMP SYSTEMS: irrigation ONE DAY PER WEEK — odd or no address Saturday, even Sunday, nonresidential Tuesday; never between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m.; maximum three-quarters inch and one hour per zone. Most well owners on two acres have never been told this applies to them. The normal schedule is codified at Clay County Code Sec. 18.5-73; Sec. 18.5-79 sets penalties — category 2 civil infraction for a first violation, category 10 for second and subsequent, up to $500 if contested and lost, EACH DAY A SEPARATE OFFENSE, and no more than one written warning. CCUA offers no landscape or irrigation rebate; it promotes reclaimed water and Florida-Friendly Landscaping and does not mention artificial turf. Turf qualifies for nothing — be honest about it and make the argument on the acre of grass they can no longer keep alive on one day a week.
facts.soil_and_yard: THE MOST VARIED GROUND IN THE BATCH, AND THE ONLY ONE WITH REAL SLOPE. A USDA point query near the Sandridge Road area returns LEON FINE SAND, 0 to 2 percent slopes — poorly drained, minimum annual water table 31 cm, hydrologic group A/D (Leon is also the single most extensive map unit in all of Clay County at about 43,100 acres). At the Black Creek margin the survey returns RUTLEGE-OSIER COMPLEX, FREQUENTLY FLOODED — very poorly drained, water table 8 cm. But uniquely in this batch the CDP also carries 5-TO-8-PERCENT SLOPE MAP UNITS: Blanton fine sand 5-8%, Penney fine sand 5-8%, Ortega fine sand 5-8%, Ridgewood fine sand 5-8% — the sandhill and ravine country above Black Creek. Everywhere else in this batch is flat 0-2% or 0-5% flatwoods; Lake Asbury genuinely falls away toward the creek. THAT CHANGES THE JOB: erosion control under and around the base, base stability on grade, seam and perimeter anchoring, and edge detail where water sheets. The county's own code names the failure mode at Sec. 18.5-53(4)(g) — 'solid sod shall be used in swales or other areas subject to erosion.' Also present: Cassia, Meadowbrook, Goldhead, Surrency, Plummer, Pottsburg, Sapelo, Maurepas and Pamlico muck, and Leon fine sand FREQUENTLY FLOODED along the creek bottoms. Add mature live oak shade on the older acreage lots, which is where the grass has already failed.
facts.housing_stock: NAME FIRST: the Census calls it ASBURY LAKE CDP; everyone local — the schools, the county code, the road signs — says LAKE ASBURY (Lake Asbury Elementary, Lake Asbury Junior High, the county's 'Greater Lake Asbury District'). Build the page to rank for both, with 'Lake Asbury' as the primary. Geography: 16.96 sq mi of land, 0.27 sq mi water (Census TIGERweb, GEOID 1202187, centroid 30.0472073,-81.7852946), 13 miles southwest of Orange Park, bordered on the north by Black Creek, a tributary of the St. Johns. THE LOWEST DENSITY IN THIS BATCH BY FAR at 859 people per square mile — versus 3,416 in Bellair-Meadowbrook Terrace — which works out to roughly two gross acres per household. This is acreage country: large lots, many on private well and septic, mature oaks, horse property and hunting land, now being infilled by newer subdivisions (Asbury Plantation, Shannon Lake, Lago Del Sur, Hunter's Trace, Sheraton Lakes). AND IT IS THE FASTEST-GROWING PLACE IN THE BATCH: 8,700 (2010) → 10,842/11,036 (2020) → about 14,565 (2026), up 34.3% since the 2020 census and running 2.58% a year. Around 80% of households are married couples. HONEST GAP: no verified CDP-level median home value or median year built — the older Wikipedia figures are 2010-vintage and its housing-unit density number appears garbled; do not republish it. Back yards here are the biggest in this batch by a wide margin, which changes the whole economics of a quote.
facts.who_lives_there: 2026 estimates: median household income $100,949; married-family median $116,795; PER CAPITA INCOME $62,221 — the highest per-capita of the five; POVERTY 2.2% — by far the lowest in the batch and less than a seventh of Bellair-Meadowbrook Terrace's 15.48%; median age 40.6 (36.4 male, 44.1 female); 108.4 males per 100 females. Racially the least diverse of the five (about 88.8% White at the 2010 count). This is quiet, established, land-owning money — older and more settled than Oakleaf, less flashy than Fleming Island, and with substantially more yard than either.
facts.golf: No golf course inside the CDP, and that is the point rather than a gap. MAGNOLIA POINT GOLF & COUNTRY CLUB, 3670 Clubhouse Drive, Green Cove Springs — an 18-hole club set in a 1,000-acre community off US 17; TIGERweb places it inside Green Cove Springs city limits, roughly 5-6 miles southeast, so municipal rather than county code governs work there. To the west, the Ravines-area courses around Middleburg sit in the same Black Creek ravine country. To the northeast, Eagle Harbor Golf Club (Clyde B. Johnston, Fleming Island) and Eagle Landing at Oakleaf Plantation (also Clyde Johnston). PRACTICAL READ: Lake Asbury households have the acreage AND the income for PRIVATE BACKYARD PUTTING GREENS but no course inside the community — which makes this the single best short-game-green market in the batch. Sell the green they build at home, not the green they live on.
facts.commercial_targets: Confirmed inside Asbury Lake CDP by TIGERweb point-in-polygon: RONNIE VAN ZANT MEMORIAL PARK (90-acre county park — tennis court surrounds, dugouts, picnic and event lawn, disc golf tee pads); LAKE ASBURY ELEMENTARY SCHOOL and LAKE ASBURY JUNIOR HIGH SCHOOL (adjacent campuses at roughly 30.044,-81.805); SHADOWLAWN ELEMENTARY. Just outside in unincorporated Clay: RIDEOUT ELEMENTARY. To the southeast in Green Cove Springs: CLAY HIGH SCHOOL, CHARLES E. BENNETT ELEMENTARY, SPRING PARK ELEMENTARY and MAGNOLIA POINT GOLF & COUNTRY CLUB (practice areas, clubhouse grounds). Also the CLAY COUNTY FLYERS RC CLUB field. HONEST NOTE: this CDP is thin on named pet businesses and daycares — the vet, grooming and childcare cluster sits north in Lakeside and Oakleaf. That is itself an opening: 14,565 people and growing 2.58% a year with no local pet-services cluster means the residential pet-turf demand is being served by nobody nearby.
facts.landmarks: RONNIE VAN ZANT MEMORIAL PARK — 90 acres in Lake Asbury (30.051°N, 81.795°W), built to honour the Lynyrd Skynyrd frontman killed in the 1977 plane crash and funded by fans and family of the band; tennis courts, fishing ponds, a disc golf course and picnic areas. There is no better local landmark in this batch and no competitor page will use it. BLACK CREEK and SOUTH FORK BLACK CREEK, the district's own boundaries. THE FIRST COAST EXPRESSWAY (SR 23) — phase two opened from SR 21 to US 17 on 9 AUGUST 2025 and the final phase-two segment to SR 16 opened 29 JUNE 2026, ten weeks before this check date; the extension to I-95 with a replacement Shands Bridge began construction in 2024 and is targeted for 2032. Sandridge Road. Lake Asbury Elementary and Lake Asbury Junior High. Penney Farms just south. Clay County Flyers RC Club flying field.

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH: 'Your backyard is 25 feet deep. We make all 25 feet usable, year-round, with two kids and a dog on it.' Nocatee's defining physical fact is the 40- and 50-foot lot — builders literally market by frontage — which leaves a rear yard roughly the depth of a two-car garage, and grass simply cannot recover from that much foot and paw traffic in that little space. This is the highest-VOLUME, most repeatable market in the four counties, and the page should be unapologetically about small-yard transformation, pet turf and compact 2–3 hole putting greens rather than sweeping estate lawns. Three town-specific proof points that no neighbouring page can use: (1) THE JEA RECLAIMED-WATER STORY. Nocatee is on JEA reclaimed irrigation and JEA had to divide the community into FOUR ZONES from 7 April 2025, assign days by zone instead of by address, and shut reclaimed water off two days a week to hold pressure. That is a documented, local, checkable fact that says your irrigation supply is not reliable — and it happened before the county went to one-day-a-week under the May 2026 Phase III order. (2) THE POND SETBACK. A huge share of Nocatee lots back onto a retention pond, and DEP Rule 62-308.100 (effective 19 May 2026) bans turf in a pond or its littoral zone and requires 10 feet of clearance from the high water line. Publishing that you design to the setback is the single cheapest credibility signal available in this town and it directly disqualifies the cut-price installer. (3) THE HOA ANSWER. Quote FS 720.3045: the association cannot restrict turf that isn't visible from the street, a neighbour, or a common area — behind a Nocatee privacy fence, that is almost every backyard. Then offer the ARC submittal package as a service. Deliberately do NOT lead with golf or luxury here — Nocatee has no championship course, its people drive to Sawgrass, and the page next door (Sawgrass) owns that story. Nocatee's story is families, dogs, small yards, referral density and a community that watches each other's backyards from 31 miles of greenway.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: Two governing layers, and the page should explain both because Nocatee buyers are process-minded. (1) CDD: infrastructure and amenities are financed through the TOLOMATO COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DISTRICT (St. Johns County portion) and the separate SPLIT PINE CDD (Duval County portion). Tolomato CDD owns the Splash Water Park, Nocatee Swim Club, Greenleaf Pavilion, Twenty Mile Park, Cypress Trail Park, the Fitness Club, Welcome Center, athletic courts and the Nocatee Room. CDD assessments appear as a separate line on the tax bill — roughly $2,000–$3,200/year for FY2026 depending on village and lot. The CDD governs COMMON AREAS; the neighborhood HOA/ARC governs your yard. (2) HOA and state law: FS 125.572 (HB 683, signed 16 June 2025) plus DEP RULE 62-308.100, EFFECTIVE 19 MAY 2026, bar LOCAL GOVERNMENTS from prohibiting compliant synthetic turf on single-family lots of 1 acre or less — but that preemption does NOT bind private HOAs. What does bind them is FS 720.3045 (HB 437, 2023): an association may not restrict artificial turf that is NOT visible from the parcel's frontage, an adjacent parcel, an adjacent common area or a community golf course. On a Nocatee interior lot with a privacy fence, that statute is the homeowner's strongest card and the page should quote it. THE OPERATIVE DESIGN CONSTRAINT IN NOCATEE IS THE WATER SETBACK: DEP Rule 62-308.100 forbids turf in a swale, ditch, stormwater pond or a pond's littoral zone and requires it to sit NO CLOSER THAN 10 FEET from a natural or man-made waterbody measured from the ordinary or mean high water line. Given how many Nocatee lots back to a retention pond, getting that 10-foot line right is the difference between a compliant job and a rip-out. Also: no in-ground irrigation of turf areas; permeable turf, no intentionally added PFAS or heavy metals; anchored at all edges and seams; not inside a tree drip line without a certified arborist's letter. Expect the ARC to want a plot plan, product spec, base and infill spec, warranty and a physical sample.
facts.water_and_rules: Nocatee's utility is JEA — potable AND a community-wide reclaimed (purple-pipe) irrigation system — which makes it unique in this batch and gives the page a story no neighbouring town has. JEA has had genuine reclaimed-water SUPPLY AND PRESSURE PROBLEMS in Nocatee. Effective 7 April 2025 JEA imposed a Reclaimed Water Conservation Schedule that split Nocatee into FOUR WATERING ZONES, assigned days BY ZONE rather than by odd/even street address, kept two designated watering days per week, and — the key fact — made reclaimed water UNAVAILABLE FOR TWO DAYS PER WEEK on non-watering days to hold system pressure, with different zones taking different blackout days. That schedule ran through 2 November 2025, after which customers reverted to the standard SJRWMD/local restrictions. Residents look up their zone by address at jea.com/nocateewatering. On top of that, the county-wide SJRWMD/St. Johns County PHASE III EXTREME WATER SHORTAGE declared 11 May 2026 limits potable and well irrigation to ONE DAY PER WEEK with no watering 8am–6pm and restricts new sod installation; reclaimed water is exempt from the once-weekly cap but, as above, Nocatee's reclaimed supply has its own limits. Normal SJRWMD schedule: DST odd Wed/Sat, even Thu/Sun; EST one day each; max 3/4 inch and one hour per zone. No artificial-turf rebate found from JEA, SJRWMD or St. Johns County in this pass — do not claim one.
facts.soil_and_yard: Reclaimed flatwoods and former timber/wetland ground, mass-graded and filled during development. Native profile is fine sand over a spodic hardpan with a high seasonal water table — which is exactly why the community is laced with stormwater ponds and why so many rear lot lines are pond banks. Post-construction reality on a 40- or 50-foot lot: shallow builder topsoil over heavily compacted fill, sod laid straight onto it, poor infiltration, standing water after summer thunderstorms, and a rear slope engineered to move water to the pond. Full sun on most new lots (the trees are ten years old at most), so shade is NOT the failure mode here the way it is in Fruit Cove or Sawgrass — the failure modes are (a) not enough room for grass to recover from dog traffic and kid traffic in a 25-foot yard, (b) soggy low corners against the pond bank, and (c) sod that never rooted into compacted fill. Preserve-backing lots in Crosswater and Coastal Oaks have more mature canopy and more of a shade problem. NOTE: soil-series detail is regional characterisation, not read from a county soil survey in this pass.
facts.housing_stock: The purest new-build small-lot product in northeast Florida. 13,323 acres, ~27.29 sq mi, approved as a Development of Regional Impact in 2001, first homes 2005, developed by The PARC Group (Roger O'Steen). Population went from 4,524 in 2010 to 22,503 in 2020 (+397.4%) to roughly 35,080 projected for 2025 — one of the fastest-growing master-planned communities in the United States for most of the last decade. Around FIFTY distinct neighborhoods as of 2025, several age-restricted. THE LOT WIDTHS ARE THE WHOLE STORY: builders sell explicitly by frontage — 40-foot lots (e.g. Daniel Park at Town Center, ~100 homes), 40/50/60-foot lots (The Crossing at Twenty Mile), 60- and 70-foot lots (The Outlook at Twenty Mile), plus low-maintenance small-lot enclaves (The Enclave, 148 homes) and townhome products (Woodland Park, high $300s). On a 40- or 50-foot lot the rear yard is typically only about 20–35 feet deep between the lanai and the rear property line, and on a very large share of lots that rear line is a RETENTION POND or a preserve edge. Named neighborhoods include Crosswater, Coastal Oaks, Greenleaf Village, Twenty Mile and River Landing at Twenty Mile, Seabrook Village, Reflections at Seabrook, Coral Ridge at Seabrook ($1.3M+), West End at Town Center, Crosswinds, Oakwood, Del Webb Nocatee (55+) and Del Webb Ponte Vedra/Riverwood (55+). Median sale price around $678,500 (May 2026), roughly $287–310/sq ft, ~330 active listings, 86–94 days on market — a cooling, buyer-friendlier market than 2022. Homes range from $300s townhomes to $2M+ estates. HOA prevalence is effectively 100% and every neighborhood has an architectural review committee.
facts.who_lives_there: Young, high-earning, dual-income families and a large 55+ contingent side by side. Median age 40.1. Median household income $131,488 (2023, Nocatee CDP); ZIP 32081 average household income $193,713 — the highest average of any ZIP in this batch. About 50% of households report income above $150,000; only ~5% below $25,000. Overwhelmingly owner-occupied, heavily relocated-in (a lot of buyers arrive from the Northeast and Midwest with no attachment to St. Augustinegrass), and extremely socially networked — Food Truck Friday, the Splash Park, the greenway trails and neighborhood Facebook groups mean one visible job produces referrals. Dog ownership is very high and the community runs multiple dog parks.
facts.golf: Nocatee deliberately has NO championship golf course, and that is a selling point rather than a gap. PALM VALLEY GOLF CLUB — a 9-hole executive course open since 1989 with a 10,000 sq ft practice putting green — sits in the heart of Nocatee and is the local's cheap round. Everything serious is a short drive: TPC Sawgrass (Players Stadium and Dye's Valley), Sawgrass Country Club's 27 Ed Seay holes, Marsh Landing Country Club, Ponte Vedra Inn & Club (Ocean and Lagoon) to the north; The Palencia Club and Marsh Creek Country Club to the south. So Nocatee is full of serious golfers who DRIVE to their course and have no practice facility at home — the exact profile for a backyard green.
facts.commercial_targets: NOCATEE TOWN CENTER — 120+ stores, restaurants, healthcare, daycares, fitness studios and business services, all walkable/golf-cart accessible; plus Marketplace at Nocatee and the planned Hub at Nocatee (2028). TOLOMATO CDD COMMON AREAS — Splash Water Park surrounds, Spray Park, Nocatee Swim Club, Greenleaf Pavilion, Twenty Mile Park, Cypress Trail Park, Fitness Club lawns, athletic courts, and the multiple dog parks (pet turf is the obvious wedge; one CDD relationship reaches the whole community). SCHOOLS: Valley Ridge Academy (K-8, 2014), Palm Valley Academy (K-8, 2018), Pine Island Academy (K-8, 2021), Sabal Crest Academy (K-7, opening 2026-27, south of the Crosswater neighborhoods), Allen D. Nease High School, plus Ponte Vedra High School for part of the community. THE $42M ST. JOHNS COUNTY REGIONAL PARK AND LIBRARY PROJECT targeted for completion around 2027 — a live public-bid opportunity worth tracking now. Del Webb Nocatee and Del Webb Ponte Vedra 55+ amenity centres (bocce, pickleball surrounds, pet areas). Preschools, daycares, doggie daycares and veterinary practices in and around Town Center. Palm Valley Golf Club practice green.
facts.landmarks: Splash Water Park (the four-storey slide tower everyone can see) and Spray Park. Nocatee Town Center with 120+ businesses. Nocatee Swim Club and the Greenleaf Pavilion. The 31+ miles of greenway trails. The Nocatee kayak launch on the Intracoastal. The Nocatee Welcome Center. Twenty Mile Park and Cypress Trail Park. Nocatee Food Truck Friday. Allen D. Nease High School at 10550 Ray Road. Palm Valley Golf Club. Crosswater Parkway and the Nocatee Parkway connecting to US-1 and A1A.

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH THE SPLIT, AND PUT EAST ARLINGTON'S GATED-GOLF MONEY FIRST. ZIP 32225 is the highest-income ZIP in this whole batch — $90,559 median household income, $355,300 median home value, 44.5% degreed, only 8% poverty — and it is the ONLY market here where the gatekeeper is an HOA architectural review board rather than a city historic preservation commission. Open the page on Queen's Harbour and the Girvin/Atlantic corridor: HOA-governed yards, championship golf and a 65-slip Intracoastal marina on the doorstep, and a Navy-heavy relocation customer (14.9% veterans, double the national rate) arriving on PCS orders who wants the yard to look finished the week the moving truck leaves. The specific service that closes it is handling the ARB submittal — because in a covenant community the obstacle is approval, not price, and nobody else offers that. THEN give old Arlington its own clearly separated half: enormous flat 1960s and 1970s ranch backyards, no HOA, no historic review, full sun all day, and base conditions so good that the USDA soil series used as the national benchmark for this profile was described right here off St. Johns Bluff Road. Those are the biggest, easiest, highest-square-footage residential installs in Jacksonville — price them on volume. THEN add a genuine THIRD LANE no other town in this batch has: institutional and multifamily pipeline — Jacksonville University's Division I athletics and the Nexus at Regency redevelopment rising on the demolished mall site. WHY THIS IS DIFFERENT FROM NEXT DOOR: Avondale and Springfield are permit-and-preservation markets on tiny shaded lots; Ortega is private-club golf on deep peninsula lots; Murray Hill is small, cheap and dog-driven. Arlington is the SQUARE FOOTAGE market — the biggest yards, the fewest public rules, the highest household income, and the only real institutional and multifamily pipeline in the batch.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: Duval is CONSOLIDATED — City of Jacksonville Ordinance Code only, no separate Arlington municipality. CRUCIALLY: there is NO historic district design review anywhere in Arlington, unlike Avondale, Springfield and (pending verification) Old Ortega. No Certificate of Appropriateness, no Historic Preservation Commission. THE BINDING RULES IN EAST ARLINGTON ARE PRIVATE, NOT PUBLIC: gated-community and subdivision HOA ARCHITECTURAL REVIEW BOARDS. Queen's Harbour and comparable communities typically require ARB approval for rear-yard hardscape and landscape changes, and covenants may restrict street-visible synthetic materials, dictate setbacks from lot lines, or require specified drainage. VERIFY THE SPECIFIC COVENANT LANGUAGE for any community you name on the page — this research confirmed Queen's Harbour's address, amenities and Invited affiliation but did NOT read its covenants. The service offer that wins here is handling the ARB submittal package — drawings, product spec sheets, drainage detail — as part of the job, because the affluent 32225 homeowner's actual obstacle is the review board, not the price. Old Arlington (32211/32277) is largely free of both HOA and historic review — sell speed there.
facts.water_and_rules: JEA is the water/sewer utility (city-owned, all Duval). SJRWMD sets irrigation days: during daylight saving time, maximum TWO days per week, before 10 a.m. or after 4 p.m. — odd or unnumbered addresses Wednesday and Saturday; even addresses Thursday and Sunday; nonresidential Tuesday and Friday. Applies to groundwater, surface water, private wells and pumps, and utility supply. Reclaimed water exempt unless a local government restricts it. Reduced schedule during Eastern Standard Time — verify current before publishing. IMPORTANT ARLINGTON-SPECIFIC LAYER: East Arlington's gated communities and HOAs commonly impose their own irrigation, landscape and lawn-appearance standards ON TOP of the district's watering days — a homeowner can be required by covenant to keep a green lawn while being restricted by the district to two watering days a week. That tension is a genuinely strong sales argument on this page and does not exist in the no-HOA neighborhoods. No verified JEA turf rebate; the JEA conservation page was CAPTCHA-blocked in this research — confirm directly before claiming one.
facts.soil_and_yard: OWNABLE DETAIL: the USDA 'Ortega' fine sand soil series was FIRST DESCRIBED IN DUVAL COUNTY IN 1977, and its TYPE LOCATION IS IN EAST ARLINGTON — recorded as about 1,100 feet east of St. Johns Bluff Road, 1 7/16 miles south of Beach Boulevard. Fine sand throughout to depths exceeding 80 inches, moderately well drained, formed in sandy marine or eolian deposits on marine terraces, with a water table between 48 and 80 inches for 6 to 8 months annually. That is close to ideal for artificial turf base construction, and it is literally the benchmark profile for the soil, described here. Old Arlington's 1960s ranch lots are typically flat, sunny and the easiest, largest-square-footage installs in Jacksonville. THE CAVEATS: low-lying blocks near the Arlington River, Mill Cove, Pottsburg Creek and the Intracoastal have shallow water tables, tidal backflow and real flood exposure — those need elevation and drainage engineering, not a standard base; and the heavily wooded Fort Caroline and Girvin corridors carry serious live oak and pine canopy with shade and root issues closer to Avondale's than to a subdivision's.
facts.housing_stock: TWO COMPLETELY DIFFERENT MARKETS UNDER ONE NAME — write the page as two halves. Arlington is a large region east and south of the St. Johns River, west of the Intracoastal Waterway and north of the Arlington River, covering ZIPs 32211, 32277 and 32225 — about 120,593 residents over 64.3 square miles as of 2013. (1) OLD ARLINGTON (32211, 32277): after the Mathews Bridge opened in 1953, Arlington maintained a faster growth rate than any other area of Jacksonville for two decades. The result is 1950s-1970s single-story RANCH housing and genuine MID-CENTURY MODERN — Arlington is specifically known for its mid-century modern architecture, including architecturally significant homes by local architects Robert C. Broward, Taylor Hardwick and William Morgan. Sandalwood, as a reference point, began developing in spring 1960. Lots are flat, regular and generous, typically 70-100 ft frontage on 8,000-15,000 sq ft parcels with large open backyards (estimates — verify against Duval property appraiser). Almost no HOAs in the older tracts; no historic district anywhere in Arlington. (2) EAST ARLINGTON (32225): later and newer — 1980s-2000s subdivisions plus GATED GOLF AND WATERFRONT COMMUNITIES along Girvin Road, Atlantic Boulevard, McCormick Road and Mount Pleasant Road, with active HOAs, architectural review boards and amenity common areas. Smaller lots than old Arlington, but far higher values and rule-bound.
facts.who_lives_there: THE INCOME SPLIT IS THE WHOLE STORY — do not write one buyer for this page. EAST ARLINGTON, ZIP 32225: 55,905 residents over 26.3 sq mi, MEDIAN HOUSEHOLD INCOME $90,559 and per-capita $47,671 (both roughly 10% above metro, state and national), MEDIAN HOME VALUE $355,300, 95.2% high school or higher and 44.5% bachelor's or higher (about 25% above national), poverty only 8%, median age 39.6, 13.2% foreign-born, and 14.9% VETERANS — roughly double the national rate, driven by Naval Station Mayport and NAS Jacksonville. This is the HIGHEST-INCOME ZIP IN THIS ENTIRE BATCH. ARLINGTON/FORT CAROLINE, ZIP 32277: 36,338 residents, median household income $61,554, median home value $283,000, poverty 18.7%, median age 31.8, 25.9% bachelor's+, 8.8% veterans, and notably high turnover with 18.5% having moved in the past year. ARLINGTON/TERRY PARKER, ZIP 32211: 36,762 residents, median household income $57,021, median home value $229,700, poverty 22.9% (nearly double the national rate), median age 33.7, 21.6% bachelor's+, 15.6% foreign-born, 10.8% veterans. Lead the page with 32225 money; serve 32211/32277 with a value-and-square-footage offer further down.
facts.golf: QUEEN'S HARBOUR YACHT & COUNTRY CLUB, 1131 Queens Harbor Blvd, Jacksonville FL 32225 — a gated East Arlington community built around 18 holes of championship golf plus a 65-slip marina and a spring-fed yacht basin connected to the Intracoastal Waterway, with a low-country clubhouse, tennis, pool and dining. It has hosted a PGA Tour Qualifier and the Mercedes Collegiate Championships, and is now part of the Invited (formerly ClubCorp) network of more than 300 clubs. This is the anchor golf name for the page. HIDDEN HILLS — long an East Arlington private club; VERIFY current operating name, ownership and status before naming it, because the old hiddenhillscc.com domain now redirects to a domain-sale page, which suggests a change. BLUE CYPRESS GOLF CLUB is the municipal course associated with Arlington — VERIFY address and current operation; its website did not resolve and the City of Jacksonville golf page returned 403 during this research. Jacksonville University also fields NCAA Division I golf.
facts.commercial_targets: THE NEXUS AT REGENCY — the highest-value near-term commercial opportunity in this entire batch. Regency Square Mall closed 1 June 2025; Blackwater Development LLC acquired it 9 April 2025 and plans demolition followed by a mixed-use project of multifamily housing, offices and retail. New multifamily means courtyards, amenity decks, rooftop terraces, DOG RUNS and pet relief areas — get in front of that developer and their landscape architect now. JACKSONVILLE UNIVERSITY — 18 Division I programs, D.B. Milne Field, Southern Oak Stadium, plus indoor practice and training-surface needs; approach carefully and informed, because JU announced a restructuring in April 2025 that cut 40 faculty positions and reduced undergraduate programs from 60 to 37, so capital decisions there are contested and budget-sensitive. QUEEN'S HARBOUR YACHT & COUNTRY CLUB — practice greens, chipping areas, pool deck surrounds, clubhouse and marina landscape, plus the ARB relationship that opens 200+ member backyards behind one gate. Hidden Hills and other gated-community common areas (verify current status). TREE HILL NATURE CENTER and the JACKSONVILLE ARBORETUM — education and event lawns, high-traffic paths. The very dense apartment stock along Arlington Expressway, Merrill Road and University Boulevard — pet relief areas and dog parks are the highest-FREQUENCY repeat commercial sale in Arlington. Schools: Terry Parker High School, Fort Caroline Middle School and the Duval County inventory across 32211/32277/32225 (VERIFY names, addresses and catchments — not confirmed in this research).
facts.landmarks: JACKSONVILLE UNIVERSITY — 260-acre Arlington campus, founded 1934 as William J. Porter University, ~2,946 undergraduates and 1,301 postgraduates as of fall 2024, NCAA Division I in the ASUN Conference with 18 varsity teams, the SECOND-LARGEST NROTC PROGRAM IN THE COUNTRY, facilities including Swisher Gymnasium, D.B. Milne Field and Southern Oak Stadium; the 1970 men's basketball team reached the NCAA Final Four. FORT CAROLINE NATIONAL MEMORIAL — the attempted French colony established 22 June 1564 under René Goulaine de Laudonnière and lost to Pedro Menéndez de Avilés on 20 September 1565; NPS memorial established 1953, with a reconstructed fort, now part of the Timucuan Ecological and Historic Preserve. TREE HILL NATURE CENTER, 7152 Lone Star Road, 32211 — trails, museum, boardwalks, rentable amphitheater and the Arlington Community Garden. JACKSONVILLE ARBORETUM & BOTANICAL GARDENS, 1445 Millcoe Road, 135.82 acres, opened 15 November 2008 on former zircon-mining land. The four bridges: Mathews (to downtown, opened 1953), Dames Point (to the northside), Charles E. Bennett Memorial and Atlantic Boulevard (to the beaches). REGENCY SQUARE MALL, 9501 Arlington Expressway — opened 1967, once one of the most successful malls in the country at $156/sq ft in yearly sales against an $88 national average; CLOSED 1 JUNE 2025.

name: Oakleaf Plantation

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH THE TWO THINGS NO COMPETITOR IN THIS MARKET WILL KNOW: Oakleaf sits inside the county's BRANAN FIELD CORRIDOR, where Clay County Code Sec. 18.5-51 extends the landscaping article to RESIDENTIAL buildings and Sec. 18.5-53(4)(h) says synthetic turf cannot stand in for required plantings — and where Secs. 18.5-27 to 18.5-32 require an approved tree preservation plan before you disturb a protected tree's roots. And the ground under Oakleaf Plantation Parkway is BOULOGNE FINE SAND, hydrologic group C/D, poorly drained, with a wet-season water table about a foot down. Put together, that is the honest Oakleaf pitch: 'In Oakleaf your yard is both the most regulated and the worst-draining in Clay County — here is how we get it approved and here is how we build a base that actually drains.' Offer to handle the CDD/POA architectural submittal as a service; in a community with two CDDs and dozens of POAs that alone wins bids. Then the volume story: 50-70 foot lots, small fenced back yards, 33,000 people growing 2.48% a year, median household income $108,543, median age 35.4 with 31.3% under 18, and a dog in most of those yards. Small square footage per job, extreme job density, and referral chains that run straight down a single street — which is exactly the market in which to hold $10-12/sq ft on premium pet and play systems in 400-900 sq ft yards rather than discount for volume. Third beat: backyard putting greens for the Eagle Landing golf membership, and the commercial pipeline of Oakleaf High, four elementaries, a junior high, two CDD athletic centres and a full-sized indoor gymnasium. WHY DIFFERENT FROM NEXT DOOR: Asbury Lake is acreage and private wells with no HOA to answer to; Bellair is a mall and apartment complexes; Lakeside is old shaded pre-HOA suburbia; Doctors Inlet has no covenants at all. Oakleaf is the only one where the yard is small, the household earns six figures, the HOA is certain, there are two CDDs above it, AND the county code follows you home.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: THE MOST REGULATED RESIDENTIAL GROUND IN THIS BATCH, and this is the fact that should make the page. Clay County Code Sec. 18.5-52(22) defines the BRANAN FIELD CORRIDOR by metes and bounds: beginning at the Clay/Duval county line and the westerly line of LITTLE BLACK CREEK, running south along Little Black Creek to BLACK CREEK, west along Black Creek and NORTH FORK BLACK CREEK, then north along the EASTERLY BOUNDARY OF JENNINGS STATE FOREST back to the county line. Oakleaf Plantation sits inside that envelope — and Eagle Landing's own marketing confirms it borders Jennings State Forest, the corridor's west edge. INSIDE THE BRANAN FIELD CORRIDOR, Sec. 18.5-51 extends the county landscaping article to ALL RESIDENTIAL BUILDINGS, not merely nonresidential ones — and Sec. 18.5-53(4)(h) then states: 'Synthetic lawns: Synthetic or artificial turf shall not be used in lieu of plant requirements in this section.' Sec. 18-5.54 also imposes a WIDER 10-foot landscaped yard along rights-of-way inside the corridor (versus 5 feet elsewhere). On top of that, Secs. 18.5-27 through 18.5-32 make it unlawful within the Branan Field Corridor to cut, remove, damage, root-disturb or even TRIM a protected tree without an APPROVED TREE PRESERVATION PLAN — which is exactly what a trenching crew does when it runs a base edge near a street tree. Verify each parcel against the metes-and-bounds before making a promise, but the posture is clear: Oakleaf is the one place in this batch where a COUNTY landscaping rule can follow you into the yard. Then layer the private layer on top: Double Branch CDD and Middle Village CDD amenity policies plus neighbourhood POA architectural review. Statewide, Fla. Stat. 373.185 and 720.3075(4) stop an HOA banning Florida-Friendly Landscaping or imposing rules that conflict with a water shortage order — but artificial turf is NOT one of the UF/IFAS Florida-Friendly nine principles, so it gets no statutory shelter. Be straight about that; then sell the service of handling the ARB/CDD submittal.
facts.water_and_rules: Clay County Utility Authority. SJRWMD Phase III Extreme Water Shortage Order 2026-017 was in force at the 2026-09-07 check: ONE irrigation day per week — odd/no address Saturday, even Sunday, nonresidential Tuesday; never 8 a.m.-6 p.m.; three-quarters inch and one hour per zone maximum; applies to all sources including private wells. Normal schedule codified at Clay County Code Sec. 18.5-73; penalties at Sec. 18.5-79 (category 2 civil infraction first offense, category 10 thereafter, up to $500 if contested and lost, each day a separate offense, one written warning maximum). CCUA runs a RECLAIMED WATER PROGRAM — worth checking which Oakleaf phases have reclaimed service before running a water-savings pitch, because reclaimed irrigation weakens the cost argument and you should know that before the homeowner tells you. CCUA offers no landscape rebate and does not mention artificial turf; it promotes Florida-Friendly Landscaping with drought-tolerant natives. Turf qualifies for nothing — say so and pivot to the maintenance and mud arguments instead.
facts.soil_and_yard: THE WORST DRAINAGE OF THE FIVE at the built core, and this is the technical story the Oakleaf page should own. A USDA Soil Data Access point query on the Oakleaf Plantation Parkway corridor returns BOULOGNE FINE SAND, 0 to 2 percent slopes — POORLY DRAINED, minimum annual water table 31 cm (about 12 inches), HYDROLOGIC GROUP C/D. Group C/D means low infiltration; water does not simply disappear into the sand the way people assume Florida works. Across the CDP the survey also returns PAMLICO MUCK and Rutlege mucky fine sand (very poorly drained, frequently flooded) along Double Branch Creek and its tributaries, YULEE CLAY depressional (C/D), STOCKADE FINE SANDY LOAM depressional (C/D), Mascotte-Pelham complex (C/D), Pelham fine sand ponded, Lynn Haven, Leon, Sapelo and Urban land-Leon-Boulogne complex. Combine that with small, fully fenced, heavily used back yards and you get the exact Oakleaf complaint: a yard that turns to mud after every afternoon storm and never fully dries, plus dog traffic that kills what grass survives. The install answer is a base ENGINEERED FOR DRAINAGE — proper excavation depth, drainage aggregate, and where needed a subsurface drain tied out — not a permeable base laid on grade and hoped for. Reinforce with the county's own line at Sec. 18.5-53(4)(g): solid sod must be used in swales and areas subject to erosion.
facts.housing_stock: The newest stock in the batch by a mile. A 6,400-acre master-planned community ESTABLISHED IN 2002 and developed by the Hutson Companies; the CDP measures 16.42 sq mi land and only 0.16 sq mi water (Census TIGERweb, GEOID 1250630, centroid 30.1689169,-81.8336493). Population 20,315 (2010) → 28,153/31,034 (2020) → about 33,142 (2026), growing 2.48% a year — 52.8% growth in the 2010s and still building. Median age 35.4, the youngest of the five, with 31.3% of residents under 18. Typical product is two-storey production-builder housing on roughly 50-70 foot lots with small, fully fenced back yards, plus townhomes and apartments (Oakleaf Plantation Apartments, Pointe Grand at Oakleaf, CornerStone, SouthWood at Watermill). HOA prevalence is effectively 100%, and it is layered: neighbourhood POAs sit under TWO COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DISTRICTS — DOUBLE BRANCH CDD (created 2002 by ordinance of Clay County under Ch. 190, Fla. Stat.; 370 Oakleaf Village Parkway) and MIDDLE VILLAGE CDD — with board meetings at the Plantation Oaks Amenity Center, 845 Oakleaf Plantation Parkway, and Double Branch Pools serving Phase 1 and Middle Village Pools Phase 2. IMPORTANT JURISDICTIONAL SPLIT verified by TIGERweb point-in-polygon: Oakleaf's RETAIL CORE — Oakleaf Town Center, PetSmart on Crosshill Boulevard — sits in JACKSONVILLE CITY, DUVAL COUNTY, not Clay. Residential work inside the CDP falls under Clay County code; commercial work at the Town Center falls under Jacksonville's consolidated city-county code. Do not conflate the two on the page. HONEST GAP: no verified CDP-level median home value or median year built (the reliable sources were blocked or key-gated) — but 'built 2002 onward' is safe and defensible.
facts.who_lives_there: 2026 estimates: median household income $108,543, the highest of the four true CDPs in this batch; married-family median $116,657; per capita income $54,419; poverty 8.76%; median age 35.4. Wikipedia's 2020-vintage figure was $102,791. Educational attainment: 94.8% of adults 25+ have a high school diploma or better and 33.2% hold a bachelor's degree or higher. THE MOST RACIALLY DIVERSE PLACE IN THIS BATCH: 43.7% White, 31.2% Black, 6.9% Asian, 12.6% two or more races, 16.1% Hispanic. Young, well-educated, two-income, kid-heavy, dog-heavy families with real money and very little yard.
facts.golf: EAGLE LANDING AT OAKLEAF PLANTATION — an 18-hole championship course DESIGNED BY CLYDE JOHNSTON with six sets of tees including youth tees, inside a resort-style golf community developed by East West Communities that borders the 25,301-acre JENNINGS STATE FOREST. TIGERweb confirms the Eagle Landing golf/gym parcel (30.1627,-81.8508) is inside Oakleaf Plantation CDP — useful, because Eagle Landing is often listed under a Middleburg mailing address. Its Village Green amenity hub includes a general store, swim park, kids club, fitness centre, tennis complex and a FULL-SIZED INDOOR GYMNASIUM. Note for the client: the SAME ARCHITECT, Clyde Johnston, designed Eagle Harbor Golf Club on Fleming Island — a nice detail for a putting-green page that spans both communities.
facts.commercial_targets: Confirmed inside Oakleaf Plantation CDP by TIGERweb point-in-polygon: OAKLEAF HIGH SCHOOL (4035 Plantation Oaks Blvd — full athletics programme including football, baseball, softball, soccer, weightlifting); OAKLEAF JUNIOR HIGH SCHOOL, Plantation Oaks Boulevard; PLANTATION OAKS ELEMENTARY; OAKLEAF VILLAGE ELEMENTARY, Oakleaf Village Parkway; DISCOVERY OAKS ELEMENTARY; ARGYLE ELEMENTARY, Spencer Plantation Boulevard; EAGLE LANDING GYM. Highest-value targets: the EAGLE LANDING FULL-SIZED INDOOR GYMNASIUM (indoor sports turf — a direct fit for the client's indoor-facility line) and the TWO CDD ATHLETIC CENTRES with water parks and sports fields, both of which are governed by public CDD boards that let contracts in open meetings (Double Branch CDD and Middle Village CDD, district manager Marilee Giles, (904) 940-5850). Also: PET HOSPITAL AT OAKLEAF PLANTATION; TUTOR TIME childcare on Watermill Boulevard South; PETSMART on Crosshill Boulevard and the Oakleaf Town Center retail (both on the DUVAL/Jacksonville side — different code jurisdiction); Enterprise Learning Academy and Chimney Lakes Elementary just over the Duval line in Argyle Forest.

OAKLEAF VILLAGE AMENITY CENTER, 370 Oakleaf Village Parkway, and PLANTATION OAKS AMENITY CENTER, 845 Oakleaf Plantation Parkway (the two CDD 'multimillion-dollar Athletic Centers' with water parks). Eagle Landing's VILLAGE GREEN. JENNINGS STATE FOREST, 25,301 acres in Clay and Duval, home to rare plants including Bartram's Ixia. THE FIRST COAST EXPRESSWAY (SR 23) along the community's edge. facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH: 'Two lawns on your street have already gone in. We do the whole community — your backyard and your CDD's amenity centre.' The genuinely different lead for this page is CDD COMMON-AREA WORK PAIRED WITH NEW-BUILD VOLUME, because 32259's newer half is organised into a handful of very large CDD-run master plans (RiverTown, Durbin Crossing, Aberdeen, Shearwater, Beachwalk) whose pools, playgrounds, dog parks and event lawns are owned by a district board and let through a management company — one relationship, many jobs, and a visible reference installation that the whole community walks past every day. No other place in this batch has that structure at that scale in that concentration. Support it with three things: (1) THE MONEY, stated plainly — ZIP 32259 median household income $150,736, average $171,694, ~30% of households over $200,000, against Duval County's $71,277. This is a place that can pay $10–12/sq ft and needs a reason to. (2) THE POND SETBACK AS PROOF OF COMPETENCE — these master plans are built around retention ponds, lakes and wetland buffers, and DEP Rule 62-308.100 (effective 19 May 2026) bans turf in a pond or its littoral zone and requires 10 feet of clearance from the high water line. Publishing that you design to it separates you instantly. (3) THE DROUGHT — the county has been on ONE-DAY-A-WEEK irrigation since 11 May 2026 with new sod installation restricted, which in a ZIP full of two-year-old sod on compacted fill is the most persuasive fact available. Finally, the page must do SEO work its neighbours do not: explicitly disambiguate St. Johns the community from St. Johns County and the St. Johns River, and state that it covers Fruit Cove, Julington Creek, Durbin Crossing, Aberdeen, Shearwater, RiverTown and Beachwalk — 'artificial turf St Johns FL' is the highest-intent query in the county and it is ambiguous unless the page resolves it. Do NOT reuse Fruit Cove's mature-canopy lead here; these are young full-sun lots and the story is new build, ponds, CDD amenities and drought.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: Three layers, and a page for this ZIP should walk through all three because these buyers read documents. (1) STATE PREEMPTION: FS 125.572 (HB 683, signed 16 June 2025) plus DEP RULE 62-308.100, EFFECTIVE 19 MAY 2026, stop local governments prohibiting or inconsistently regulating compliant synthetic turf on single-family lots of 1 acre or less. No St. Johns County Land Development Code turf ban was located in this pass, and the county could not enforce one against a compliant residential install after that date. (2) DEP MINIMUM STANDARDS, which are the real design constraints in this ZIP: permeable turf, free of intentionally added PFAS and heavy metals; must not increase stormwater runoff or harm adjacent property or natural systems; NO in-ground irrigation of turf areas; NEVER in a swale, ditch, stormwater pond or a pond's littoral zone; NO CLOSER THAN 10 FEET from a natural or man-made waterbody measured from the ordinary or mean high water line — with this many pond-, lake- and creek-backing lots that is the make-or-break rule; not inside a tree drip line without a certified arborist's certification; anchored at all edges and seams to withstand wind or flooding. (3) PRIVATE HOA AND CDD: the state preemption binds local government, NOT associations. The homeowner's protection against the HOA is FS 720.3045 (HB 437, 2023) — an association may not restrict artificial turf not visible from the parcel frontage, an adjacent parcel, an adjacent common area or a community golf course; on Cimarrone and Julington Creek golf-frontage lots that last clause removes the protection. Separately, common areas, amenity centres, playgrounds and dog parks in RiverTown, Durbin Crossing, Aberdeen, Shearwater and Beachwalk are CDD-owned and administered by district managers, so common-area work is a procurement conversation with a board and management company, not a homeowner conversation.
facts.water_and_rules: Split service — confirm by address. St. Johns County names three providers county-wide (St. Johns County Utility, JEA, City of St. Augustine) and publishes no service-area map; the county utility has a facility at 1282 Fruit Cove Road South in this ZIP, and JEA serves parts of northwest St. Johns County. Residents call 904-209-2700 to confirm. Several master plans distribute RECLAIMED water for irrigation, which is exempt from the once-weekly cap but subject to subdivision-specific schedules — verify per community. As of the check date the county is under the SJRWMD/St. Johns County PHASE III EXTREME WATER SHORTAGE declared 11 May 2026: ONE DAY PER WEEK irrigation, none 8am–6pm, applying to utility water, private wells and pumps, and ground or surface water, with new sod and new plantings restricted and pressure washing and aesthetic water uses curtailed. This is a live and unusually strong argument in a ZIP full of brand-new sod on brand-new fill. Normal SJRWMD schedule: DST odd Wed/Sat, even Thu/Sun, non-residential Tue/Fri; EST one day each; max 3/4 inch and one hour per zone. No artificial-turf rebate found from any northeast Florida utility or SJRWMD in this pass — do not claim one.
facts.soil_and_yard: Mass-graded flatwoods and former pine plantation and wetland, filled and compacted during development, with the wetlands preserved as the amenity (Aberdeen alone keeps 500+ acres of wetland conservation and 65+ acres of lakes; Shearwater keeps 600 acres of green space along Trout Creek). Practical consequences on a 2010–2025 lot: thin builder topsoil over compacted structural fill, sod that never rooted, poor infiltration, and standing water in the low rear corner after a summer storm because the grade is engineered to move water to a retention pond. High seasonal water table and a spodic hardpan in the native profile. Most lots are full sun — trees are young — so shade is not the dominant failure mode here the way it is in Fruit Cove; preserve-backing lots are the exception. Pond banks, lake edges and wetland buffers are everywhere, which is what drives the setback issue below. NOTE: soil description is regional characterisation, not read from a county soil survey in this pass.
facts.housing_stock: IMPORTANT DISAMBIGUATION FIRST — the page has to handle this or it will confuse readers and search engines: 'St. Johns, FL 32259' is a POSTAL COMMUNITY NAME, not a city and not a census place. The same ZIP contains the Fruit Cove CDP and the Julington Creek CDP. It is also distinct from St. Johns COUNTY and from the St. Johns RIVER. Locals say 'St. Johns' to mean the newer master-planned half of 32259 — the CR-210 / Race Track Road / St. Johns Parkway corridor — while 'Fruit Cove' means the older Julington Creek Plantation side. The stock is accordingly NEWER than Fruit Cove: predominantly 2004–2026 production and semi-custom homes in large CDD-financed master plans. Named communities: RIVERTOWN (Mattamy, ~4,500 planned homes on the St. Johns River, multiple amenity centres, plus WaterSong at RiverTown, a gated 55+ enclave), DURBIN CROSSING (mature resale, north and south amenity centres), ABERDEEN (1,300+ acres with 500+ acres of wetland conservation and 65+ acres of lakes), SHEARWATER (600 acres of green space and preserved wetlands on Trout Creek), CELESTINA, BEACHWALK (Crystal Lagoon community off CR-210 — note there is also a 'Beachwalk' subdivision near Vilano Beach, so verify which one before naming it on a page), Greenbriar, Stone Creek, Worthington Park. Typical lot widths run 50–75 feet in the production sections with wider estate and preserve sections — narrower than Fruit Cove's quarter-to-half-acre Plantation lots, wider than Nocatee's 40s. Backyards are commonly 30–50 feet deep, very frequently backing a retention pond, lake or wetland preserve. HOA prevalence is effectively universal and almost every community carries a CDD assessment on top.
facts.who_lives_there: The wealthiest of the two 32259 profiles and among Florida's higher-income ZIPs. ZIP 32259 median household income $150,736, average household income $171,694, with about 30% of households above $200,000 a year and income peaking at $170,033 for householders aged 45–64. For comparison the page can use: Duval County $71,277, Jacksonville $69,872. Demographically this is dual-income professional families who moved to St. Johns County explicitly for the school district — the schools are the product, and everything from lot choice to renovation spend follows from that. High relocation share, high new-construction share, high mobility between communities inside the ZIP.
facts.golf: CIMARRONE GOLF CLUB, 2800 Cimarrone Boulevard, 32259 — semi-private, just off I-95, about ten minutes from World Golf Village, with golf-frontage residential lots. JULINGTON CREEK GOLF CLUB, 1111 Durbin Creek Blvd, 32259 — public 18-hole par 72, remodelled 2022, voted Best Public Golf Course in Northeast Florida in the 2025 JAXBest awards. Within a 15–20 minute drive via CR-210 and I-95: World Golf Village (King & Bear and Slammer & Squire) and St. Johns Golf & Country Club to the south, Jacksonville Golf & Country Club and the Deerwood clubs to the north. This is NOT a golf-identity town the way Sawgrass is — golf is one of several amenity options, and the master plans compete on lagoons, kayak clubs and fitness centres rather than fairways.
facts.commercial_targets: CDD AND HOA COMMON AREAS ARE THE STANDOUT OPPORTUNITY IN THIS ZIP, and they are institutional buyers with budgets and RFPs rather than homeowners: RiverTown (RiverClub, RiverHouse and the riverfront amenity campus), Durbin Crossing north and south amenity centres, Aberdeen amenity centre, Shearwater's Kayak Club and lagoon/pool complex, Beachwalk's Crystal Lagoon club and beach club areas, Celestina and Julington Creek Plantation recreation. Each has pool surrounds, playground fall zones, event lawns, bocce/pickleball surrounds and DOG PARKS. District management companies (the boards contract through firms like GMS, Rizzetta or VESTA — verify which manages which district before naming them) are the single highest-leverage relationship in the ZIP. SCHOOLS in and serving 32259: Patriot Oaks Academy, Freedom Crossing Academy, Liberty Pines Academy, Timberlin Creek Elementary, Durbin Creek Elementary, Cunningham Creek Elementary, Hickory Creek Elementary, Julington Creek Elementary, Switzerland Point Middle, Bartram Trail High School, Creekside High School (verify current attendance zones — St. Johns County rezones frequently). Also: Durbin Park retail centre landscaping and pad-site tenants, daycares and preschools along CR-210 and Race Track Road, veterinary practices and doggie daycares, and youth sports programs and travel-ball facilities in the northwest county.
facts.landmarks: Durbin Park / Durbin Pavilion regional retail centre at I-95 and CR-210 (verify individual tenants before naming them). The Crystal Lagoon at Beachwalk. RiverTown's riverfront amenity centres and the St. Johns River frontage along SR-13. Trout Creek and the Shearwater trail system. The Aberdeen wetland preserve and lakes. Julington-Durbin Preserve to the north. Cimarrone Golf Club off CR-210. Bartram Trail High School and Creekside High School. CR-210, Race Track Road and St. Johns Parkway — the three roads everyone in the ZIP navigates by. Note the ZIP is bounded roughly by the Duval/Mandarin line to the north and CR-210 to the south.

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH LAND, NOT LAWN, AND WITH THE ONE-DAY-A-WEEK WELL. Every other page in this service area sells a yard. Clay Hill does not have yards, it has acreage. Nobody here is turfing five acres and nobody should suggest it. The lead is: turf the 800 square feet that actually gets used, and stop fighting the rest. That means the dog run, the play set area, the practice green, the gate apron and barn approach that turns to soup every August, the pad beside the shop. Pair it with the fact that these households are on private wells and SJRWMD's Phase III Extreme Water Shortage puts private wells on ONE watering day a week with an 8 a.m.-6 p.m. blackout, so the sprinkler is not going to save the grass in the sand this year no matter what anyone does. Second differentiator, and it is a real one: this is a drive-time market that most Jacksonville turf companies simply will not serve. A page that says plainly 'we come out CR 218, we bring the trailer, we have done work past the Duval line' beats any amount of polish, because the competitor set is nearly empty. Third: no HOA, no CDD, no architectural committee, no permit theater. Customer decides on Saturday, job starts Monday. That is the opposite of the Nocatee and Fleming Island pages, where half the copy has to be about getting approval. Tone should match the place: work trucks, dogs, kids, cattle panel fence. Not resort language. Realistically this is a lower-ticket page that will not carry the $10-12/sq ft ambition on residential alone; its value is dog runs, play areas, small greens and the school/church commercial pipeline, plus proving service-area credibility on the western edge.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: The least regulated setting in the whole four-county service area, and that is a selling point. Unincorporated Clay County has no municipality involved, no CDD, and no meaningful HOA presence in the CR 218 corridor, so there is no architectural review board to satisfy and no design standard to fight. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING: I could not access the Clay County Land Development Code (Municode returned 403 and the county site was unreachable), so I found no evidence either way of a synthetic turf provision. Call Clay County Development Services and confirm before making any flat 'no restrictions' claim on the page. One statewide point that IS confirmed and that the whole site should get right: Florida Statute 373.185 bars deed restrictions and local ordinances from prohibiting Florida-Friendly Landscaping, but the statute does NOT explicitly mention or protect artificial turf. Do not tell customers state law protects their right to install turf; it does not say that.
facts.water_and_rules: Two things matter and the second is the sales lever. First, Clay Hill is largely off the utility grid: private wells and septic. Clay County Utility Authority (headquartered at 3176 Old Jennings Road, Middleburg) serves the developed Fleming Island/Orange Park/Middleburg/Oakleaf/Green Cove corridor, and its service area does not extend meaningfully into the CR 218 rural corner. VERIFY the exact CCUA boundary before making a flat claim on the page. Second, and this is the lead: the St. Johns River Water Management District has a Phase III Extreme Water Shortage order in effect, still active as of July 2026, and it explicitly covers private wells and pumps, not just utility customers. Under Phase III, landscape irrigation is limited to ONE day per week (odd or no street number: Saturday; even: Sunday; nonresidential: Tuesday), no irrigation between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m., and no more than three-quarters of an inch per zone or one hour per zone on the allowed day. New sod gets a tapering establishment allowance only (daily for 15 days, then three days a week for 30, then two days a week for 15). Clay County is named in the covered counties, and SJRWMD's own map puts the most severe shortage in the western and northwestern portion of the district, which is precisely this corner. Rebates: I found NO SJRWMD or CCUA rebate that artificial turf qualifies for. Do not imply one exists.
facts.soil_and_yard: Northwest Clay County is flatwoods country: sandy, acidic, low-organic soils over a spodic hardpan, with a seasonal high water table. The practical result is the worst of both worlds for natural grass, and it is worth saying plainly on the page: yards here bake and go droughty through the spring dry season because the sand holds nothing, then hold standing water through the summer rainy season because the hardpan will not let it go. Clay County's average elevation is only 95 ft and there is very little relief in this corner, so runoff is slow. Live oak and planted pine shade is common on older homesteads, and dense oak canopy plus sand is where St. Augustine and bahia give up entirely. Pasture-adjacent yards get chewed up by dogs, horses, ATVs and truck traffic to the shop or barn. NOTE: I was not able to pull a parcel-level USDA soil survey in this session; the flatwoods/spodic characterization is regional and should be presented as general Clay County conditions rather than a site-specific claim.
facts.housing_stock: Rural, dispersed, almost entirely non-subdivision. Northwest corner of Clay County along County Road 218, west of Middleburg and just south of the Duval line at Maxville. Wikipedia calls it a rural bedroom community with several working farms producing beef, cattle, hay and timber. Density tells the story: ZCTA 32234 (the Maxville/Clay Hill ZIP, the best available proxy since Clay Hill is not a Census Designated Place and has no standalone census data) covers 152.1 sq mi with 9,678 people, 3,464 housing units, 63.6 people per sq mi. Median home value $262,800, about 75% of the Jacksonville metro figure. Typical parcels run 1 to 10+ acres of cleared pasture and planted pine: older frame houses, 1980s-2000s ranch homes on 1-5 acre cutouts, doublewides and manufactured homes on private lots, pole barns, workshops, fenced pasture. Effectively no tract subdivision, no CDD, no meaningful HOA. Backyards are not backyards, they are acreage. CAVEAT for whoever writes the page: the Wikipedia infobox lists coordinates 30.33694N/81.66139W and elevation 250-255 ft; both look like GNIS errors (those coords plot in north Duval, and Clay County's high point is 259 ft at Camp Blanding across the county). Anchor location language to Clay Hill Elementary at 6345 County Road 218, not to that infobox. Second checkable local quirk worth using: Clay Hill mail carries a Jacksonville, FL 32234 address even though the community is in Clay County. Locals say Clay Hill; their mail says Jacksonville.
facts.who_lives_there: Bimodal, and the page should not flatten it. ZIP-wide the numbers look prosperous: median household income $87,331 (about 10% above both the Jacksonville metro and the national figure), poverty 3.9% (roughly a third of the state rate), average household size 3.0 (about 20% above state and national), residential mobility only 11.3% a year. But Clay Hill Elementary runs 60% free lunch plus 12% reduced (72% combined), which means the families with school-age kids skew well below that ZIP median. Read together: land-rich long-tenure households and higher-earning trade/commuter families on acreage, alongside a substantial lower-income population in manufactured housing. Education is blue-collar: 91.5% high school or higher, but only 20% with bachelor's degrees versus 36.5% for the Jacksonville metro. Veterans are 13.3% of the population, more than double the national rate. Foreign-born only 5.9%. Clay County overall has the third-highest median household income in Florida ($76,679 in 2021, behind St. Johns and Santa Rosa), but that wealth is concentrated in Fleming Island/Oakleaf, not out here. Most working adults commute; over half of Clay County workers work in another county and the county has Florida's third-highest average commute at nearly 33 minutes.
facts.golf: This is the honest finding: there is no golf course and no golf community in Clay Hill, and none adjacent. The nearest Clay County clubs are in the Oakleaf/Middleburg/Green Cove Springs corridor, roughly 20-40 minutes east and southeast on CR 218 and Blanding Blvd. NOTE ON VERIFICATION: I could not confirm specific course names from a live source in this session (golflink, golfpass, exploreclay and the individual club sites all returned 403/DNS errors, and the web search budget was exhausted). Do not publish course names off this brief without a quick check. The names to verify are Eagle Landing Golf Club at Oakleaf Plantation, The Ravines Golf Club in Middleburg, and Magnolia Point Golf and Country Club in Green Cove Springs. The strategic point stands regardless: the absence of golf is the golf angle here. A Clay Hill golfer drives 30-45 minutes each way to play, which makes a backyard practice green a genuinely different sell than it is in a golf community where the course is out the back gate.
facts.commercial_targets: Thin, and the page should be honest about scale rather than inventing a sports complex. Real targets: Clay Hill Elementary (426 students, PK-6) playground surfacing and field areas; Wilkinson Elementary and Wilkinson Junior High in Middleburg; the rural churches along CR 218 with fellowship lawns and children's play areas; small in-home and church daycares; kennels, boarding and veterinary clinics along the 218 corridor; horse boarding and training facilities (gate aprons, wash racks, high-traffic mud zones); the sawmill and fabrication yards for office-front and break-area installs. There is no municipal parks department competing for this work and no HOA common-area budget, so the commercial pipeline is schools, churches and animal businesses, in that order.
facts.landmarks: Clay Hill Elementary School, 6345 County Road 218 (PK-6, 426 students, 13:1 ratio). County Road 218 itself, the spine of the community. The Duval line at Maxville just to the north. Middleburg to the east, Baldwin to the north. Wilkinson Elementary and Wilkinson Junior High serve the area alongside Clay Hill Elementary. The local employer mix is itself a landmark set: a sawmill, auto and small engine repair shops, welding and fabrication yards, tree services, Dollar General stores and convenience stores. The First Coast Expressway (SR 23) is the newest one and the most useful: as of June 2026 it is open from I-10 near Whitehouse south through western Clay to SR 16 east of Green Cove Springs, with Phase 3 and the new St. Johns River bridge not due until 2031-32. That corridor runs through western Clay County near the CR 218 area and has cut drive times sharply. VERIFY whether there is an actual CR 218 interchange before claiming one. Jennings State Forest in northwest Clay County is worth verifying and using if confirmed.

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH: forest-edge acreage on wet flatwoods — the page where you prove that a turf install here is a DRAINAGE build, not a lawn swap. Bryceville is defined by Cary State Forest: 13,385 acres of longleaf pine, wet flatwoods, cypress domes and swamp forest pressed right up against private property lines since 1937. The soil under those neighbouring yards is Leon fine sand with a spodic hardpan 30-50 inches down and a water table that sits within a foot of the surface for months — soil that the USDA description says is used for forestry and pasture rather than intensive use 'without drainage improvements.' That is why grass here drowns in August and scorches in spring, and it is why the coastal contractor's standard four-inch compacted base fails. So the Bryceville lead is technical credibility: sub-base drainage, elevated base sections, perimeter drains to a real outfall, permeable backing, water-table-aware design. Nobody else's town page in this batch gets to lead with engineering, and no competitor advertising 'Jacksonville artificial turf' will say a word about a spodic hardpan. Second lead, right beneath it: this is the best putting-green geography in the whole service area for a completely different reason than Nassauville's waterfront money — there is NO golf course within 30-40 minutes, there is no HOA, no ARB, no neighbour sightline and effectively unlimited flat land, so a serious 1,000-2,000 sq ft multi-pin green with bunker and fringe is buildable at a scale that will never fit a Nocatee or Wildlight lot. Third: the $22M Westside Regional Park is the highest-value named commercial target in west Nassau and should be worked at the design stage, with the existing three-field Bryceville Ball Park as the credibility job that comes first.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: Unincorporated Nassau County — no municipal code, no HOA, no CDD, no architectural review. Nassau County LDC applies, including Appendix A, Article 37, § 37.05 (Landscaping), which states that 'Synthetic or artificial trees, shrubs, groundcovers or vines are not acceptable substitutes' — meaning synthetic material cannot count toward required landscape material on commercial, multi-family or subdivision plans, though it does not restrict a residential yard. § 37.05's residential tree standard (one tree per 3,000 sq ft of lot area for the first quarter acre, plus one per additional quarter acre, with existing canopy trees, sabal palms and pine trees counting) is met many times over on Bryceville acreage. State overlay: F.S. 125.572, from Ch. 2025-140 / HB 683 effective July 1, 2025, prevents counties from prohibiting compliant synthetic turf on single-family residential parcels of one acre or less once FDEP adopts standards — note that many Bryceville parcels exceed one acre and so fall outside that preemption's literal scope, which is academic since nothing prohibits it here anyway. Verify FDEP's rule adoption status before treating it as final. The binding constraints in practice are wetland delineation and buffers, septic drainfield and well setbacks, and Nassau County stormwater / land-disturbance thresholds — those are what a Bryceville job actually has to clear, and saying so on the page signals competence.
facts.water_and_rules: JEA serves Bryceville per the Nassau County Chamber resident guide (alongside Yulee, Callahan and Hilliard), but at this density a large share of properties are on private wells and septic — confirm per address. Electricity is Florida Power & Light and Okefenokee REMC. SJRWMD Phase III Extreme Water Shortage Declaration is in force across Nassau County (declared May 11, 2026): landscape irrigation limited to one day per week, prohibited 8 a.m.–6 p.m., maximum three-quarters of an inch and one hour per zone; odd or no address = Saturday, even = Sunday, non-residential = Tuesday. The order explicitly covers private wells and pumps and ground or surface water — so the well owners here are not exempt, which is worth stating plainly because most assume they are. New plantings and sod get only a tapering grow-in allowance: daily for 15 days, then 3 days/week for 30 days, then 2 days/week for 15 days — under Phase III, establishing new St. Augustine sod in west Nassau is close to unworkable. Reclaimed water is exempt from the one-day schedule but is not distributed here. No artificial turf rebate is offered by JEA, SJRWMD or Nassau County. UF/IFAS does not classify artificial turf as Florida-Friendly, so do not make FFL claims.
facts.soil_and_yard: This is the wettest, most technically demanding ground in the batch, and it should be the page's proof of expertise. Bryceville is wrapped around Cary State Forest, which encompasses eleven habitats dominated by longleaf pine, WET FLATWOODS, CYPRESS DOMES and swamp forest — the forest's own habitat inventory tells you exactly what the neighbouring private land is. Soils are Leon fine sand and related spodosols: very deep, poorly to very poorly drained acid fine sand throughout, a spodic (Bh) hardpan beginning roughly 30-50 inches below the surface, very rapid permeability near the surface transitioning to much slower permeability below, slopes 0-2%, and a high water table commonly at 0-12 inches for significant parts of the year, subject to prolonged saturation and hydric conditions. Under natural conditions these soils support wetland-adapted forest and are used for forestry, range and pasture rather than intensive use 'without drainage improvements.' Translated into installation practice: the top foot percolates beautifully and then water sits on the hardpan; a standard 3-4 inch compacted-base spec designed for well-drained coastal sand will float, rut and hold odour here. You need to talk about sub-base drainage, elevated base sections, French drains or perimeter drains tied to a real outfall, permeable backing and mid-summer versus spring water table swings. Add pine straw drop, palmetto, deep pine shade, deer and, on cleared parcels, real sun exposure with no windbreak.
facts.housing_stock: Unincorporated community in southwestern Nassau County along US 301 at roughly 30.38N, -81.94W, ZIP 32009, with CR 119 intersecting to the north and Otis Road to the south. No CDP and no census-place table exists, so the commonly cited population of about 4,045 is a ZIP-code-level figure, not a place figure — label it as such. Housing is rural acreage: scattered single-family homes, ranches and manufactured homes on large parcels between the state forest tracts and the timber land, with newer custom builds appearing as Jacksonville commuters push west. No HOA, no CDD, no architectural review, no platted subdivision character. Not historic, not new-build — this is working rural Nassau County that happens to sit 30 minutes from downtown Jacksonville via US 301 and Baldwin. Backyards are effectively unlimited in size but heavily wooded and often wet: pine, palmetto, cypress heads and pasture rather than turf-ready graded lawn. The turf-relevant consequence is that the DESIGNED area is small even though the parcel is large — a defined 800-2,000 sq ft outdoor room carved out of woods, not a lawn edge to edge.
facts.who_lives_there: Middle-income, mixed-collar, family-aged, and notably better off than Nassau Village-Ratliff next door. Median household income $72,792. Median age 36, with roughly 17.2% under 15, 21.5% aged 15-24, 18.3% aged 25-44, 27.7% aged 45-64 and about 15.3% aged 65+. 15.45% of adults 25+ hold a bachelor's or advanced degree — below the national average. The workforce is described as genuinely mixed rather than predominantly blue- or white-collar: managers, professionals, sales and office workers alongside trades. Crime is among the lowest in the country. Read for the client: these are people who own land, own trucks and trailers, do a lot of their own work, and will price-shop hard — but who have real household income and are used to spending on the property. They buy on durability and on 'I am done fighting this,' not on prestige. Horse and livestock properties are common in this soil and zoning context; verify before claiming a specific equestrian market.
facts.golf: None. There is no golf course in Bryceville and nothing nearby — the Amelia Island / SR 200 cluster (The Golf Club at North Hampton, Amelia National, Fernandina Beach Golf Club, Amelia River Club) is roughly 30-40 minutes northeast, and the Jacksonville westside public courses are the other option. This is the most golf-isolated place in the batch and the page must not pretend otherwise. The honest inversion is the strongest putting-green argument in the whole service area: a Bryceville golfer has no convenient short-game practice anywhere, and has the one thing coastal buyers do not — unlimited flat land, no HOA, no ARB and no neighbour sightlines. A 1,000-2,000 sq ft multi-pin green with bunker and fringe is buildable here at a scale that simply will not fit on a Nocatee or Wildlight lot.
facts.commercial_targets: The single biggest named opportunity in west Nassau is here: Westside Regional Park, a roughly $22M Nassau County facility in Bryceville, described by the county as 'serving all of Nassau County, with emphasis on underserved residents in the Western parts of Nassau.' Get in front of Nassau County Parks & Recreation and the design consultant during programming, not at bid — a regional park of that budget will be deciding natural versus synthetic on multi-purpose fields. Existing Bryceville Ball Park / Bryceville Sports Association: three baseball/softball fields, a concessions/restroom building and a playground, with a new playground added under the county's roughly $3M parks investment and an Integrated Lightning Prediction and Warning System installed — near-term jobs are batting/practice areas, bullpen and mound covers, dugout floors, playground fall zones and infield surrounds. Bryceville Elementary School (state-graded 'A'), under Nassau County School District, the county's largest employer at 1,598 staff. Nassau County Public Library, Bryceville branch. Nassau County Fire Rescue Station 60. Bryceville Methodist Church. Cary State Forest's campsite and day-use facilities (state Forest Service — a slower procurement path, but real). Equine, boarding and kennel operations on the surrounding acreage are the likeliest private commercial accounts; verify individual businesses before naming them.
facts.landmarks: Cary State Forest — Florida's second state forest, established 1937, 13,385 acres, on the east side of US 301 between Bryceville and Ingle, with the Cary (main) Tract, the Monticello Tract behind it and the Norfolk Southern Tract to the southeast; hiking, biking and equestrian trails, primitive and RV campsites with restroom and shower facilities, and eleven habitat types including longleaf pine, wet flatwoods, cypress domes and swamp forest. Bryceville Methodist Church. Bryceville Elementary School (K-5). Nassau County Public Library, Bryceville branch. Nassau County Fire Rescue Station 60. Bryceville Ball Park. US 301, CR 119 and Otis Road. Position between Baldwin (Duval) to the south and Callahan to the north, inside the Jacksonville metro / First Coast.

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH THE 25-YEAR-OLD SHADED BACKYARD IN THE HIGHEST-INCOME ZIP ON THE FIRST COAST — and with the POA submittal you handle for them. This is the page that is NOT about new construction. Nocatee's page is a 2020 house on a 50 ft lot with bare fresh sand; Julington Creek is a 1998-2005 house whose lawn has already been replaced twice, under slash pines and live oaks that were saplings at closing and now shade the whole rear yard, on a lot that likely backs to one of 100+ lakes or to preserve. The homeowner has already tried resod, already tried a landscaper, and lost. Two things make this town's lead different from every neighbour: (1) ZIP 32259 quietly out-earns Ponte Vedra Beach — $149,213-$150,736 median household income versus $127,105 in 32082 — so this is $10-12/sq ft territory that does not read that way from the outside, and the page should say so plainly rather than positioning JCP as budget suburbia; (2) the double CDD+POA governance is a friction point every competitor ignores. Say out loud that the POA administers covenant compliance, that you prepare the architectural submittal with product spec, pile height, colour, drainage detail and border treatment, and that you know which older neighbourhoods opted out of the CDD. Layer the drought over it: under the Phase III order in effect since 11 May 2026 it is currently ILLEGAL to install new sod in St. Johns County, and irrigation is one day a week — so the honest headline is that the thing his competitor sells cannot legally be installed right now and turf can. Then close on golf: with Julington Creek Golf Club inside the community and Cimarrone next door, the backyard putting green is a normal purchase here, not an extravagance.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: No artificial-turf-specific residential provision exists in the St. Johns County Land Development Code — verified by full-text search of Article V (Development Options, 11 Aug 2025) and Article VI (Design Standards, 12 Jan 2026); neither 'artificial turf' nor 'synthetic turf' appears anywhere. The operative county constraints are the 70% impervious surface ratio cap and the 10 ft rear-yard setback in Table 6.01. ONE real code trap, and it is a commercial one: LDC Sec. 6.06.02.A.5 states that non-living ground cover such as rocks, gravel and mulch may be used in combination with living plant material, but 'The use of artificial plants shall not be permitted to meet any of the landscaping requirements.' Those landscaping regulations apply to development requiring a Development Permit (buildings, off-street parking areas) — NOT to a homeowner re-doing a backyard. So on an HOA-common-area or commercial job in JCP, artificial turf cannot be counted toward the required landscape area; on a house, it is unregulated by the county. The gate is the POA. JCP's POA administers covenant compliance, so every install should assume an architectural/ARB submittal. Florida Statute 373.185 bars a deed restriction from prohibiting Florida-Friendly Landscaping, but the statutory definition — quality landscapes that conserve water, protect the environment, are adaptable to local conditions and are drought tolerant — does NOT name synthetic turf, so that protection does not cleanly extend to artificial grass. Also county-wide: fertilizer capped at 5 lbs nitrogen per 1,000 sf per year, none applied under a flood/tropical storm/hurricane watch.
facts.water_and_rules: Provider: JEA. JEA's Major Grid supplies water to most of Duval County and the NORTHWEST portion of St. Johns County, which is exactly this area. Current status at check date 2026-09-07: SJRWMD Phase III EXTREME Water Shortage Declaration, issued 11 May 2026, still in effect across Clay, Duval, Flagler, Nassau, Putnam and St. Johns counties. Under Phase III: landscape irrigation ONE day per week only — odd-numbered or no address Saturday, even-numbered Sunday, nonresidential Tuesday — with NO irrigation 8 a.m. to 6 p.m., max 3/4 inch per zone and one hour per zone. Critically, the order PROHIBITS NEW SOD INSTALLATION AND NEW PLANTINGS outright, plus aesthetic water uses, street and pressure washing. It applies to public and private utilities AND private wells and pumps. St. Johns County calls this the most severe drought level in Florida since the U.S. Drought Monitor began in 2000.
