Standard non-drought schedule for when the order lifts: DST (Mar-Nov) odd Wed+Sat, even Thu+Sun, nonres Tue+Fri; EST (Nov-Mar) odd Sat, even Sun, nonres Tue; never 10 a.m.-4 p.m. Reclaimed water is exempt from the one-day rule, but St. Johns County reclaimed service covers only Twin Creeks and SilverLeaf — JCP is not on it. NO artificial turf rebate found: the county water conservation page lists no landscape or turf-conversion incentive (Utility Dept 904-209-2700, utilbill@sjcfl.us). Enforcement via SJC Code Enforcement 904-209-0734 or the SJC Connect app.
facts.soil_and_yard: Northeast Florida coastal-plain flatwoods sand. The dominant regional series is Myakka fine sand, Florida's official state soil — a spodosol whose profile runs dark gray sand at the surface, gray sand to about 26 inches, then an organic-stained spodic layer (the 'hardpan') to roughly 60 inches. Water permeates rapidly through the surface and subsurface but only moderately through that subsoil, and the natural water table sits within 10 inches of the surface for one to five months a year, dropping past 40 inches in dry spells. Practical consequence for turf base: excavation is easy but the perched layer means water goes sideways, not down, in the wet season — base depth and a positive drainage plane matter more here than compaction. JCP adds 100+ lakes and 1,200 acres of preserve, so a large share of lots sit low and adjacent to standing water. Shade is the other half of the story: 25-30 years of live oak and slash pine growth has produced the classic thinning, bare, root-competed St. Augustine backyard that is the single most common reason a JCP homeowner calls a turf installer.
facts.housing_stock: 4,120-acre master-planned CDD community, ~5,800 homes, NW St. Johns County along Race Track Road east of SR 13, ~20 mi south of downtown Jacksonville and 7 mi south of I-295. District created 15 Aug 1994 by FLWAC rule Ch. 42-T-11-13 F.A.C., so the stock is a late-1990s-to-mid-2000s production build-out. NOT new build, NOT historic: these are 20-30 year old yards where the original St. Augustine sod is on its third or fourth generation and the slash pines and live oaks planted at build-out are now mature enough to shade a north-facing backyard out completely. JCP is a PUD so its own standards govern, but county baseline Table 6.01 (LDC Art. VI, 12 Jan 2026) brackets the product: RS-3 7,500 sf / 75 ft width, RS-2 10,000 sf / 90 ft, RS-1 13,200 sf / 120 ft; 10 ft minimum rear yard; 70% impervious surface ratio cap in every residential district. Expect usable backyards roughly 1,500-4,000 sf, with premium lots backing to one of the community's 100+ lakes or to the 1,200 acres of nature preserve. Preserve-backing lots are the shadiest and most turf-hostile. HOA prevalence is effectively total and unusually LAYERED: JCP runs both a CDD and a POA. The CDD (Ch. 190 F.S. special-purpose government, five elected supervisors, managed by Wrathell Hunt & Associates, 561-571-0010) owns the amenities and the landscaping between Race Track Road and the sidewalks; the POA handles irrigation/landscaping on interior common ground AND administers covenant compliance. Some pre-existing neighborhoods inside Julington Creek voted to OPT OUT of the CDD and are not in the district — worth asking every lead which side of that line they are on. River Oaks Plantation is entirely inside the same CDD.
facts.who_lives_there: No census-place data exists for Julington Creek Plantation — the Wikipedia article is a stub with no demographic table, and it is not a CDP. Use ZIP 32259 (Saint Johns / Fruit Cove) as the honest proxy: median household income $150,736 in 2024 (zipdatamaps/incomebyzipcode) and $149,213 as of Dec 2025 per a St. Johns Citizen analysis, which makes 32259 the HIGHEST-income ZIP on the First Coast — ahead of Nocatee 32081 ($132,087), 32095 ($128,915), Ponte Vedra Beach 32082 ($127,105) and World Golf Village 32092 ($126,947). Countywide median is $108,800, up 55% since 2015. ZIP population 62,169, median age 41.5, home value $533,400, and 57 properties in 32259 listed over $1M in a recent week. Profile: dual-income professional and executive families with school-age kids who moved here for the schools (JCP is fed by top-rated St. Johns County schools; the district has held an A grade for two decades).
facts.golf: Julington Creek Golf Club / The Champions Club at Julington Creek, 1111 Durbin Creek Blvd, St. Johns/Fruit Cove FL 32259 — 18-hole par 72, remodeled 2022, (904) 287-4653. Listed as public by PGA of America and as private in St. Johns Magazine's local course list, so verify current access before referencing it. Cimarrone Golf Club, 2800 Cimarrone Blvd, 32259 — semi-private, a gated golf community immediately adjacent off CR 210. The CDD's own material lists 'golf opportunities' among resident amenities. Further out but same customer: TPC Sawgrass and the Ponte Vedra Inn & Club are a 25-30 minute drive east.
facts.commercial_targets: CDD-owned amenity grounds first — the Plantation Club Recreation Center (350 Plantation Club Pkwy), the Aquatic Complex, the Sports Plex, the tennis courts, the basketball courts and Plantation Park are all CDD assets with a five-member elected board that meets the second Tuesday of every month in public, plus a district manager (Wrathell, Hunt & Associates, 561-571-0010) and an on-site rec center staff — a genuinely reachable procurement path for court surrounds, dog areas and worn field corners. The POA separately maintains neighborhood entrances, boundary fences, playgrounds and signage. Schools: Julington Creek Elementary, Durbin Creek Elementary, Cunningham Creek Elementary, Hickory Creek Elementary, Fruit Cove Middle, Switzerland Point Middle, Bartram Trail High (7399 Longleaf Pine Pkwy) and Creekside High. Julington Creek Golf Club / Champions Club at 1111 Durbin Creek Blvd for practice greens, tee lines and range mats. Cimarrone Golf Club, 2800 Cimarrone Blvd. The Race Track Road retail corridor for daycares, vets and pet businesses.
facts.landmarks: The Plantation Club Recreation Center, 350 Plantation Club Parkway, Fruit Cove (904-438-2530). The JCP Aquatic Complex and the Sports Plex. Race Track Road and Durbin Creek Blvd. State Road 13, the William Bartram Scenic and Historic Highway, on the community's western edge. The four-lane span over Julington Creek. Over 100 lakes, 1,200 acres of nature preserve and seven miles of bike and jogging trails inside the community. The CDD boundary quirk that locals know: some older neighborhoods opted out of the district and do not get amenity access.

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH ACREAGE AND NO ARCHITECTURAL REVIEW BOARD — the private backyard golf complex on a river-bluff acre under 200-year-old live oaks. Every other page in this batch is about fitting turf into someone else's rules. Switzerland is the page where you say: this is a one-acre-minimum, RS-E and Open Rural zoning corridor along a designated scenic highway, many of these SR 13 parcels are not in any HOA, and there is nobody to ask. That flips the entire pitch from compliance to ambition — not a 400 sq ft green squeezed against a 10 ft rear setback, but a multi-tier practice complex with a chipping area, a bunker and a real tee line, because there is finally room for one. Three supports no neighbouring town can copy: (1) 32259 is the highest-income ZIP on the First Coast at ~$150k median household income, above Ponte Vedra Beach, and the river estates sit at the top of it, so this is the $10-12/sq ft page; (2) the live oaks are the genuine article on old plantation ground — under that canopy St. Augustine will never take, and the shaded-oak-drip-line install is the highest-conviction job in the county; (3) a large share of these homes irrigate an ACRE off a PRIVATE WELL, and the Phase III order in effect since 11 May 2026 expressly covers private wells and pumps, cuts irrigation to one day a week, and prohibits new sod installation outright. So the honest close is: you cannot legally sod it right now, your well cannot economically water it when you can, and there is no ARB standing between you and the alternative. Contrast the page explicitly against Julington Creek Plantation next door — same ZIP, same money, completely different job: JCP is a 7,500 sf lot with a POA covenant submittal, Switzerland is an acre with a gate and a dock.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: The most permissive rule environment of the five. Switzerland is unincorporated St. Johns County, so there is no municipal ordinance layer at all — Duval-style consolidated city rules do not apply here. The county Land Development Code contains NO artificial-turf provision: full-text search of Article V (11 Aug 2025) and Article VI (12 Jan 2026) returns no 'artificial turf' or 'synthetic turf' anywhere. The only county limits on a residential job are the 70% impervious surface ratio and the yard setbacks in Table 6.01 (RS-E 30/20/20 ft, OR 25/10/10 ft). LDC Sec. 6.06.02.A.5 — 'The use of artificial plants shall not be permitted to meet any of the landscaping requirements' — is tied to development requiring a Development Permit, so it bites on a commercial or multifamily landscape plan, not on a homeowner's backyard. Crucially, many older SR 13 acreage parcels sit OUTSIDE any HOA, so there is no architectural review board to satisfy — a real differentiator worth stating outright. Newer platted estate subdivisions in the corridor will have covenants, so qualify each lead. Florida Statute 373.185 prevents a deed restriction prohibiting Florida-Friendly Landscaping, but its definition does not name synthetic turf, so do not promise that statute as an HOA override. County fertilizer rule: 5 lbs nitrogen per 1,000 sf per year maximum, none under a storm watch or warning. Septic drainfield location is the practical constraint to survey before excavating.
facts.water_and_rules: Mixed provider picture, and this is worth getting right on the page. JEA's Major Grid supplies the northwest portion of St. Johns County, which covers much of the Switzerland/Fruit Cove corridor — but a meaningful share of the rural acreage along SR 13 is on PRIVATE WELLS and septic. That does not exempt anyone: the SJRWMD Phase III Extreme Water Shortage Declaration issued 11 May 2026 and still in effect on 2026-09-07 applies expressly to 'water supplied by public and private utilities, private wells and pumps, and ground or surface water sources.' Phase III means landscape irrigation ONE day a week — odd or no address Saturday, even Sunday, nonresidential Tuesday — no irrigation 8 a.m. to 6 p.m., max 3/4 inch and one hour per zone, and NEW SOD INSTALLATION AND NEW PLANTINGS PROHIBITED, along with aesthetic water uses, street and pressure washing. St. Johns County describes it as the most severe drought level in Florida since the U.S. Drought Monitor began in 2000. Standard schedule when it lifts: DST odd Wed+Sat / even Thu+Sun / nonres Tue+Fri; EST odd Sat / even Sun / nonres Tue; never 10 a.m.-4 p.m. County reclaimed water reaches only Twin Creeks and SilverLeaf, neither of which is here. No turf rebate found in St. Johns County — the county water conservation page offers no landscape or turf-conversion incentive; confirm with Utilities at 904-209-2700. Extra angle unique to well owners: an acre of irrigated lawn on a private well is a pump-and-electricity cost, and on a shared shallow aquifer a genuine dry-season risk.
facts.soil_and_yard: Same flatwoods spodosol as the rest of northwest St. Johns — Myakka-type fine sand, dark gray at the surface, gray to roughly 26 inches, then an organic-stained hardpan to about 60 inches, with the natural water table within 10 inches of the surface for one to five months a year and dropping past 40 inches in dry periods. But Switzerland adds two things the suburban communities do not. First, RIVER FRONTAGE: parcels running down to the St. Johns River mean bluff slope, tidal/brackish influence at the toe, and stormwater arriving from uphill neighbours — grading and edge restraint matter more here than anywhere else in the batch. Second, GENUINELY OLD CANOPY: this is 250-year-old plantation country along a designated scenic highway, and the live oaks are the real thing, not builder plantings. Under a mature live oak the combination of dense shade, surface root mat and leaf/acorn drop makes St. Augustine effectively impossible — that shaded oak drip line is the highest-conviction turf pitch in this town. Also expect areas of wooded parcel that have never been cleared, so scope should assume grubbing and root work, not just sod removal.
facts.housing_stock: The oldest and most rural face of northwest St. Johns County, and the exact opposite of the CDD suburbia next door. Switzerland is an unincorporated community on the EASTERN BANK of the St. Johns River, adjacent to Fruit Cove, across the water from Green Cove Springs and Middleburg in Clay County, sharing ZIP 32259. Its spine is State Road 13, designated the William Bartram Scenic and Historic Highway. The pattern here is large parcels along SR 13, riverfront properties, horse land and stretches of woods that were never developed — plus newer estate infill squeezed between them. The relevant county zoning is not the 7,500 sf suburban product: it is RS-E (minimum 1 acre, 150 ft lot width, 30/20/20 ft yards) and Open Rural OR (minimum 1 acre, 100 ft width, 25/10/10 ft yards, 35% max lot coverage), both capped at a 70% impervious surface ratio (LDC Art. VI Table 6.01, 12 Jan 2026). Section 6.01.05 sets larger minimum lot area and width where a septic tank is used — and septic and private wells are common out here. So the typical job is an acre-plus parcel with a genuinely large rear yard, mature canopy, a long driveway, possibly a dock, and frequently NO HOA at all. Historic in name rather than in built fabric: the name comes from Francis Philip Fatio's New Switzerland Plantation, established between 1771 and 1774, but the houses are overwhelmingly late-20th-century and newer.
facts.who_lives_there: Honest caveat: Switzerland has no census-place data of its own — no CDP, no population table on Wikipedia. The only defensible proxy is ZIP 32259, which it shares with Fruit Cove: median household income $150,736 (2024) / $149,213 (Dec 2025), the highest ZIP median on the First Coast, ahead of Ponte Vedra Beach 32082 at $127,105; ZIP population 62,169, median age 41.5, home value $533,400, 57 listings over $1M in a recent week. Within that ZIP, Switzerland skews toward the acreage-and-riverfront end: established, older-skewing, equity-rich owners plus horse people and boat people, alongside newer high-income families buying estate lots. Wikipedia notes that newer residents simply call the whole Fruit Cove/Switzerland area 'Saint Johns' while the historic names persist locally — a useful detail for how the page should talk.
facts.golf: There is no golf course IN Switzerland — say so honestly rather than inventing one. The nearest are Julington Creek Golf Club / The Champions Club at Julington Creek, 1111 Durbin Creek Blvd, Fruit Cove 32259 (18 holes, par 72, remodeled 2022) and Cimarrone Golf Club, 2800 Cimarrone Blvd, 32259, a gated semi-private golf community off CR 210 — both a short drive north/east. St. Johns Golf & Country Club (205 St Johns Golf Dr, 32092) and King & Bear / Slammer & Squire at World Golf Village are 25-35 minutes south. That absence is the selling point, not a weakness: the acreage here is what lets a Switzerland owner build the practice complex at home that a JCP lot cannot fit.
facts.commercial_targets: Schools are the anchor: Hickory Creek Elementary, Cunningham Creek Elementary, Switzerland Point Middle School and Bartram Trail High School all serve this area (Wikipedia, Switzerland FL). Switzerland Community Church, 2179 SR 13. Equestrian properties and boarding barns along the SR 13 corridor — horse land is explicitly part of the local pattern, and paddock aprons, wash racks and barn alleys are a real turf application. Marinas, private docks and riverfront event venues. Veterinary and boarding businesses serving the acreage crowd. Because so much of Switzerland is unplatted, HOA common-area work is thinner here than in the CDD towns — be honest about that and aim commercial effort at schools, the church, barns and riverfront venues instead.
facts.landmarks: State Road 13 / the William Bartram Scenic and Historic Highway itself. Switzerland Community Church, 2179 SR 13, St. Johns FL 32259. Hartley's Switzerland Store, an Old Florida landmark on SR 13. The St. Johns River shoreline with Green Cove Springs and Middleburg visible across the water. Switzerland Point Middle School. The site of Francis Philip Fatio's New Switzerland Plantation (established 1771-1774), the source of the community's name. Bartram Trail High School, named for the same naturalist. The Mill Creek historic mill site (archaeological site 8SJ2458) west of SR 13 — an earthen dam thought to date to the late 18th or early 19th century.

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH: 'Thirty years of live oak canopy killed your lawn. Here is the yard that actually works under it — and the arborist letter to do it legally.' Fruit Cove is the ONLY place in this batch where the problem is mature shade rather than new construction, coastal salt or a tiny lot. Median year built 2002, Julington Creek Plantation dating to the late 1980s, quarter- to half-acre lots on a river bluff cut by Julington and Durbin creeks — meaning full-sun sod laid 25–35 years ago now sitting under a closed oak canopy, with root competition the homeowner cannot beat and a soggy low corner that never dries because of the flatwoods hardpan. Every neighbouring town page is about new lots; this one is about a retrofit on a big, mature, half-shaded yard, and the ticket is bigger because the yards are bigger. The killer technical hook is DEP Rule 62-308.100's requirement (effective 19 May 2026) that synthetic turf NOT be installed inside a tree's drip line unless a CERTIFIED ARBORIST certifies it will not harm the tree. In a town of 30-year-old live oaks that rule touches most of the backyard — so the page should say plainly that you work with a certified arborist, keep the root zone breathing with a permeable base, and hold the required 10-foot setback off Julington and Durbin creek banks and any pond. That is a genuinely specialist claim, it is checkable, it is unavailable to the $7/sq ft crew, and it is exactly the argument that moves this town toward $10–12/sq ft. Secondary hooks: drainage correction as part of the install (the wet back corner is half the reason they are calling); and the fact that Julington Creek Golf Club and Cimarrone put golf frontage on ordinary suburban lots, so FS 720.3045's community-golf-course exception applies here and the ARC package matters. Do NOT reuse the Nocatee small-lot lead or the St. Johns 32259 new-build lead — Fruit Cove is the mature-canopy retrofit town.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: The tree rule is the one that defines work in this town. DEP RULE 62-308.100, EFFECTIVE 19 MAY 2026 under FS 125.572 (HB 683, signed 16 June 2025), sets statewide minimum standards for synthetic turf on single-family lots of 1 acre or less and bars local governments from regulating inconsistently. Its provisions, ranked by how much they matter in Fruit Cove: (1) SYNTHETIC TURF SHALL NOT BE INSTALLED INSIDE A TREE DRIP LINE UNLESS A CERTIFIED ARBORIST CERTIFIES THAT INSTALLATION WITHIN THAT DRIP LINE WOULD NOT BE HARMFUL TO THE TREE — in a neighborhood of 30-year-old live oaks whose drip lines cover most of the backyard, this is not a footnote, it is the job; (2) no closer than 10 feet from a natural or man-made waterbody measured from the ordinary or mean high water line, and never in a swale, ditch, stormwater pond or littoral zone — this governs the creek-, ravine- and pond-adjacent lots; (3) turf must be permeable, free of intentionally added PFAS and heavy metals, and must not increase stormwater runoff or harm adjacent properties; (4) no in-ground irrigation of turf areas; (5) anchored at all edges and seams to withstand wind or flooding; (6) septic tank access must be maintained where applicable — relevant on older unsewered SR-13 river parcels. HOA layer: FS 720.3045 (HB 437, 2023) prevents an association restricting turf not visible from the parcel frontage, an adjacent parcel, an adjacent common area or a community golf course — note the golf-course clause applies on Julington Creek Golf Club and Cimarrone frontage lots. Julington Creek Plantation is CDD-governed for common areas with a separate homeowner architectural process for individual lots. No St. Johns County LDC provision specifically banning artificial turf was located in this pass, and after 19 May 2026 the county could not enforce one against a compliant residential install anyway.
facts.water_and_rules: Split service — confirm by address. St. Johns County lists three providers county-wide (St. Johns County Utility, JEA, City of St. Augustine) with no published service-area map; the ST. JOHNS COUNTY UTILITY DEPARTMENT has a facility at 1282 Fruit Cove Road South, 32259, and JEA also serves parts of the northwest county. Residents confirm by calling 904-209-2700. As of the check date the county is under the SJRWMD/St. Johns County PHASE III EXTREME WATER SHORTAGE declared 11 May 2026: irrigation ONE DAY PER WEEK, no watering 8am–6pm, applying to public and private utility water, PRIVATE WELLS AND PUMPS (relevant — a lot of the older large-lot and riverfront properties here irrigate from wells), and ground or surface water; new sod and new plantings restricted. Normal SJRWMD schedule: DST odd Wed/Sat, even Thu/Sun, non-residential Tue/Fri; EST one day each; max 3/4 inch and one hour per zone. Reclaimed water is exempt from the once-weekly cap, but reclaimed distribution here is patchy compared with Nocatee. No artificial-turf rebate found from any northeast Florida utility or SJRWMD in this pass — do not claim one.
facts.soil_and_yard: This is the SHADE-AND-DRAINAGE town. Fruit Cove sits on the east bank of the St. Johns River on a low bluff and ravine system cut by Julington Creek and Durbin Creek — the Julington-Durbin Preserve occupies the peninsula between them. Native cover is live oak, laurel oak, magnolia and slash pine, and in the Plantation-era neighborhoods that canopy has had 25–35 YEARS to close over lawns that were sodded in full sun in 1990. The result is the single most common call in this ZIP: St. Augustinegrass thinning to bare dirt under mature oaks, root competition the homeowner cannot beat, and moss and weeds taking the difference. Underneath, flatwoods fine sand over a spodic hardpan holds water in low spots, and the ravine and creek-adjacent lots have real slope plus a shallow water table near the creeks and river — so the same yard often has a bone-dry sand ridge and a permanently soggy back corner. Riverfront and creek-front parcels along SR-13 add bank erosion and floodplain considerations. NOTE: soil-series characterisation is regional knowledge, not read from a county soil survey in this pass — verify before publishing as a specific claim.
facts.housing_stock: THE OLDEST LARGE SUBURBAN STOCK IN THIS BATCH and the reason its page is different from every other one. 2020 census population 32,143 (up from 29,362 in 2010; roughly 37,051 estimated for 2026), 16.12 sq mi of land plus 2.37 sq mi of water, 10,755 households, 12,567 housing units. 86.8% detached single-family; ~4.6% duplex/townhome; the remainder multifamily and a small number of mobile homes. MEDIAN YEAR BUILT 2002, with 39.3% of all homes built 2000–2009 — and the anchor community, JULINGTON CREEK PLANTATION, broke ground in the LATE 1980s. So the stock spans roughly 1988–2010 with pockets of 1970s riverfront and newer infill. Other named subdivisions: Cunningham Creek Plantation, Hickory Creek, Greenbriar Plantation, Stone Creek, Worthington Park, Durbin Creek. Lots are generously sized by modern St. Johns standards — commonly 1/4 to 1/2 acre in the Plantation-era neighborhoods, with real rectangular backyards, plus larger riverfront and creek-front parcels along SR-13 (the Riverside/William Bartram Scenic Highway corridor). Homeowner vacancy 1.0%, rental vacancy 5.5% — very stable, low-turnover ownership. HOA prevalence is high but not universal; Julington Creek Plantation is CDD-governed with its own recreation district, and the older SR-13 river parcels are often unrestricted.
facts.who_lives_there: Established, settled, family-dominated. Median household income around $141,863 with a poverty rate of just 2.68%; per-capita income about $78,869. Median age 41.3–42.6. 71.6% of households are married couples. 81.6% White, 8.5% Hispanic, 3.7% Asian, 3.4% Black, 9.2% two or more races (2020). These are second- and third-owner households in 20–35 year old houses — the classic renovation-cycle customer, replacing pools, decks, screens and irrigation rather than buying new. That is a fundamentally different sales conversation from Nocatee: nobody here is choosing a lot from a builder's plat, everyone here has a specific dead patch of yard they have fought for a decade.
facts.golf: JULINGTON CREEK GOLF CLUB — public, 18 holes, par 72, at 1111 Durbin Creek Blvd, Fruit Cove 32259; remodelled in 2022 and voted Best Public Golf Course in Northeast Florida in the 2025 JAXBest awards. CIMARRONE GOLF CLUB — 2800 Cimarrone Boulevard, 32259, semi-private, just off I-95 and about ten minutes from World Golf Village, with golf-frontage homesites. Both are inside the ZIP, both have residential golf frontage, and neither is a private tour venue — which is the point: this is affordable, everyday, public-and-semi-private golf played by people who would practise at home if they could. Within a short drive: Jacksonville Golf & Country Club and the Deerwood/Baymeadows clubs to the north in Duval, St. Johns Golf & Country Club and World Golf Village (King & Bear, Slammer & Squire) to the south via CR-210.
facts.commercial_targets: JULINGTON CREEK PLANTATION recreation district — pools, tennis courts, athletic fields and playground surrounds, run as a community development district with a board and management company, so one relationship covers a very large common-area footprint. Julington Creek Golf Club and Cimarrone Golf Club (practice greens, tee-line surrounds, clubhouse landscaping). SCHOOLS: Cunningham Creek Elementary, Durbin Creek Elementary, Freedom Crossing Academy, Hickory Creek Elementary, Julington Creek Elementary, Switzerland Point Middle, Bartram Trail High School and Creekside High School all serve this CDP — playground fall zones, courtyards, pre-K play areas. Marywood Retreat Center (retreat lawns, event space, grounds maintenance budget). Churches and preschools along SR-13 and Race Track Road. Veterinary practices, doggie daycares and pet boarding along the San Jose Blvd / SR-13 corridor spilling over from Mandarin. Youth sports programs in the northwest county.
facts.landmarks: The Julington-Durbin Preserve between Julington Creek and Durbin Creek. Julington Creek itself and the Julington Creek bridge on SR-13. The William Bartram Scenic & Historic Highway (SR-13) running along the St. Johns River. Marywood Retreat Center for the Diocese of St. Augustine, on the river in Fruit Cove. Julington Creek Golf Club at 1111 Durbin Creek Blvd. Bartram Trail High School. The Julington Creek Plantation recreation complex. The St. Johns County Utility office at 1282 Fruit Cove Road South. The Mandarin line just to the north across the Duval County border — Fruit Cove is functionally the St. Johns County side of Mandarin.

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH: 'Salt, wind and sand kill lawns here. We build yards that survive a hurricane.' This is the one town in the service area where turf is not an upgrade over a lawn — it is the only thing that works. The page should open on the physical reality (deep sterile dune sand with no water-holding capacity, permanent salt aerosol, onshore wind, and a shoreline that has been eroding and renourishing since Irma took the back half off a house on South Ponte Vedra Beach Boulevard in January 2018) and then convert that into an engineering promise, because DEP Rule 62-308.100 literally requires it: turf anchored at every edge and seam, rated to withstand wind and flooding, installed landward of the dune and never replacing dune vegetation, permeable, and held 10 feet back from the Intracoastal or Guana shoreline. Nobody selling at $7/sq ft is engineering to a wind-and-flood standard, and this is the town where saying so is checkable rather than marketing. Second, distinct hook: ABSENTEE AND RENTAL OWNERSHIP. A large share of this strip is second homes and vacation rentals whose owners are paying a landscaper to keep a lawn alive that they never look at — a zero-irrigation, zero-mow courtyard, dog run or rooftop-deck green is a direct operating-cost argument to an out-of-state owner and to the rental-management companies, which is an argument that means nothing in Nocatee or Fruit Cove. Third, note honestly on the page that South Ponte Vedra has no golf course of its own — which is exactly why the private green sells. Do NOT reuse the Ponte Vedra Beach / Sawgrass 'PGA TOUR money' lead here; this is a windswept two-lane beach road next to a nature reserve, not a country club, and locals know the difference.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: The state rules matter here more than the HOA rules, and one clause is almost purpose-written for this town. DEP RULE 62-308.100 (effective 19 MAY 2026) under FS 125.572 (HB 683, signed 16 June 2025) sets minimum statewide standards for synthetic turf on single-family lots of 1 acre or less and stops local governments regulating inconsistently with them. The provisions that govern a South Ponte Vedra job: turf must be ANCHORED AT ALL EDGES AND SEAMS AND MUST AT MINIMUM WITHSTAND THE EFFECTS OF WIND OR FLOODING (written for exactly this exposure); it must be permeable and free of intentionally added PFAS and heavy metals; it must not increase stormwater runoff or harm adjacent properties or natural systems; NO in-ground irrigation of turf areas; not in a swale, ditch, stormwater pond or littoral zone; NO CLOSER THAN 10 FEET from a natural or man-made waterbody measured from the ordinary or mean high water line (this governs every Intracoastal- and Guana-side lot); and not inside a tree drip line without a certified arborist's sign-off. Separately, industry summaries of the law state turf must be installed LANDWARD OF ANY DUNE SYSTEM AND CANNOT REPLACE EXISTING DUNE VEGETATION — verify the exact rule text before publishing that sentence, but it is the operative constraint on oceanfront jobs. Layer on top: Florida DEP's Coastal Construction Control Line permitting applies to work seaward of the CCCL along this coast, and St. Johns County coastal/dune protection provisions apply — a page here should tell the reader you check CCCL status before quoting. HOA side: FS 720.3045 protects turf not visible from frontage, an adjacent parcel, common area or community golf course; in the gated enclaves (Turtle Shores, Serenata) the association still governs anything street-visible. Note that Serenata's oceanfront flats are condominium, not HOA — different statute, different approval route.
facts.water_and_rules: Provider must be confirmed by address: St. Johns County lists only three water providers county-wide (St. Johns County Utility, JEA, City of St. Augustine) and publishes no service-area map, directing residents to 904-209-2700. Along the South Ponte Vedra/Vilano strip expect St. Johns County Utility on much of it, with older isolated parcels on PRIVATE WELLS — and private wells are explicitly covered by the drought order, so 'I'm on a well' is not an escape. As of the check date the whole county is under the SJRWMD/St. Johns County PHASE III EXTREME WATER SHORTAGE declared 11 May 2026: irrigation ONE DAY PER WEEK, none between 8am and 6pm, applying to utility water, private wells and pumps, and ground or surface water. New sod installation is restricted under the same order. Normal SJRWMD schedule when the order lifts: DST — odd Wed/Sat, even Thu/Sun; EST — one day each; max 3/4 inch and one hour per zone. Reclaimed water is exempt but reclaimed distribution on this strip is limited. No artificial-turf rebate found from any northeast Florida utility or from SJRWMD in this pass — do not claim one.
facts.soil_and_yard: This is the single hardest growing environment in the whole four-county service area and the page should say so plainly. Deep, sterile, fast-draining relict-dune and beach sand with almost no organic matter and negligible water-holding capacity; constant salt aerosol off the Atlantic that scorches St. Augustinegrass and most ornamentals; persistent onshore wind; and, on the west side of A1A, an abrupt transition to salt-marsh muck and a water table at or near the surface. Grades are extreme by Florida standards — houses sit on or behind primary dunes with steep sand slopes that erode in every storm. EROSION IS THE DEFINING LOCAL FACT: a beachfront house on South Ponte Vedra Beach Boulevard partially collapsed in January 2018 when erosion from Hurricane Irma washed the dune out from under it, and this stretch has been in and out of renourishment ever since. Any turf work here is a dune-adjacent, wind-loaded, salt-exposed engineering job, not a landscaping job. NOTE: dune/marsh soil description is regional characterisation, not read from a county soil survey in this pass.
facts.housing_stock: HONEST CAVEAT FIRST: South Ponte Vedra Beach is NOT a census place. There is no CDP, no city, no ACS table for it. Everything below comes from real-estate market data and county/reserve sources, and the town page should be written from physical description and named subdivisions rather than from statistics. Physically it is a narrow ribbon of development along roughly 10 miles of two-lane A1A between Ponte Vedra Beach and Vilano Beach, with the Atlantic on one side and the Guana River / Intracoastal on the other. Stock is a genuine mix rather than one era: 1960s–80s beach cottages and stilt houses, 1990s–2010s custom oceanfront rebuilds, and a handful of gated enclaves. Named subdivisions include Turtle Shores (~300 residences, gated, with a pedestrian TUNNEL UNDER A1A to an oceanfront pavilion, community pool and clubhouse, low HOA), Serenata Beach (88 gated Mediterranean-style oceanfront flats built 2000–2002, house-sized at 2,180–4,760 sq ft, elevator, garage, private pool), Ponte Vedra Shores, Marsh View at Ponte Vedra Shores, Seaside Vista, Kingston Dunes, South Beach, Tides Edge, Seacrest of Vilano and Villages of Vilano. Typical single-family listings exceed 3,000 sq ft; market range roughly $595K–$4M, average around $1.8M at roughly $692/sq ft. Lots are DEEP AND NARROW, oriented perpendicular to the beach; the usable outdoor space is usually a dune-side deck, a small courtyard, or a west-side marsh-view yard — not a conventional rectangular backyard. New construction is scarce because the Guana Tolomato Matanzas Reserve locks up most of the land behind it. HOA prevalence is patchy: gated enclaves have them, the strung-out A1A lots often do not — meaningfully different from every other place in this batch.
facts.who_lives_there: No reliable census profile exists for the strip, so avoid quoting income figures. Behaviourally it is second-home owners, short-term-rental investors, retirees who traded a Ponte Vedra golf lot for an ocean view, and a smaller set of full-time locals in the older cottages. Purchase driver is the view and the beach access, not schools or amenities. A large share of properties are not owner-occupied year-round, which matters commercially: an absentee owner will pay a premium for a yard that requires zero maintenance visits and cannot be killed by a missed irrigation cycle. Rental-management companies and vacation-rental owners are a real and distinct buyer segment here that does not exist in Nocatee or Fruit Cove.
facts.golf: BE HONEST — THIS IS NOT A GOLF TOWN, AND THAT IS PART OF THE POSITIONING. There is no course inside South Ponte Vedra Beach. TPC Sawgrass sits roughly five miles north. Other courses within a short drive: Ponte Vedra Inn & Club (Ocean and Lagoon Courses) and Marsh Landing Country Club to the north; Marsh Creek Country Club and The Palencia Club across/along the Intracoastal to the south and west; Palm Valley Golf Club (9-hole executive) inland. Residents who golf drive to it. That is precisely why a private backyard or rooftop-deck putting green sells here — it is the only golf on the property.
facts.commercial_targets: Serenata Beach Club (oceanfront pool deck, dining terrace, fitness lawn — salt- and wind-exposed and expensive to keep green). Turtle Shores clubhouse, pool surround and the pavilion at the top of the beach tunnel. Serenata condominium common areas and courtyards. The GTM Research Reserve Environmental Education Center. VACATION-RENTAL AND PROPERTY-MANAGEMENT COMPANIES operating the A1A rental inventory — a genuinely distinct segment here: zero-maintenance courtyards and dog-relief areas for houses whose owners live out of state. Vilano Beach Town Center businesses and the Vilano restaurant/marina cluster to the south. Boutique inns and short-term-rental compounds along A1A. Note: there are no schools, sports complexes or daycares physically on the strip — those are in Ponte Vedra Beach or St. Augustine. Say that rather than inventing them.
facts.landmarks: The Guana Tolomato Matanzas National Estuarine Research Reserve and the GTM Environmental Education Center. The Guana Dam and the Guana River impoundment. The Reserve's ~16 miles of trails. Six Mile Landing public boat ramp on the Intracoastal. Serenata Beach Club. The A1A Scenic & Historic Coastal Byway itself — two lanes, ocean on the left, marsh on the right. The oceanfront pedestrian tunnel under A1A at Turtle Shores. Mickler's Landing to the north and Vilano Beach Town Center and the Usina (Vilano) Bridge to the south. The eroded, sandbagged, repeatedly renourished dune line that everyone who lives here talks about.

name: Doctors Inlet

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH: the rural CR 220 corridor — well water, acreage, no HOA. This is the ONLY place in the batch where the buyer probably owns real land, irrigates from a private well, and answers to nobody's architectural review board. The hook nobody else in this market is using: the SJRWMD Phase III order (Order 2026-017, active as of 7 Sept 2026) applies to ALL water sources INCLUDING PRIVATE WELLS AND PUMPS, one day a week, and almost every well owner on this road believes it doesn't apply to them. Open the page there. Second beat: NO HOA APPROVAL TO CHASE — say it plainly, because the Oakleaf page five miles north will be all about architectural review, and the contrast is the whole point. Third beat, the technical credibility move: Doctors Inlet is not uniform sand. USDA maps Ocilla loamy fine sand at CR 220/CR 224 and Meggett fine sandy loam (hydrologic group C/D) elsewhere in the corridor, alongside well-draining Ortega — so quote the base per lot, not per template. Then sell the jobs the land supports: full-yard conversions with real square footage, backyard putting greens with room for more than one hole, Doctors Lake waterfront and dock-surround turf where brackish splash kills St. Augustine, and RV/event lawn work. WHY THIS IS DIFFERENT FROM NEXT DOOR: Lakeside is shaded 1970s subdivision and strip mall; Fleming Island is gated golf money on a peninsula; Oakleaf is 600 square feet of fenced HOA yard. Doctors Inlet is the pickup-truck rural spine that runs between all three — big lots, private wells, no covenants, and soil that changes every quarter mile.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: Clay County's landscaping article (Code Ch. 18.5, Art. III) does NOT reach ordinary single-family back yards here. Sec. 18.5-51 applies the article to the landscaping of paved ground surface areas of all NONRESIDENTIAL buildings; to ALL residential buildings only within the Branan Field Corridor and the Greater Lake Asbury District; and to residential buildings with contiguous parking over 4,500 sq ft elsewhere. Doctors Inlet sits east of Little Black Creek (so outside the Branan Field Corridor as defined at Sec. 18.5-52(22)) and north of Black Creek (so outside the Greater Lake Asbury District as defined at Sec. 18.5-52(24)) — verify each parcel against the metes-and-bounds, but the corridor as a whole is outside both overlays. Consequence: Sec. 18.5-53(4)(h) ('Synthetic lawns: Synthetic or artificial turf shall not be used in lieu of plant requirements in this section') bites only on nonresidential paved-area landscaping here. HOA prevalence is the LOWEST of the five places — much of this corridor is pre-HOA rural plat and unplatted acreage. That is a selling point: no architectural review board to satisfy. Statewide backdrop: Fla. Stat. 373.185 and 720.3075(4) bar HOAs and deed restrictions from prohibiting Florida-Friendly Landscaping and from imposing requirements that conflict with Chapter 373 water conservation law or a water shortage order — but be honest, artificial turf is NOT one of the UF/IFAS Florida-Friendly nine principles, so those statutes do not shield synthetic turf. Do not overclaim this on the page.
facts.water_and_rules: Clay County Utility Authority (CCUA), HQ 3176 Old Jennings Rd, Middleburg, (904) 272-5999 — plus a significant number of PRIVATE WELLS on the rural western end. As of the 2026-09-07 check, CCUA's site carries the banner 'Phase III Water Shortage Restrictions Now in Effect.' The St. Johns River Water Management District has Phase III Extreme Water Shortage Order 2026-017 active across Clay, Duval, Nassau, St. Johns, Putnam, Flagler, Baker, Bradford, Alachua, Marion, Lake and Orange counties. Under Phase III, landscape irrigation is limited to ONE DAY PER WEEK: odd-numbered or no address = Saturday, even = Sunday, nonresidential = Tuesday; never between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m.; maximum three-quarters inch per zone and one hour per zone. THE KEY LOCAL POINT: the order applies to ALL water sources, INCLUDING PRIVATE WELLS AND PUMP SYSTEMS. Most well owners on CR 220 assume restrictions don't touch them. They do. Clay County's own code mirrors the normal schedule at Sec. 18.5-73 and sets penalties at Sec. 18.5-79 — a category 2 civil infraction for a first violation, category 10 for second and subsequent, up to $500 if contested and lost, each day a separate offense, and no more than ONE written warning. CCUA's conservation page promotes reclaimed water and Florida-Friendly Landscaping and offers no rebate program; artificial turf is not mentioned anywhere in CCUA materials and does not qualify for anything.
facts.soil_and_yard: USDA Soil Data Access point query at the CR 220/CR 224 area returns OCILLA LOAMY FINE SAND, 0 to 5 percent slopes — somewhat poorly drained, minimum annual water table 53 cm (~21 in), hydrologic group B/D. Note the word LOAMY: this is not the clean flatwoods sand people assume. Across the corridor bounding box the survey also returns Albany fine sand (somewhat poorly drained, WT 53 cm), Ortega fine sand (moderately well drained, WT 130 cm), MEGGETT FINE SANDY LOAM (poorly drained, hydrologic group C/D — the lowest-infiltration soil in the whole area), Sapelo fine sand (WT 7 cm), Pottsburg, Leon and Pelham, plus Maurepas muck, Pamlico muck, Santee fine sandy loam and Rutlege-Osier complex (all frequently flooded, very poorly drained) along the Doctors Lake and Swimming Pen Creek margins. Practical translation for the page: Doctors Inlet is the least uniform ground in this batch. Two lots 400 yards apart can be moderately well drained Ortega sand and poorly drained Meggett loam. Never quote this corridor off a template base spec — the base build and drainage detail have to be set lot by lot. Add: brackish water. Doctors Lake is estuarine, and shoreline lawns near the splash zone struggle with salt as well as with wet-season water table.
facts.housing_stock: HONEST WARNING: this is the thinnest place in the batch and there is no reliable statistical profile for it. Doctors Inlet is an unincorporated community, NOT a census-designated place, so there is no CDP-level median income, median home value, median year built or lot-size data. Wikipedia's entry is a stub. I verified its geography instead. Census TIGERweb point-in-polygon checks (run 2026-09-07) show the community is split: the OSM 'Doctors Inlet' place node (30.1013,-81.7773) and Doctors Inlet Elementary School (30.1025,-81.7799) fall INSIDE Lakeside CDP, while the CR 220 / CR 224 area further west (30.0985,-81.8095) and the west end of Doctors Inlet Road (30.0917,-81.8435) fall outside EVERY census place — pure unincorporated Clay County. Character from mapped features and road geometry rather than statistics: a linear corridor strung along Doctors Inlet Road (CR 220) running roughly 10 miles east-west at latitude 30.10, made of older non-subdivision rural residential, small pre-HOA plats, a dense band of small churches, brackish waterfront lots on Doctors Lake and Swimming Pen Creek to the east, and newer build spilling in from Fleming Island (east) and Oakleaf (north). Expect a very wide range: half-acre to multi-acre lots, big back yards, mostly no HOA, mixed 1960s-1990s stock with scattered new construction. Mail almost never says 'Doctors Inlet' — the 32030 ZIP is small and most addresses go out as Orange Park 32073, Fleming Island 32003, Middleburg 32068 or Green Cove Springs 32043. Build the page to catch 'Doctors Inlet' plus 'CR 220' plus 'Doctors Lake' searches rather than a ZIP.
facts.who_lives_there: No CDP-level data exists — do not fabricate a number. Positionally the corridor runs between Fleming Island CDP (2026 est. median household income $116,611, median age 47.7, poverty 5.65%) on the east and Middleburg CDP ($74,634, median age 44.7, poverty 7.99%) on the west, and the Doctors Inlet corridor genuinely spans both worlds — waterfront Doctors Lake money at the US 17 end, working rural Clay at the CR 224 end. Households here are more likely than anywhere else in this batch to be on a private well and septic, to own their acreage outright, and to have no HOA.
facts.golf: No golf course inside Doctors Inlet itself. Nearest and most relevant: EAGLE HARBOR GOLF CLUB, 2217 Eagle Harbor Parkway, Fleming Island FL 32003 — 18-hole semi-private championship course designed by Clyde B. Johnston, described by the club as 'set amidst a forest of 60-foot pines'; confirmed by TIGERweb to sit in Fleming Island CDP, about 4 miles east down CR 220 (verified in OSM at 30.1107,-81.7278). Also THE GOLF CLUB AT FLEMING ISLAND on Town Center Boulevard (OSM 30.0701,-81.7162), further south. Eagle Landing at Oakleaf Plantation (Clyde Johnston) is about 6 miles north. So: no course in town, but the corridor sits between three of them — the local play is private backyard putting greens for people who drive to golf, not golf-course-frontage work.
facts.commercial_targets: Doctors Inlet Elementary School (30.1025,-81.7799). Swimming Pen Creek Elementary, Coppergate Elementary, Tynes Elementary and Rideout Elementary — all confirmed by TIGERweb to be in unincorporated Clay outside any CDP, i.e. genuinely in the Doctors Inlet/Middleburg-east fringe. Saint Luke's Catholic Church and SAINT LUKE CHILD CARE CENTER (30.114,-81.816) — a daycare play-surface target. The Salvation Army facility on Doctors Inlet Road. Whitey's Fish Camp's RV park and event lawn. Four miles east, the EAGLE HARBOR SOCCER COMPLEX on Lakeshore Drive, Fleming Island — OSM maps 17+ named pitches there (Fields 1-17 plus 'The Marshmallow'), the largest field cluster anywhere near this corridor. Plantation Sports Complex, Fleming Island. Faith Evangelical Free, Fellowship Bible and Doctors Inlet Church of God (church grounds and preschool yards).
facts.landmarks: WHITEY'S FISH CAMP — 2032 County Road 220 (Doctors Inlet Road), the restaurant/fish camp/RV park that has been 'a North Florida staple since 1963'; TIGERweb places the parcel just inside Fleming Island CDP at the corridor's east end, so describe it as 'at the Doctors Inlet end of CR 220' rather than 'in Doctors Inlet.' Doctors Inlet Elementary School. The US 17 bridge over Doctors Inlet, the channel that links 13-square-mile brackish Doctors Lake to the St. Johns River. Salsas of 220 and the CR 220 Waffle House. Doctors Inlet Church of God. Doctors Inlet Substation #16 (115 kV). Doctors Lake Marina. The old hamlet names a long-timer will recognise: Peoria Siding (30.1089,-81.7695), Neilhurst, Rattlesnake Bend, Rideout. Faith Wesleyan, Pinewood, Fellowship Bible and Peoria Church strung along the road.
