facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH: "A Donald Ross course laid this neighborhood out in 1925. Build a green worthy of it." San Jose is the only place in this batch where championship golf architecture is INSIDE the neighborhood rather than adjacent to it — Ross designed the course, John Nolen planned the streets, Marsh & Saxelbye drew the buildings, and only 21 of the original Mediterranean Revival houses survive. That pedigree, plus contoured and generously sized lots, plus a $48,195 per-capita income, makes San Jose the highest-value residential putting-green page in the batch and the clearest place to charge $10–12/sq ft: 600–1,200 sq ft multi-break greens with real undulation, because the ground here actually has fall, unlike flat Mandarin. Two supporting angles nobody else will run. First, the Phase III order limits GOLF COURSE FAIRWAY irrigation to one day a week — if the Ross course is rationed, so is the member's lawn. Second, and commercially sharpest: Bolles converted Hodges Field to artificial turf in 2016, putting it in the replacement window now, and 19.2% of 32217 moved house in the past year — the highest churn in the batch, a constant supply of new owners staring at an inherited dead lawn with a renovation budget open. Completely different from Beauclerc immediately south (young families, ranch houses, pet and play turf) and from San Marco north (preservation review and riverfront drainage).
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: Duval consolidated — Jacksonville's single code, no separate municipal layer. I could NOT reach Municode (403) to confirm any express artificial-turf provision in Chapter 656 Part 12 landscape regulations; do not make a code claim without verifying. Two real association layers exist here and should be named: Epping Forest (gated, 90 homes and 80 condos, on a National Register property, developed by Gate Petroleum from 1984) will have architectural review, and Villages of San Jose (1980s, built on the old Beauclerc Country Club land) is an association community. For any HOA-governed lot the useful statutory point is that Florida Statute 373.185 stops local governments and deed restrictions from banning "Florida-friendly landscaping" — but the statutory definition is framed around plant selection, efficient watering, mulching, wildlife and stormwater, and does NOT name synthetic turf, so it does NOT give an owner a right to install artificial turf over a covenant. Advise ARB submittal and offer to prepare the submittal package — a service differentiator worth putting on the page. Jacksonville tree protection applies given the canopy.
facts.water_and_rules: Provider: JEA. Regulator: SJRWMD. Standard: two days/week under Daylight Saving Time, ONE day/week under Eastern Standard Time; odd or no address = Wednesday/Saturday, even = Thursday/Sunday, non-residential = Tuesday/Friday; not 10 a.m.–4 p.m. AS OF 2026-09-07 A PHASE III EXTREME WATER SHORTAGE ORDER IS ACTIVE over parts of Duval and ten other counties: ONE day per week (odd = Saturday, even = Sunday, non-residential = Tuesday), NO irrigation 8 a.m.–6 p.m., three-quarters of an inch and one hour per zone maximum, and — the detail that lands hardest on this specific page — GOLF COURSE FAIRWAY IRRIGATION IS ALSO LIMITED TO ONE DAY PER WEEK. That is a legitimate, verifiable line: if the Ross course down the road is on a one-day allowance, the member's home lawn is not winning either. Exemptions: micro-irrigation and hand-held hose anytime; new landscape 30 days unrestricted then 30 days every-other-day. No artificial-turf rebate is documented; JEA's own conservation pages are CAPTCHA-blocked and unverified — make no rebate claim without calling JEA.
facts.soil_and_yard: Sandy marine-sediment soils on the St. Johns east-bank terrace, with the same condition that runs south into Mandarin: somewhat poorly drained fine sand over a seasonal high water table. Yard character is set by three things. (1) MATURE CANOPY — the cape's documented planting palette is oak, pine and traditional southern, and by 2026 the 1920s–1950s trees are enormous; live oak shade and root competition kill St. Augustine under them. (2) THE RIVER GRADE — San Jose runs down to the St. Johns and to Goodby's Creek/Goodby's Lake on its south side, so lower lots stay wet and the base spec must handle it. (3) SLOPE — unlike flat Mandarin, the cape has contour: Point La Vista is described as a contoured cul-de-sac, and San Jose Boulevard is a two-mile curved half-loop parallel to the river. Contoured lots mean sheet-flow management and, on the golf side, real green-contouring opportunity — you can build genuine break into a green here because the ground already has fall. Installation implication: this is the page to talk about shaping, undulation and a drainage layer under the green, not just flat carpet.
facts.housing_stock: A genuinely historic planned suburb on the St. Johns east bank, 4.5 miles from downtown, bounded by University Boulevard north, San Clerc Road south, and the railroad tracks west of U.S. 1 east. Conceived in 1914 by Cadillac dealer Claude Nolan, chartered as San Jose Estates on 25 January 1925 to Charles W. Strickland, master-planned by landscape architect JOHN NOLEN, with the golf course by DONALD ROSS and buildings by Marsh & Saxelbye in Mediterranean Revival — planned for a golf course, two hotels, a country club, a riverbank esplanade, a yacht club, a school, a church, parks, retail and nearly 2,000 homes. Sales hit $732,000 in the first week; Phase I sold out in early August 1925. Then the 1926 Miami hurricane and the Depression killed it — the San Jose Hotel closed for good in 1928. AS OF 2025 ONLY 21 ORIGINAL MEDITERRANEAN REVIVAL SAN JOSE ESTATES RESIDENCES SURVIVE — a specific, checkable, extraordinary number. Everything else filled in over the following seventy years, which is why the housing runs from "million-dollar waterfront mansions to small wood-frame starters." Adjacent cape subdivisions date the infill: San Jose Lane (1945), San Jose Terrace/Landover Drive (1950), Worth Drive (1950), Old Grove Manor (1954), Heaven Trees (1961), Point La Vista (1965), Philips Manor (1973), Edenwold (1984). Lot sizes span the widest range in this batch — quarter-acre 1950s ranch parcels with 50x60 backyards up to riverfront estate lots with an acre of lawn. Sidewalks were paved throughout from the start, unusual for the era. HOA prevalence is mixed: original plats unassociated, Epping Forest and Villages of San Jose gated/associated. CHECK DATE 2026-09-07.
facts.who_lives_there: ZIP 32217 (ACS 2024 5-yr): 20,221 people across just 5.4 sq mi (3,760/sq mi — densest of the five), median household income $73,832, per-capita $48,195 (~10% above region and nation), median home value $325,100, median age 37.7, 41.3% bachelor's or higher, 14.6% foreign-born, 11.2% poverty, 21.8-minute commute, ~9,453 housing units. One number matters commercially more than the rest: 19.2% MOVED WITHIN THE PAST YEAR — the highest turnover in this batch by a wide margin. New owners are the artificial-turf buyer: they arrive, look at an inherited dead lawn, and have a renovation budget open. That justifies a page built around "just moved in" timing. The ZIP median masks a barbell — Epping Forest and riverfront San Jose carry seven-figure houses while the eastern edge holds modest wood-frame stock. Segment accordingly: estate putting greens on one side, whole-backyard ranch conversions on the other.
facts.golf: THIS IS THE GOLF PAGE. San Jose Country Club is the only original San Jose Estates commercial building still doing the job it was built for, and its course was laid out by DONALD ROSS as part of the 1925 plan — a genuine, nameable, championship-pedigree architect inside the neighborhood boundary. Epping Forest Yacht & Country Club sits on Alfred I. duPont's 58-acre Christopher Point estate off San Jose Boulevard: a 15,000 sq ft, 25-room Harold Saxelbye Mediterranean Revival mansion on the National Register since 1973 that hosted presidents, Vanderbilts and Carnegies, now the club at the centre of 90 gated homes and 80 condominiums. The Beauclerc Country Club, founded mid-1950s just south, is defunct. Deerwood Country Club and Jacksonville Golf & Country Club lie east; Timuquana Country Club across the river. San Jose is where the batch's true putting-green money is: members of a Donald Ross club, living within a mile of it, on lots big enough for a 600–1,200 sq ft multi-break green with fringe and chipping approach — the $10–12/sq ft work the business is trying to win.
facts.commercial_targets: THE BOLLES SCHOOL, 7400 San Jose Boulevard — 84-acre San Jose upper-school campus, ~1,742 students across four campuses (San Jose upper, Bartram middle, Whitehurst and Ponte Vedra lower), 12:1 ratio. Critically: GEORGE H. HODGES FIELD WAS CONVERTED TO ARTIFICIAL TURF IN 2016. Synthetic fields run an 8–12 year service life, putting that field squarely in its replacement window now — the single most actionable named commercial lead in the batch, on a campus that also carries two pools (one Olympic), practice areas and extensive grounds. THE JEWISH COMMUNITY ALLIANCE, 8505 San Jose Boulevard, 32217 — built where the Beauclerc Country Club's clubhouse and pool once stood, running a preschool and kindergarten, playgrounds, tennis and pickleball, sports fields, aquatics, the Baptist Health Wellness Center, theatre and gallery; preschool play surfaces and field areas are a direct fit (verify field naming with JCA before publishing — my fetch may have conflated a field name with Bolles's). Epping Forest Yacht & Country Club common areas, pool deck and gated-community shared landscape. Villages of San Jose HOA common areas. San Jose Country Club practice, chipping and putting surfaces. San Jose Elementary School and San Jose Elementary School Park. San Jose Episcopal Church campus.
facts.landmarks: San Jose Country Club and its 1925 clubhouse — the only original San Jose Estates commercial building still in its intended use. The Bolles School's Bolles Hall, which IS the former San Jose Hotel (opened New Year's Day 1926 with 100 guest rooms plus 125 more in secondary structures, closed 1928, reopened as a school in 1933). Epping Forest, the duPont mansion at Christopher Point, on the National Register since 1973 and honoured by AIA Florida in 2012, with its formal English gardens and lion's-head fountain. San Jose Episcopal Church. San Jose Boulevard's curved half-loop. San Clerc Road, the southern boundary. San Jose Acre Park. The 21 surviving Mediterranean Revival originals — neighbourhood trivia locals will recognise and share.

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH: the ball park and the small-town yard — Callahan as the commercial and youth-sports page, not a residential luxury page. Everything else in this batch is unincorporated and residential; Callahan is a 115-year-old incorporated town of 1.81 square miles with its own water utility, its own permit desk (Chapter 195, admin2@townofcallahan-fl.gov), four A-rated schools inside the town, and the biggest ball complex in west Nassau — seven diamonds, a football stadium, two soccer fields, batting cages, currently mid-upgrade with county money. That gives the page a lead nothing next door can copy: batting-cage and bullpen turf, dugout floors, school and municipal field work, quoted by an installer who knows the town issues its own permits. The residential lead runs underneath and is equally distinct: median age 34.4, 45.9% of households with kids, small platted in-town lots at 16 feet elevation with ditch drainage and live-oak shade near the depot. That means the whole backyard is the problem area — a trampoline ring, a dog track along the fence, a swing-set mud pit, and a shaded strip where St. Augustine has never held. A full 1,200-2,500 sq ft backyard install is a one-day job here and reads as a fix, not a splurge. Do NOT lead with golf: there is no course in Callahan, and the 'Callahan Golf Links' that search engines surface is in Georgia. And do not publish the $25,234 median household income floating around — it is a 2000 census figure.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: This is the one place in the batch with a municipal permit desk of its own. The Town of Callahan issues Building, Demolition, Electrical, Mechanical, Plumbing, Re-Roof and Sign permits (some taking up to 48 hours; applications to admin2@townofcallahan-fl.gov; fees under Chapter 102) and directs applicants to Chapter 195 for what is allowed within town limits. No landscaping, fence, driveway, impervious-surface or turf permit is listed on the town's permits page — but for any job that disturbs ground or changes drainage inside town limits, call the town rather than assume, and note that Callahan is small enough that the code is not fully published online. Outside town limits (most of the 32011 mailing area), Nassau County's LDC governs, including Appendix A, Article 37, § 37.05, which states that 'Synthetic or artificial trees, shrubs, groundcovers or vines are not acceptable substitutes' — a bar on counting synthetic material toward required landscaping on commercial/multi-family/subdivision plans, not a ban on residential lawns. § 37.05 also sets a residential tree minimum of one tree per 3,000 sq ft of lot area for the first quarter acre plus one per additional quarter acre, with existing canopy trees, sabal palms and pine trees counting. State overlay: F.S. 125.572 (counties) from Ch. 2025-140 / HB 683, effective July 1, 2025, preempts local prohibition of compliant synthetic turf on single-family residential parcels one acre or less once FDEP adopts standards — verify FDEP's rulemaking status before presenting this as settled.
facts.water_and_rules: Callahan runs its OWN municipal water system — the Nassau County Chamber resident guide lists 'Town of Callahan' as the water provider for Callahan, while JEA serves Yulee, Hilliard, Bryceville and portions of Callahan; confirm per address, since town limits are only 1.81 sq mi and much of the '32011' mailing area is unincorporated county on JEA or private wells. Electricity is Florida Power & Light and Okefenokee REMC. SJRWMD Phase III Extreme Water Shortage Declaration applies to Nassau County (declared May 11, 2026): landscape irrigation limited to one day per week, prohibited between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m., maximum three-quarters of an inch and one hour per zone. Odd-numbered or no street address = Saturday; even-numbered = Sunday; non-residential = Tuesday. Applies to public and private utilities, private wells and pumps, and ground or surface water. New sod and plantings get only a tapering grow-in allowance: daily for 15 days, 3 days/week for 30 days, 2 days/week for 15 days. Reclaimed water is exempt from the one-day schedule but is not distributed in Callahan. No turf rebate exists from the Town of Callahan, JEA, SJRWMD or Nassau County — state that honestly.
facts.soil_and_yard: Flat and low: town elevation is 16 feet. Soils are the same north Florida flatwoods spodosols as the rest of west Nassau — Leon fine sand and relatives: very deep, poorly to very poorly drained acid fine sand, spodic (Bh) hardpan roughly 30-50 inches below the surface, very rapid permeability at the top and slower beneath, slopes 0-2%, seasonal high water table typically 0.5-1.5 ft. Older in-town lots often drain to roadside swales and open ditches rather than to modern piped stormwater, so standing water at the low corner of the back yard after a summer downpour is a familiar Callahan complaint. Mature live oak and pine shade over the older streets near the depot means thin, root-competed St. Augustine on the shaded sides. Because in-town lots are small, the whole backyard is often the shaded, compacted, dog-worn area — which is why a complete small-yard install reads as good value here rather than as a luxury add-on.
facts.housing_stock: The only incorporated municipality in this batch — settled 1856, incorporated as a town in 1911, 1.81 square miles of land, elevation 16 feet. Wikipedia records 1,526 residents at the 2020 census (up from 1,123 in 2010) and 652 housing units with a 5.7% vacancy rate; note that other aggregators report 1,972 for 2020 and roughly 1,892 for 2026, so pick one figure, cite it, and do not mix them. Census classification is striking: 0.0% of residents live in urban areas, 100% rural, despite being an incorporated town. Housing is small-town Southern: modest single-family homes on compact platted in-town lots along and around the US 1/301 and Dixie Avenue grid, mixed with post-2000 infill and larger-lot properties on the fringes where the town boundary meets unincorporated county. Median age 34.4 and 45.9% of households with children under 18 means this is a young-family town — small backyards with swing sets, trampolines and dogs, not estate lawns. HOA prevalence inside town limits is low; newer fringe subdivisions may have them. Not historic-district protected in the Fernandina sense, but the depot core is genuinely old. Backyards in town are typically a few thousand square feet — which makes a whole-backyard install a realistic single-visit job rather than a phased estate project.
facts.who_lives_there: Young working families. Median age 34.4; 29.2% of residents under 18 and 14.0% aged 65+; 82.7% non-Hispanic white, with Black residents around 9.8% and Hispanic around 4.9%. 615-652 households, 45.9% with children under 18, and a notably high share of single-parent households (roughly 34.3% female-householder, 16.7% male-householder, 39.7% married-couple). Income is the weak spot in the public record: the most-cited Callahan median household income, $25,234 with 21.9% below the poverty line, is from the 2000 census and is badly stale — do not publish it as current. Anchor instead on Nassau County and on the adjacent CDP figures (Nassau Village-Ratliff $62,417; Bryceville area $72,792; Yulee $79,818) and describe Callahan as a modest-income, young-family town. Employment skews to Jacksonville commuting (Callahan is adjacent to Duval), the school district (Nassau County's largest employer, 1,598 staff), trucking and rail given the US 1/23/301 junction, and local trades.
facts.golf: IMPORTANT CORRECTION for the page: there is NO golf course in Callahan, Florida. Directory sites surface 'Callahan Golf Links' for this query — that course is in Waleska, GEORGIA (a D.J. DeVictor design opened 2007 on the historic Callahan family farm). Do not cite it. The nearest real golf is roughly 15-20 miles east on the SR 200 corridor and Amelia Island: The Golf Club at North Hampton (22680 N Hampton Club Way, Fernandina Beach — Arnold Palmer design, 40+ ft elevation changes, ten spring-fed lakes with coquina boulders), Amelia National Golf & Country Club, Fernandina Beach Golf Club (27-hole municipal), Amelia River Club, The Golf Club of Amelia Island, Amelia Island Club, Omni Amelia Island Resort. Golf is genuinely absent locally — which is itself the sales argument for a home practice green, but the page should not pretend Callahan is a golf town.
facts.commercial_targets: The strongest institutional cluster in west Nassau. Callahan Ball Park: seven baseball/softball fields, one football field/stadium, one multi-purpose field, two soccer fields, batting cages, concession/restroom buildings, with shade structures and bleacher upgrades under way as part of a roughly $3M county-wide parks investment and an Integrated Lightning Prediction and Warning System installed. That is real, near-term synthetic work — batting cage floors and tunnels, bullpen and mound covers, dugout floors, warning-track and sideline surrounds, and eventually a synthetic multi-purpose field. Schools, all in town and all state-graded 'A' except the high school at 'B': Callahan Elementary (K-2), Callahan Intermediate (3-5), Callahan Middle (6-8), and West Nassau County High School (933 students, grades 9-12) — school district accounts run through Nassau County School District, the county's largest employer at 1,598 people. Nassau County Public Library, Callahan branch. Town of Callahan municipal facilities. West Nassau Museum of History / Callahan Train Depot grounds at 45383 Dixie Avenue. Churches along the US 1 corridor. Given the US 1/23/301 truck junction and two CSX subdivisions, there is also a small commercial/industrial frontage market for low-maintenance median and entrance turf.
facts.landmarks: The historic 1880s-era Callahan Train Depot, which served CSX predecessor railroads until 1983 and now houses the Greater Nassau County Chamber of Commerce and the West Nassau Historical Society; the West Nassau Museum of History is inside it at 45383 Dixie Avenue, with a CSX caboose on display adjacent. The Railroad Day Festival and car show, run annually by the West Nassau Historical Society since 2006 — the 20th Railroad Day was held Saturday, March 29, 2025. The junction where US 1, US 23 and US 301 converge, and the northern terminus of State Road A1A. Two CSX railroad subdivisions. The site of the Revolutionary War Battle of Alligator Bridge. Callahan Ball Park. Nassau County Public Library, Callahan branch. West Nassau County High School. Notable natives: MLB player Howie Kendrick and NFL player Frank Murphy. David Yulee's Florida Railroad reached Callahan by 1856.

name: Bellair-Meadowbrook Terrace

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD COMMERCIAL AND MULTIFAMILY — NOT RESIDENTIAL. This is the one page in the batch that should not open with a homeowner. The numbers say so: median household income $59,388 and a 15.48% poverty rate, the worst of the five, and the only population that is falling. But inside those same 4.1 square miles sit 3,416 people per square mile, a 953,000 sq ft regional mall in active redevelopment as Orange Park Place with Sprouts, a private country club, two elementary schools and a wall of apartment communities. So write the page for PROPERTY MANAGERS AND FACILITIES DIRECTORS: apartment dog parks and courtyards, mall common-area and outparcel amenity turf, school and daycare play surfaces, country club practice greens. Give it two pieces of technical authority no competitor will have. FIRST, the code: Clay County Sec. 18.5-53(4)(h) says synthetic turf cannot be used in lieu of plant requirements, and Sec. 18-5.54 requires that screening plus internal landscaping total at least 10% of the developed area — so turf here has to be specified as amenity surface outside the required landscape calculation, and Timeless knows how to scope it that way so the submittal clears. SECOND, the ground: the soil survey classifies this CDP's core as 'Urban land' — decades of fill and compacted subgrade over Meadowbrook and Scranton sands with a water table under a foot — so the excavation IS the job here, and a bid that assumes clean sand will lose money. Close on the nonresidential Phase III line: one irrigation day a week, Tuesday only, with each day of violation a separate civil infraction. WHY DIFFERENT FROM NEXT DOOR: Lakeside next door has the live-oak shade and the pet businesses; Oakleaf has six-figure households on new small lots; Asbury Lake has acreage. Bellair-Meadowbrook Terrace has the density, the mall and the property managers — it is a B2B page dressed as a town page.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: Outside both Clay County overlay districts (east of Little Black Creek, north of Black Creek), so Sec. 18.5-51 applies the landscaping article here only to the landscaping of PAVED GROUND SURFACE AREAS OF NONRESIDENTIAL BUILDINGS and to residential buildings with contiguous parking over 4,500 sq ft. BUT THIS IS PRECISELY THE CDP WHERE THAT MATTERS MOST, because this is where the commercial parcels are. Sec. 18-5.54 requires screening plus internal landscaping totalling NOT LESS THAN 10 PERCENT of the total developed area around a paved surface, and Sec. 18.5-53(4)(h) states flatly: 'Synthetic lawns: Synthetic or artificial turf shall not be used in lieu of plant requirements in this section' (and (i) does the same for synthetic trees, shrubs, ground covers and vines). Origin Ord. No. 85-22, Sec. 3, adopted 26 Feb 1985; the Code is codified through Ord. No. 2026-12, enacted 14 April 2026 (Supplement 86). WHAT THIS MEANS COMMERCIALLY, and it is the expert line for the page: at Orange Park Mall, at an apartment community, at a Blanding Boulevard retail strip, synthetic turf CANNOT be counted toward the required parking-lot landscape area — so it must be specified as an AMENITY surface (courtyard, dog run, play area, rooftop or plaza) that sits outside the required-landscape calculation, with the plantings done separately. A contractor who knows that will not get a submittal rejected; one who does not will. Residential HOAs are common in the platted subdivisions (Loch Rane Estates and similar) and multifamily is landlord-governed. Fla. Stat. 373.185 and 720.3075(4) protect Florida-Friendly Landscaping and bar HOA rules that conflict with a water shortage order, but artificial turf is not a Florida-Friendly practice under the UF/IFAS nine principles — do not claim otherwise.
facts.water_and_rules: Clay County Utility Authority. SJRWMD Phase III Extreme Water Shortage Order 2026-017 in force at the 2026-09-07 check: irrigation ONE DAY PER WEEK — odd/no address Saturday, even Sunday, NONRESIDENTIAL TUESDAY; never 8 a.m.-6 p.m.; three-quarters inch and one hour per zone maximum; all sources including private wells. Because this CDP's opportunity is commercial, lead with the NONRESIDENTIAL line: a mall, a country club, a school or an apartment community gets ONE DAY A WEEK, Tuesday, to irrigate acres of turf. The normal schedule is codified at Clay County Code Sec. 18.5-73 (nonresidential Tuesday and Friday under Daylight Saving, Tuesday only under Eastern Standard, never 10 a.m.-4 p.m.), with Sec. 18.5-79 penalties: category 2 civil infraction first offense, category 10 second and subsequent, up to $500 if contested and lost, EACH DAY A SEPARATE OFFENSE, one written warning maximum. For a property manager running a dozen zones, that is a real compliance exposure and it is the strongest argument on the page. CCUA offers no rebate and does not mention artificial turf; it promotes reclaimed water and Florida-Friendly Landscaping. Turf qualifies for nothing.
facts.soil_and_yard: The CDP core samples as 'URBAN LAND' in the USDA soil survey — the map unit assigned when the natural profile has been so thoroughly built over that it can no longer be classified. That single fact is the technical story here. Around it the survey returns disturbed and complexed units: Urban land-Leon-Boulogne complex (poorly drained, WT 31 cm, A/D), Urban land-Mascotte-Sapelo complex, Pelham-Urban land complex (WT 15 cm, B/D), Urban land-Hurricane-Albany complex, Arents nearly level (disturbed fill), plus MEADOWBROOK SAND — a soil series that shares the neighbourhood's name — poorly drained with a minimum annual water table of 10 cm, and Scranton fine sand at 7 cm. Practical translation: expect FILL, buried construction debris, compacted subgrade, old utility trenches and a shallow water table rather than clean native sand. Excavation is slower, spoil disposal costs more, and base depth has to account for compacted fill. Price this ground differently from Oakleaf's raw sand. There is also very little live-oak canopy left across much of the built-out area, so the shade argument that works in Lakeside works less well here.
facts.housing_stock: The smallest and by far the densest of the five: 4.10 sq mi of land, 0.06 sq mi water (Census TIGERweb, GEOID 1205025, centroid 30.1795686,-81.7375544) holding roughly 14,000 people — 3,416 per square mile, about FOUR TIMES the density of Asbury Lake. 6,168 housing units at the 2020 census with a 7.0% vacancy rate. It is also the ONLY place in this batch that is SHRINKING: 15,168 at the 2020 census down to about 14,013 in 2026, roughly minus 7.6%. This is 1950s-1970s platted Orange Park suburbia — the Wikipedia article names over a dozen neighbourhoods including Bellair, Meadowbrook, Wells Ridge and Loch Rane Estates — built out along Blanding Boulevard, with Orange Park Mall (opened 2 October 1975) anchoring the commercial spine, and a large apartment/rental component layered on top (Victoria at Orange Park, Holly Cove, ARIUM Orange Park and others map inside or on the edge). Small lots, small back yards, ranch and split-level era stock, a meaningful share of it rented rather than owned. HONEST GAP: no authoritative CDP-level median year built or median home value could be retrieved (city-data, Niche, BestPlaces blocked; Census API now key-gated). Do not publish a home-value figure without verifying it. SEO note: every address here says 'Orange Park' (ZIP 32073/32065) — 'Bellair-Meadowbrook Terrace' is a census label almost nobody uses in conversation. Write the page for 'Orange Park' plus 'Orange Park Mall,' 'Blanding Boulevard,' 'Wells Road' and 'Loch Rane.'
facts.who_lives_there: The lowest-income and highest-poverty place in this batch, and it is not close. 2026 estimates: median household income $59,388 (versus $108,543 in Oakleaf and $100,949 in Asbury Lake); married-family median $85,541; per capita income $40,846; POVERTY RATE 15.48% — nearly seven times Asbury Lake's 2.2%. Median age 37.9. Sex ratio 87.8 males per 100 females. It is also the most diverse: 56.1% White, 21.4% Black, 3.1% Asian, 12.5% multiracial and 16.8% Hispanic at the 2020 census. Be realistic on the page: the $10-12/sq ft premium residential job is thin on the ground here. The money in this CDP is commercial and multifamily.
facts.golf: COUNTRY CLUB OF ORANGE PARK, Country Club Boulevard — CONFIRMED by Census TIGERweb point-in-polygon to lie INSIDE Bellair-Meadowbrook Terrace CDP (OSM 30.1747,-81.7663). This is the asset that lets the page punch above the CDP's income number: a private club and its membership sitting inside an otherwise modest-income four-square-mile CDP, which means practice-green and clubhouse-grounds work plus a member base with backyard-putting-green money that the median household figure completely hides. Beyond the CDP: Eagle Harbor Golf Club (Clyde B. Johnston, Fleming Island) about 8 miles south, Eagle Landing at Oakleaf Plantation (also Clyde Johnston) about 6 miles west.
facts.commercial_targets: ORANGE PARK MALL and the ORANGE PARK PLACE redevelopment — courtyards, common areas, kids' play zones, pet relief areas, and the Sprouts-anchored outparcels; the single largest commercial opportunity in this batch. COUNTRY CLUB OF ORANGE PARK — practice green, clubhouse surrounds, pool deck. S. BRYAN JENNINGS ELEMENTARY SCHOOL and W. E. CHERRY ELEMENTARY SCHOOL, both confirmed inside the CDP. CHARTERHOUSE PRIVATE SCHOOL OF CLAY COUNTY. ORANGE PARK JUNIOR HIGH. PETSMART on Wells Road. The apartment portfolio — Victoria at Orange Park, Holly Cove Apartments, ARIUM Orange Park and neighbours: multifamily dog parks, courtyards and leasing-office frontage are the highest-volume, fastest-repeating work available anywhere in this batch, because one property-management relationship yields many sites. Allied Veterinary Specialists on Corporate Way just north.
facts.landmarks: ORANGE PARK MALL — 953,000 square feet, opened 2 October 1975, anchored by Dillard's, JCPenney, Belk, Dick's Sporting Goods and AMC Theatres, sold to Washington Prime Group in 2014 and managed by CBRE. Wikipedia's own article notes the mall is actually located in unincorporated Bellair-Meadowbrook Terrace despite its name, and TIGERweb confirms the parcel is inside this CDP. The former Sears is being redeveloped as ORANGE PARK PLACE, a mixed-use project with Sprouts Farmers Market and other retailers. Country Club of Orange Park on Country Club Boulevard. Blanding Boulevard and Wells Road as the arterials — Wikipedia calls Blanding 'the major arterial roadway,' running north to Jacksonville and south to Lakeside. Loch Rane Estates, Wells Ridge, Bellair and Meadowbrook as the named neighbourhoods.
