facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH KIDS AND DOGS, NOT GOLF — and lead with a number nobody else has: ZIP 32257's fertility rate runs MORE THAN 1.5 TIMES the Florida and national average. Beauclerc is where the young families are, on 1950s–70s ranch lots with backyards big enough to actually use (roughly 3,000–5,600 sq ft) and a $75,780 median household income — a mortgage-and-stroller neighborhood, not a country-club one. So this is the PET AND PLAY page for the whole batch: the muddy patch by the back door, the dog-run stripe worn along the fence, the bare arc under the swing set, all caused by a seasonal high water table sitting 18–42 inches down in Mandarin-series fine sand, and none of it fixable with grass — especially not on a one-day-a-week Phase III allowance through a Florida summer. Two things make it unmistakably not-San-Jose and not-Mandarin. First, the golf is GONE: Beauclerc's country club, founded in the mid-1950s as the club that welcomed Jewish members when others would not, closed, became the Villages of San Jose in the 1980s, and its clubhouse site is now the Jewish Community Alliance — real local history that lets you say "Beauclerc lost its golf course; you can put a piece of it back in your own yard," a warm secondary offer rather than the lead. Second, HOA REVIEW IS THE ACTUAL OBSTACLE for the 1980s-and-later infill, so the page's conversion promise should be that you prepare the architectural-review submittal for them — with the honest note that Florida's Florida-friendly landscaping statute does not cover synthetic turf and will not override a covenant. Be candid on the page that Beauclerc is the quiet neighborhood between two famous ones; local readers will recognise that as true and it will build more trust than manufactured landmarks.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: Duval is consolidated — one Jacksonville code, no separate municipality. I could NOT reach Municode (403) to verify any express artificial-turf provision in the Chapter 656 landscape regulations; verify before making a code claim. The HOA layer is the operative one in Beauclerc and the most important thing on this field for this page, because the 1980s–2000s infill — Villages of San Jose above all, built on the old Beauclerc Country Club land — carries associations with architectural review, while the original 1950s–70s plats generally do not. Homeowners will ask "am I allowed?" and the honest answer is: FLORIDA STATUTE 373.185 PREVENTS LOCAL GOVERNMENTS AND DEED RESTRICTIONS FROM PROHIBITING FLORIDA-FRIENDLY LANDSCAPING, BUT THE STATUTORY DEFINITION IS BUILT AROUND PLANT SELECTION, EFFICIENT WATERING, MULCHING, WILDLIFE AND STORMWATER REDUCTION AND DOES NOT NAME SYNTHETIC TURF — so that statute does not override an HOA covenant against artificial turf. Put that on the page plainly, then offer to prepare the ARB submittal with product spec sheets, drainage detail and photographs. Doing the HOA paperwork for a young family is a genuine differentiator and it converts.
facts.water_and_rules: Provider: JEA. Regulator: SJRWMD. Standard: two irrigation days/week under Daylight Saving Time, ONE day/week under Eastern Standard Time; odd or no address = Wednesday/Saturday, even = Thursday/Sunday, non-residential = Tuesday/Friday; never 10 a.m.–4 p.m. AS OF 2026-09-07 A PHASE III EXTREME WATER SHORTAGE ORDER IS IN FORCE across parts of Duval and ten other counties: ONE day per week (odd = Saturday, even = Sunday, non-residential = Tuesday), NO irrigation 8 a.m.–6 p.m., three-quarters of an inch and one hour per zone maximum, decorative fountains prohibited, tightened new-planting rules. Exemptions: micro-irrigation and hand-held hose with shut-off nozzle anytime; new landscape 30 days unrestricted then 30 days every-other-day. Frame this for the family audience: a one-day-a-week allowance through a Florida summer, with kids and a dog on the lawn, produces a mud pit — that is the argument, not water-bill arithmetic. No artificial-turf rebate is documented anywhere I could reach and JEA's conservation pages are CAPTCHA-blocked — DO NOT claim a rebate without confirming with JEA.
facts.soil_and_yard: Beauclerc sits on the same somewhat-poorly-drained sandy marine-sediment terrace as Mandarin immediately south — the USDA MANDARIN SOIL SERIES, established 1977 with its type location in Duval County, is fine sand throughout with a SEASONAL HIGH WATER TABLE AT 18 TO 42 INCHES, present June–December or November–April. On a 1950s–70s ranch lot with a shallow foundation and mature trees that means the classic Beauclerc failure: standing water and a soft boggy low corner through the wet season, then bone-dry sand in the dry months, with nothing surviving the swing. Add Goodby's Creek/Goodby's Lake on the northern boundary and Craven Creek drainage through the area, and the low-lying lots are genuinely wet. Canopy is heavy — 60–70-year-old live oaks and pines over ranch backyards produce shade plus root competition plus needle litter. For a family page the pitch writes itself: the muddy patch by the back door, the dog-run stripe along the fence and the bare arc under the swing set are all the same problem, and grass will not fix any of them. Installation implication: deep aggregate base, perforated drain to daylight, permeable backing so wet-season water moves through rather than ponding on top.
facts.housing_stock: BE HONEST ON THE PAGE: Beauclerc is the thinnest-documented place in this batch. It has no Wikipedia entry, no historical-society write-up I could reach, and no coverage on the Jacksonville neighborhood-history sites — I checked several and found nothing. What IS verifiable: Beauclerc sits directly between San Jose and Mandarin on the St. Johns east bank, forming Mandarin's northern boundary, with San Clerc Road marking San Jose's southern edge just above it, straddling ZIPs 32217 and 32257 along the San Jose Boulevard corridor. Its development clock is set by the Beauclerc Country Club, founded in the MID-1950s, which dates the surrounding subdivision wave: predominantly 1950s–1970s single-storey CONCRETE-BLOCK-AND-STUCCO AND BRICK RANCH housing on quarter-acre-ish lots, with backyards commonly 50x60 to 70x80 (roughly 3,000–5,600 sq ft), plus later infill. The one dateable modern development is the VILLAGES OF SAN JOSE, built in the 1980s on the old country club land — an association community with common areas. Expect original 1950s–70s plats with little or no HOA, and 1980s–2000s infill subdivisions with active HOAs and architectural review. Verify lot dimensions against the Duval County Property Appraiser before publishing specifics. CHECK DATE 2026-09-07.
facts.who_lives_there: Beauclerc straddles two ZIPs and the 32257 numbers carry the story. ZIP 32257 (ACS 2024 5-yr): 42,904 people over 12.2 sq mi (3,503/sq mi), median household income $75,780, median home value $339,300, 36.6% bachelor's or higher, 19.4% FOREIGN-BORN (nearly double the Jacksonville metro's 10.3%), and — the standout figure — A FERTILITY RATE MORE THAN 1.5 TIMES THE STATE AND NATIONAL AVERAGE. That is the sharpest single datapoint available on any of these five places and it points straight at the offer: 32257 is where northeast Jacksonville's young families with small children are concentrated. ZIP 32217 on the northern side: 20,221 people, median household income $73,832, per-capita $48,195, median age 37.7, median home value $325,100, 41.3% bachelor's-plus, 19.2% moved in the past year. Combined: a young, diverse, middle-to-upper-middle family neighborhood with a mortgage and a stroller, not a country-club neighborhood — the old country club is gone. Realistic ticket: $4,500–$11,000 for a backyard play/pet conversion, with a strong case for financing messaging.
facts.golf: THE BEAUCLERC COUNTRY CLUB IS GONE — and its story is the best single piece of local colour on this page. It was founded in the mid-1950s specifically as an alternative for Jewish members excluded from other Jacksonville clubs; it eventually closed, its land became the Villages of San Jose in the 1980s, and the JEWISH COMMUNITY ALLIANCE NOW OPERATES ON THE SITE WHERE THE CLUBHOUSE AND POOL ONCE STOOD, at 8505 San Jose Boulevard, 32217. That is a real, verifiable, moving local history most turf competitors will never know, and it lets the page say honestly: "Beauclerc lost its golf course. You can put a piece of it back in your own yard." Nearest working golf: San Jose Country Club (Donald Ross) immediately north, Epping Forest Yacht & Country Club north on San Jose Blvd, Deerwood Country Club and Jacksonville Golf & Country Club east. Golf is a SECONDARY offer here — a 200–400 sq ft backyard green for a parent who still plays — not the lead.
facts.commercial_targets: THE JEWISH COMMUNITY ALLIANCE, 8505 San Jose Boulevard, 32217 — the standout target: preschool and kindergarten classrooms, playgrounds, dedicated children's spaces (ages 1–5 and 6–12 programming), tennis and pickleball courts, sports fields, aquatics with an Olympic-style pool, and the Baptist Health Wellness Center. Preschool play surfaces, shade-structure areas and field work all fit. (Confirm any field naming directly with JCA before publishing — one of my fetches may have conflated a field name with Bolles's Hodges Field.) Beauclerc Elementary School — playground and courtyard. Villages of San Jose HOA common areas, entry features and pool surrounds. Twin Lakes Academy Middle School and the 32257 elementary campuses. The 32257 fertility figure means an unusually high density of DAYCARES, PRESCHOOLS AND CHILDCARE CENTERS along the San Jose Boulevard corridor — canvass them systematically; they are small, repeatable, fast-turnaround pet-and-play jobs with a decision-maker who owns the building or leases with landlord consent. Veterinary practices, groomers and boarding/daycare kennels on San Jose Blvd. Church campuses with children's ministry playgrounds.
facts.landmarks: The Jewish Community Alliance, 8505 San Jose Boulevard, 32217 — standing where the Beauclerc Country Club clubhouse and pool once were. Villages of San Jose, the 1980s community on the old club land. Beauclerc Elementary School. San Clerc Road, the San Jose/Beauclerc dividing line and the source of the name pairing locals notice. The San Jose Boulevard corridor. Goodby's Creek and Goodby's Lake on the north side. Beauclerc Road. Craven Road. NOTE HONESTLY: Beauclerc has no signature park, no historic district, no museum and no landmark building — the page should not invent one. Its identity is quiet residential streets between two better-known neighbours, and saying so plainly will read as local knowledge rather than as a gap.

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH THE CERTIFICATE OF APPROPRIATENESS AND THE LIVE-OAK SHADE LAWN — not golf, not pets, not water bills. Fernandina Beach is the only place in this batch where a design-review board can reject your back yard. A homeowner in the 1,500-acre National Register district who wants to stop fighting a bare, root-choked, permanently shaded patch under a 200-year-old live oak has to get past the Historic District Council, and pools and hardscape already trigger site plan review to protect 'historic lot patterns and mature landscaping.' The page should say plainly: we design turf that reads as lawn from the street, we keep the historic lot pattern, we work around protected root zones without trenching, and we prepare and file the COA package. Layer the demographics on top: median age 58.6, median household income $97,903, median home value $555,400, 53% college-educated — a customer who values 'done correctly and permitted' over 'cheap', which is exactly the customer who pays $10–12/sq ft instead of $7–8. Then the water fact as the closer: SJRWMD Phase III has had Nassau County on ONE watering day a week since 11 May 2026 — Saturday for odd addresses, Sunday for even — and a normal year is still only two days in summer, one in winter. Fernandina Beach is a permitting-and-shade page. Amelia Island next door is a golf-and-club-money page. Yulee is a small-lot new-build page. They must not share a lead.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: THE defining constraint, and the thing no competitor's page explains: any work on the exterior of a structure in a Fernandina Beach historic district requires a Certificate of Appropriateness from the Historic District Council — either staff-level approval or a hearing before the full Council depending on scope. Applications are required before modifying visible facades, rooflines, windows, doors, porches, fencing or SITE FEATURES, and pools and hardscape trigger site plan review specifically to preserve historic lot patterns and mature landscaping. The HDC applies design guidelines based on the U.S. Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation. Old Town has its own guideline set, currently being rewritten with resident input. Second constraint: the Land Development Code defines impervious surface as any surface compacted or covered so it is 'highly resistant to infiltration by water,' and enforces a maximum impervious surface ratio (impervious area / lot area) by land use category. WHETHER FERNANDINA CLASSIFIES ARTIFICIAL TURF AS IMPERVIOUS IS UNVERIFIED — fbfl.us was unreachable and Municode blocked automated access on the check date (2026-09-07). Call Fernandina Beach Planning before publishing any claim on that point; it is the highest-value fact on the page and competitors likely have it wrong. State-law backdrop: Fla. Stat. §373.185 and Ch. 720 stop HOAs from imposing unreasonable bans on water-conserving landscaping, but state law does not override city or county zoning, and synthetic grass is not explicitly named as protected.
facts.water_and_rules: CRITICAL AND CURRENT: the St. Johns River Water Management District declared a Phase III Extreme Water Shortage effective 11 May 2026, covering Nassau County (with Clay, Duval, Flagler, Putnam, St. Johns and portions of Baker, Bradford, Lake, Alachua and Marion). Under Phase III, landscape irrigation is limited to ONE DAY PER WEEK, never between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m., no more than 3/4 inch and no more than one hour per zone. Residential odd-numbered or no address = Saturday; even-numbered = Sunday; non-residential = Tuesday. New plantings get 15 days daily, then 3 days/week for 30 days, then 2 days/week for 15 days. Aesthetic water use is prohibited. Even in a normal year the SJRWMD baseline is only two days a week during daylight saving time and one day a week during Eastern Standard Time, with no irrigation 10 a.m.–4 p.m. PROVIDER: the City of Fernandina Beach operates its own municipal water/sewer utility inside the city (JEA serves much of mainland Nassau) — VERIFY the exact service boundary with the city before publishing; reporting on this is inconsistent. NO artificial-turf rebate was found anywhere in this district; SJRWMD and JEA conservation incentives target irrigation-system efficiency and Florida-Friendly plantings, not synthetic grass. Do not claim a rebate on the page.
facts.soil_and_yard: Amelia Island is the southernmost Sea Island, 13 miles long and about 4 miles wide — barrier-island sand. The Nassau County 2030 Comprehensive Plan describes Amelia Island as poorly drained on its west (river/marsh) side and better-drained, higher sand elsewhere, and flags the county-wide problem as a lack of topographic relief combined with abundant poorly drained soils — which is why stormwater engineering is hard here. Practical yard conditions in the historic core: deep permanent shade from mature live oaks (the Bailey House's 'Kate's Tree' and the Lesesne House's two-century-old live oak are literally named landmarks), compacted 100-year-old fill and shell in old lots, root plates you cannot trench through, and low back corners that stay wet after summer thunderstorms. St. Augustine grass fails under that canopy — the single most common reason a Fernandina historic-district homeowner calls a turf installer.
facts.housing_stock: Two distinct products in one small city. (1) The historic core: the Fernandina Beach Historic District was listed on the National Register 20 Jul 1973 (~1,500 acres) and expanded 20 Apr 1987 (+970 acres); Wikipedia counts ~300 structures inside the boundary, the tourism bureau counts 50+ blocks and 400+ historic structures. Predominant styles are Victorian and Frame Vernacular with Queen Anne influence — plus Colonial Revival, bungalows and shotgun houses. Separately, Old Town (the original Spanish plat of 1811, the last Spanish city platted in the Western Hemisphere) is its own NRHP historic site with its own design guidelines, currently being overhauled with resident input. These are 1860s–1920s lots: narrow platted city lots, shallow-to-medium back yards, detached garages/alleys, heavy live-oak canopy. Backyards here are commonly 800–2,000 sq ft of mostly-shaded ground. (2) Outside the district: mid-century ranch through 1990s–2020s coastal infill and gated golf product on the island's west and south sides, plus condo/villa stock. ACS: 8,168 housing units, 6,464 households, median home value $555,400 — roughly 1.7x the US median. HOA prevalence is low in the historic core (city HDC review substitutes for it) and high in the golf/gated communities. A historic-district home here is the opposite of a Nocatee job: no HOA, but a city design-review board instead.
facts.who_lives_there: Population 13,052 (2020 census), ~13,420 ACS. This is the oldest and one of the wealthiest customer bases in the whole four-county service area: median age 58.6 years (about 1.5x the US figure of 38.9), median household income $97,903, per capita income $65,868, 53.4% hold a bachelor's degree or higher (~1.5x US), 12.3% are veterans (about double the US rate of 6.2%), poverty 11.3%. Average household is 2 persons. Translation: affluent empty-nesters, retirees and relocation/second-home buyers in 100-year-old houses they have restored and do not want to mow. Seasonal population swells well above the resident count.
facts.golf: On-island and immediately adjacent, all checkable by name: Fernandina Beach Golf Club — city-owned municipal, 27 holes, 2800 Bill Melton Road. Amelia River Golf Club — public, 18 holes, Tom Jackson design, 4477 Buccaneer Trail. The Golf Club at North Hampton — Arnold Palmer Signature course (Palmer/Ed Seay, built 2001, MacCurrach Golf), par 72 / 7,080 yards, TifEagle greens, 419 Bermuda fairways, ten boulder-lined lakes, elevation changes over 40 ft, open to the public, 22680 N. Hampton Club Way (Fernandina Beach mailing address, off-island in the North Hampton community). Amelia National Golf & Country Club — gated ICI Homes community of ~750 custom/semi-custom homes around a Tom Fazio course (2006), currently in its first major Fazio-firm renovation; a Lifestyle Membership (clubhouse, resort pool and spa, eight Har-Tru courts, fitness, dining) is mandatory with every home purchase. In-town novelty: Gregor MacGregor Mini Links & Drinks in historic Fernandina Beach. Resort courses (Oak Marsh, Long Point, Little Sandy, Golf Club of Amelia Island, Amelia River Club) are a short drive south — see the Amelia Island entry.
facts.commercial_targets: Fernandina Beach Golf Club (2800 Bill Melton Road) — city-owned 27 holes; practice green, short-game and nursery-green work is a municipal procurement, and a municipal reference sells every private club afterward. Amelia River Golf Club (4477 Buccaneer Trail). The Golf Club at North Hampton (22680 N. Hampton Club Way) — public-access clubhouse and practice areas. Amelia National Golf & Country Club — gated, ~750 homes, mandatory membership, active renovation cycle. Nassau County School District schools inside the city. Downtown Centre Street hospitality: bed-and-breakfasts and inns in restored Victorians with tiny courtyard side yards that never grow grass — high-margin small jobs with photo value. The historic-district event-venue segment (the Lesesne House operates as a restored venue). Vacation-rental management companies on the island (a turnover-proof, zero-irrigation lawn is an easy line item on a rental pro forma). Also veterinary and pet-boarding businesses and city/county park facilities.
facts.landmarks: Centre Street (the historic commercial spine); the Old Train Depot, now the Welcome Center; the Lesesne House (1860, Classical Revival, hand-hewn lumber and wooden pegs, the 'Crown Jewel of Centre Street', now a restored event venue); the Bailey House (1885, Queen Anne, three-story turreted bays and fish-scale shingles, architect George W. Barber, heart pine and Tiffany-style windows, corner of Ash and 7th); the Tabby House (Robert Sands Schuyler, Portland cement and oyster shell — the island's only surviving tabby structure); Fort Clinch State Park; the Amelia Island Lighthouse; Main Beach; Egans Creek Greenway; the Port of Fernandina and the shrimp docks; the Palace Saloon; the Amelia Island Museum of History; Fernandina Beach Municipal Airport. Events: the Isle of Eight Flags Shrimp Festival, first weekend in May, 150,000+ visitors; the Amelia Island Concours d'Elegance. The 'Isle of 8 Flags' name is genuine — France, Spain, Britain, Spain again, the Republic of East Florida (1812), the Republic of the Floridas (1817), Mexico, the Confederacy and the United States.

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH: deep-water acreage with nobody to ask for permission — the high-ticket private putting green page. Nassauville is the only place in this batch where all three high-margin conditions line up at once: one-acre-minimum lots (so there is physically room for a 1,500-3,000 sq ft green with fringe and multiple pins), no deed restrictions and no architectural review board, and a 15-minute drive to the Amelia Island golf cluster — North Hampton, Amelia National, Fernandina Beach GC — which means the buyer already plays and already knows what a good green rolls like. That is a genuinely different lead from every neighbour: Yulee Heights is a shaded 1970s tract subdivision, Callahan is small in-town lots, Nassau Village-Ratliff is manufactured homes and mowing fatigue, Bryceville is forest-edge acreage. The technical proof point that makes the page credible and locally specific rather than generic: this is tidal-marsh-edge ground with a spodic hardpan and a seasonal water table sometimes within a foot of the surface, plus a septic drainfield on every lot — so the page should show that you locate the drainfield, design the base for perched water rather than free drainage, and build the green so it plays true in August instead of turning into a sponge. Second angle underneath: the acre-lot well owners are NOT exempt from the SJRWMD Phase III one-day-a-week order, and new sod cannot realistically be established under the current grow-in allowance. That reframes turf from a luxury to the only thing that stays green.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: Unincorporated — Nassau County Land Development Code applies, not a city code, and there is no HOA on most parcels. The county provision to know: LDC Appendix A, Article 37, § 37.05 (Landscaping) states outright that 'Synthetic or artificial trees, shrubs, groundcovers or vines are not acceptable substitutes.' That does NOT ban a residential backyard turf lawn — it means synthetic material cannot be counted toward required landscape material on plans that trigger landscaping review (commercial, multi-family, subdivisions). Same section requires single- and two-family lots to carry at least one tree per 3,000 sq ft for the first quarter acre plus one per quarter acre thereafter, with existing canopy trees, sabal palms and pine trees counting — so on an acre lot in Nassauville the existing oaks and palms almost always satisfy it, and turf between them is fine. State overlay: Ch. 2025-140 (HB 683), effective July 1, 2025, created F.S. 125.572 — once FDEP adopts minimum synthetic turf standards, counties may not prohibit a property owner from installing compliant synthetic turf on single-family residential property one acre or less, nor regulate it inconsistently with those standards. Note the one-acre ceiling cuts oddly here, since Nassauville's minimum lot is one acre. Confirm FDEP's rule adoption status before publishing this as settled law. Also: septic and well setbacks, and any Nassau County wetland/marsh buffer, will constrain layout more than any turf rule.
facts.water_and_rules: SJRWMD Phase III Extreme Water Shortage Declaration is in force across Nassau County (declared May 11, 2026). Residential landscape irrigation is limited to ONE day per week, prohibited 8 a.m.–6 p.m., max three-quarters of an inch and one hour per zone: odd or no street number = Saturday, even = Sunday, non-residential = Tuesday. Critically for Nassauville: the restrictions expressly apply to 'water supplied by public and private utilities, private wells and pumps, and ground or surface water sources' — so the acre-lot well owners who assume they are exempt are NOT. New sod gets a grow-in allowance only (daily for 15 days, then 3 days/week for 30 days, then 2 days/week for 15 days), which makes establishing new St. Augustine sod here a genuinely losing proposition right now. Reclaimed water is excluded from the one-day schedule, but Nassauville has no reclaimed distribution — these are wells. Provider: private wells and septic on the acre lots; unincorporated Amelia Island area is served by Nassau Amelia Utilities (system sold by Nassau County to the Florida Governmental Utility Authority). No artificial turf rebate exists from SJRWMD, JEA, FGUA/NAU or Nassau County — say so plainly rather than implying one. UF/IFAS is explicit that the Florida-Friendly Landscaping program does not classify artificial turf as a Florida-Friendly product, so do not claim FFL credit.
facts.soil_and_yard: This is the most drainage-complicated site type in the batch, for a different reason than Bryceville. Nassauville is on the tidal Nassau River / salt-marsh interface: parcels typically step from a sandy ridge down to marsh, so the same yard can have fast-draining fine sand at the house and saturated, sometimes brackish, hydric soil 60 feet away. Regional soils are flatwoods spodosols — Leon fine sand and relatives: very deep, poorly to very poorly drained acid fine sand with a spodic (Bh) hardpan roughly 30-50 inches down, very rapid permeability at the surface and much slower below it, seasonal high water table commonly 0.5-1.5 ft and sometimes 0-12 inches for months. Practical consequences: (a) percolation tests at the surface lie — the hardpan perches water; (b) live oak, cabbage palm and pine shade along the river kills St. Augustine on the north side of houses, which is where turf wins; (c) every acre lot has a septic drainfield you must locate and design around — no compaction, no covering; (d) salt spray and occasional tidal overwash on the low parcels; (e) FEMA flood zones are real here, check them before base design. Base spec should assume perched water, not free drainage.
facts.housing_stock: No census place, no CDP, no ACS table — Nassauville is a named unincorporated community only, so treat all numbers as directional. What IS documented and consistent across sources: it sits on the north bank of the Nassau River near its northernmost bend (approx. 30.57N, -81.52W), strung along CR 107 / Nassauville Road, which runs roughly 5 miles south off A1A and dead-ends near Holly Point. The defining housing fact is the LOT, not the era: minimum lot size is one acre because parcels carry both a private well and a septic system. Local brokerage descriptions are blunt that stock ranges 'from single wide mobile homes to 4000 square foot mansions along the creeks and rivers' — meaning two distinct markets on the same road: legacy single-wides and 1970s-90s frame houses on interior acre lots, and custom waterfront builds on navigable deep water. Backyards are enormous by service-area standards (an acre minimum, many multi-acre, several with marsh frontage and docks), which is the opposite of every Nocatee/Wildlight lot. HOA prevalence is effectively nil — the area is explicitly marketed as offering 'freedom from deed restricted communities and room to breathe.' Buildable lots still exist but are described as scarce. Neither historic-district nor new-build: it is unregulated rural-coastal infill. Verify actual parcel sizes and flood zones on Nassau County Property Appraiser before quoting any specific job.
facts.who_lives_there: Genuinely thin — there is no ACS profile for Nassauville. Inference from surrounding geography and listing content: two buyer types. (1) Long-tenured east-Nassau families on interior acre lots, many in older frame or manufactured homes, working in Fernandina, Yulee or the Westlake/Rayonier industrial corridor. (2) In-migrating waterfront buyers who wanted Amelia Island water access without Amelia Island prices or rules — retirees, boat owners, remote workers. Nassau County as a whole ran 90,352 in 2020 with a 2025 estimate of 106,879, one of the fastest-growing counties in Florida, and Nassauville is one of the few remaining acre-lot outlets for that growth on the east side. For income anchoring, the nearest defensible figures are Yulee CDP at $79,818 median household income and Nassau County overall; do NOT publish a Nassauville-specific income figure, because no credible one exists.
facts.golf: No golf course in Nassauville. The relevant cluster is 15-20 minutes north/east on Amelia Island and the SR 200 corridor: The Golf Club at North Hampton (22680 N Hampton Club Way, Fernandina Beach — Arnold Palmer design, over 40 ft of elevation change, ten spring-fed lakes lined with coquina boulders), Amelia National Golf & Country Club (private, Fernandina Beach), Fernandina Beach Golf Club (27-hole municipal), Amelia River Club, The Golf Club of Amelia Island, the Amelia Island Club, and the Omni Amelia Island Resort courses. Nassauville is the closest un-deed-restricted acreage to that entire golf cluster — which is the whole putting-green pitch here: members at Amelia National or North Hampton who live 15 minutes away on an acre with no ARB to ask.
facts.commercial_targets: Honest assessment: Nassauville has almost no commercial base — it is a residential road ending at a boat ramp. Verified public assets: Goffinsville Nassau River Park (county, improvements underway — pavilion and picnic surrounds, playground fall zones) and Holly Point Boat Ramp Park (planned improvements). Mount Olive Missionary Baptist Church grounds. Beyond that, the realistic commercial pipeline sits 10-20 minutes away in Yulee and on Amelia Island — the Amelia golf clubs' practice areas, resort properties, and Yulee's Blackrock Cove Park and Eastside Regional Park. Do not pad this page with invented local businesses; point the commercial CTA at east Nassau generally.
facts.landmarks: Mount Olive Missionary Baptist Church, listed on the National Register of Historic Places — the community's one nationally-listed landmark. Goffinsville Nassau River Park & Boat Ramp at the end of Old Nassauville Road (public ramp, playground, picnic areas, restrooms, sweeping views across the Nassau River toward Amelia Island; puts you into the ICW at the south end of Amelia in minutes; currently receiving county facility improvements). Holly Point Boat Ramp Park, at the south end of Nassauville Road, for smaller vessels via tidal creek. CR 107 / Nassauville Road itself. The Nassau River and its northernmost bend. Roughly 15 minutes to Amelia Island beaches, 20-25 minutes to Jacksonville International Airport and River City Marketplace.

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH HOA AND CDD APPROVAL — 'WE SUBMIT YOUR BAR PACKAGE FOR YOU.' Fleming Island is where the sale is won on paperwork, not price. The money is unambiguous (median household income $116,611, median value $422,400, 85.3% homeownership, poverty 5.65%). The golf appetite is unambiguous (a Bobby Weed U.S. Open qualifying course and a Clyde Johnston TifEagle-green course both inside the community — residents know what a real green looks like, which justifies $10–12/sq ft instead of $7–8). The pain is unambiguous (CCUA enforcing one watering day a week and no irrigation 8 a.m. to 6 p.m., with pine shade and needle drop killing the preserve-backing lawns anyway). But every one of the 2,400+ Fleming Island Plantation homes needs a Board of Architectural Review application under BAR Guidelines Revision N before a single roll goes down, with fines for non-compliance, and Eagle Harbor stacks its own HOA on The Crossings CDD. Florida's 2025 turf preemption does NOT help — DEP says so explicitly. So the page's hero promise is administrative: we prepare and submit the BAR/ARC package, we show approved installs in named neighbourhoods, and we hand the board the technical proof it asks for — permeable subgrade, no alteration of the permitted stormwater system, no turf in the pond littoral zone, the 10-ft Doctors Lake/Black Creek setback, natural silica or shell infill, and no PFAS or heavy metals. Sell to the board first and the homeowner second. Then upsell the two- or three-hole bent-look putting green to someone who plays Eagle Harbor every week. Nothing else in this batch has this structure: Baldwin has no HOA at all, Orange Park is old and largely un-covenanted, Oceanway's CDDs are newer and looser, and Beach Haven is mostly condo boards.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: THIS IS THE TOWN WHERE PRIVATE RULES OUTWEIGH PUBLIC ONES. Since 19 May 2026 Clay County cannot prohibit compliant synthetic turf on a single-family lot of 1 acre or less (s. 125.572, F.S. / DEP Rule 62-308.100) — but DEP's own FAQ is explicit that the rule "does not address HOA requirements, deed restrictions or other private property agreements," and Fleming Island is wall-to-wall covenanted. Fleming Island Plantation is a deed-restricted CDD governed by recorded Covenants, Restrictions and Easements plus BAR Guidelines (Revision N); any exterior modification requires a Board of Architectural Review application before work starts, and non-compliance draws fines (managed by Inframark; community manager Jessica Rivera). Eagle Harbor sits under The Crossings at Fleming Island CDD plus its own HOA. Pace Island has its own association. On top of that, the DEP rule's hard limits bite hardest exactly here: no turf in a swale, ditch, stormwater pond or a pond's littoral zone (every CDD lot drains to one); no increase in runoff volume, direction or rate to adjacent properties and no alteration of the permitted stormwater management system; a 10-ft setback from any natural or man-made waterbody measured from ordinary/mean high water unless a seawall or bulkhead intervenes (Doctors Lake, Swimming Pen Creek, Black Creek and every retention lake); no in-ground irrigation over turf with heads removed and pipe capped; infill limited to clean silica sand, rock, shell or natural material (rubber only within a playground footprint); and no heavy metals or intentionally added PFAS in turf, backing or infill.
facts.water_and_rules: Clay County Utility Authority (CCUA), and the operational difference that matters: CCUA supplies RECLAIMED water for irrigation across Fleming Island (and Oakleaf), with a required free cross-connection inspection and an approved-irrigation-contractor list. Even with reclaimed available, CCUA is enforcing the SJRWMD Phase III Extreme Water Shortage: one irrigation day per week, no watering 8 a.m.–6 p.m., one hour per zone maximum, odd/no address Saturday, even Sunday, nonresidential Tuesday. Normal-year schedule: two days a week in Daylight Saving Time (odd Wed/Sat, even Thu/Sun, nonresidential Tue/Fri), one day in Eastern Standard Time. CCUA offers a New Sod Credit (30 days billed at Tier 2 rates with a Water Conservation Assessment) and leak/pool-fill credits — but NO artificial-turf rebate. That New Sod Credit is a useful rhetorical hook: the utility will discount your water while you try to establish sod it then restricts you from watering.
facts.soil_and_yard: Sandy pine flatwoods on a peninsula surrounded by water on all four sides. Eagle Harbor's own course description — "a forest of 60-foot pines" — and the Golf Club of Fleming Island's "mature live oaks, longleaf pines, and natural wetlands" describe the native condition accurately. Homes sit on engineered pads above a wet natural grade; the water table is close and every neighbourhood drains to a CDD retention pond. The specific turfgrass killer here is not flood but PINE: deep pine shade and continuous needle drop on the preserve-backing lots, exactly the yards whose owners paid a premium for the preserve view. Salinity is low this far up (about 2.9 ppt at the Buckman Bridge, 0.81 ppt by Green Cove Springs), so it is fresh-to-brackish, not coastal salt.
facts.housing_stock: The purest master-planned suburb in the batch, built almost entirely from the late 1990s onward on a peninsula ringed by water — the St. Johns River east, Doctors Lake north, Black Creek south and Swimming Pen Creek west (23.12 sq mi total, 15.84 sq mi land). 11,438 housing units at a 5.4% vacancy rate; 29,142 people at the 2020 census (29,766 in current ACS/DataUSA). The stock is defined by three developments: Fleming Island Plantation — roughly 1,600 acres, opened 2000, now 2,400+ homes across seventeen to eighteen sub-communities with two amenity facilities and an 18-hole Bobby Weed championship golf and country club; Eagle Harbor — roughly 3,000 acres with resort-style amenities, governed by The Crossings at Fleming Island CDD (established by rule 20 November 1989) alongside its own HOA; and gated Pace Island on Doctors Lake, which even has its own water treatment plant. Typical product: 1995–2015 one- and two-storey production and semi-custom homes on engineered fill pads, roughly 55–80 ft fronts, with a lanai and a small-to-medium fenced back yard that very often backs onto a preserve, a golf hole or a CDD stormwater pond. Median property value $422,400; homeownership 85.3% — the highest in the batch. HOA/CDD coverage is effectively total.
facts.who_lives_there: The money and the family market. Population 29,766, median household income $116,611 (Census Reporter ACS; DataUSA concurs), poverty just 5.65%, homeownership 85.3%, median age 44.7–47.7. Wikipedia notes it is one of the wealthiest ZIP codes in the Jacksonville metro. 76.6% non-Hispanic White, 11.2% Hispanic, 4.2% Asian. Largest industries: Health Care & Social Assistance (1,936), Professional/Scientific/Technical Services (1,805), Retail Trade (1,360). Average commute 30 minutes, two cars per household — these are Jacksonville professionals who chose Clay County schools. 95.8% have health coverage.
facts.golf: Two full 18-hole courses INSIDE the community — the only place in this batch where that is true. THE GOLF CLUB AT FLEMING ISLAND, Town Center Boulevard, 32003 — a Bobby Weed design opened in the late 1990s on gently rolling terrain with mature live oaks, longleaf pines and natural wetlands; ranked fifth 'Best New Affordable Golf Course in America' by Golf Digest in January 2003 and an official qualifying site for the 2003 U.S. Open. EAGLE HARBOR GOLF CLUB, 2217 Eagle Harbor Parkway, 32003 — 18 holes by Clyde B. Johnston, "set amidst a forest of 60-foot pines," rolling Bermuda fairways, multi-tiered TifEagle greens, and both grass and fine white sugar-sand bunkers, with the Talons restaurant at the clubhouse; largely a private membership drawn from the surrounding development. Adjacent: Country Club of Orange Park and NAS Jacksonville Golf Course to the north, Magnolia Point Golf & Country Club in Green Cove Springs to the south. TifEagle and multi-tier greens next door set the visual standard a homeowner here will expect from a backyard green — that is a spec-and-quality argument, not a price argument.
facts.commercial_targets: EAGLE HARBOR SOCCER COMPLEX — 29 acres at 4387 Lakeshore Drive, leased to Clay County Soccer Club and used by United Soccer Alliance as its primary location, with a dozen-plus mapped pitches. This is the single best sports-field target in the whole batch and it is inside the community. Clay County Regional Sports Complex in Middleburg (eight multipurpose lighted fields, tournament facilities) and Ronnie Van Zant Memorial Park (90 acres — soccer, softball, tennis/pickleball, basketball, disc golf) are the county-level extensions. Schools: Fleming Island High School (2233 Village Square Pkwy, ~1,862 students, Golden Eagles), Thunderbolt Elementary, Fleming Island Elementary (Lakeshore Dr), R.M. Paterson Elementary (Pine Ave), Swimming Pen Creek Elementary, Doctors Inlet Elementary, Hickory Creek Elementary, St. Johns Classical Academy, Heritage Christian Academy. Childcare: O2B Kids, Town Center Boulevard, 32003. Pet: Pet Supermarket (Blanding Blvd), Clay Humane. Golf: practice greens, short-game areas and tee-line surrounds at both Eagle Harbor Golf Club and The Golf Club at Fleming Island. And the CDDs themselves — Fleming Island Plantation's two amenity facilities (pools, basketball, volleyball, clay tennis courts, parks, playgrounds) and Eagle Harbor's swim parks, tennis and pickleball courts.
facts.landmarks: St. Margaret's Episcopal Church and Cemetery at Hibernia, 6874 Old Church Road — Carpenter Gothic, built 1875–78, financed by Margaret Fleming, added to the National Register 4 June 1973; the cemetery holds George, Lewis and Margaret Fleming and their son Francis P. Fleming, Governor of Florida 1889–1893, plus Second Seminole and Civil War veterans. Hibernia itself — the 1,000-acre Spanish land grant George Fleming received and named for Ireland, settled with Sophia Fatio in the 1790s, later the Hibernia Winter Resort. Holly Cottage (c.1897–98, National Register). Doctors Lake Marina and the Doctors Lake boat ramp. Black Creek. Fleming Island Town Center on Village Square Parkway. Eagle Harbor's Talons restaurant and swim parks. The former Naval Outlying Field (1942–1960s) that the suburb was built over. Fleming Island High School, opened 2003.

facts.strongest_angle: SHADE AND DRAINAGE — NOT WATER SAVINGS. Every artificial turf page in Florida opens with drought and water bills. That lead is nearly useless in Riverside, where many homes have no irrigation system at all. Open instead with the failure the homeowner has already paid for twice: nothing grows under a live oak, and nothing ever will. Use the Cummer Oak — 400 to 450 years old, 138 feet of canopy span — as the visual proof of what these trees do to a lawn, because every Riverside reader has one over their back fence. Then make the second lead drainage and craftsmanship: flat filled ground, century-old compacted soil, storm exposure serious enough that Memorial Park has been damaged by two named hurricanes since 2017 and the city's 2017 flooding was the worst since 1846. That demands an engineered base, real slope and a drain tie-in — work most competitors will not do and cannot price. Third lead: the Certificate of Appropriateness. Offer to navigate historic district review and to excavate without damaging a protected oak's root plate. That combination — shade, drainage, historic-district competence, tiny high-craft courtyard installs behind 1920s bungalows and in Five Points bar patios — is a completely different page from anything else in this batch. Bartram Park is small new HOA yards and dog parks; Baymeadows is golf-club credibility and 1980s condo common areas; Julington Creek is big wet acreage; Southside is commercial and corporate. Riverside is the craftsmanship page, and it is where the client proves he is a builder rather than a turf-roller — which is precisely the proof that justifies $10–12/sq ft.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: There are no HOAs — the binding constraint is HISTORIC DISTRICT REVIEW, and that is the page's biggest differentiator. Jacksonville City Council created the Historic Preservation Commission in 1990, and exterior work within the Riverside Avondale historic district requires a Certificate of Appropriateness (COA) from the City of Jacksonville. Riverside Avondale Preservation, founded 1974 and one of the largest such organisations in the country, does not approve renovations itself but publishes a Preservation Video Series walking homeowners step by step through obtaining a COA and directs them to the COJ Historic Preservation Guidelines. VERIFICATION GAP the client must close before publishing: I could not retrieve the guidelines document itself, so I cannot state definitively whether rear-yard synthetic turf triggers a COA (front-yard and street-visible work almost certainly gets more scrutiny than a fenced rear courtyard). Nor could I verify Jacksonville's tree protection code section for protected-tree root zones (jacksonville.gov and Municode both returned 403). Both must be confirmed with COJ Planning and Development and the Historic Preservation Commission — and both, once confirmed, become a paid service line: 'we handle the COA and we excavate to protect your oak.'
facts.water_and_rules: JEA water and sewer. SJRWMD irrigation rule applies: Daylight Saving Time, up to two days per week — odd addresses Wednesday and Saturday, even addresses Thursday and Sunday, nonresidential Tuesday and Friday — before 10 a.m. or after 4 p.m. only; reclaimed water exempt unless locally restricted. Winter EST schedule unverified (JEA's page is CAPTCHA-gated). No artificial turf rebate found. Worth noting on this page specifically: many Riverside homes have no irrigation system at all, or a partial 1980s retrofit, so the water-savings argument lands weakly here — which is exactly why the lead must be shade and drainage, not conservation. Florida Statutes 373.185(3)(b) and 720.3075 protect Florida-Friendly Landscaping but do NOT extend to artificial turf.
facts.soil_and_yard: River-terrace sand overlaid by a century of fill, construction debris and compaction — the hardest ground to build a proper base on anywhere in this batch. Root plates from enormous live oaks run through most backyards, so excavation depth is constrained and root pruning is a real risk to a protected tree. Deep shade is the defining condition: the Cummer Oak on the Cummer Museum grounds is estimated at 400 to 450 years old, 80 ft tall, with a 138-foot canopy span and a 21-foot trunk circumference — that is the scale of tree overhanging Riverside yards, and grass simply cannot grow beneath it. Drainage is the second defining condition: the neighborhood is flat, filled, poorly drained and storm-exposed. Jacksonville sits about 3 ft above sea level and takes roughly 52 inches of rain a year; the city's Hurricane Irma flooding in 2017 was of a severity not seen since 1846, and Memorial Park in Riverside has taken storm damage from both Irma (2017) and Idalia (2023). Base build and positive drainage are the whole job here.
facts.housing_stock: Checked 2026-09-07. Zips 32204 and 32205, immediately west and south of downtown on the north bank of the St. Johns. Almost all development occurred between 1901 and the late 1920s, rebuilding after the Great Fire of 1901. The Riverside Historic District was added to the National Register in 1985 and contains 2,120 historic buildings across 687 acres; Avondale followed in 1989. Riverside is bungalow country — 'largely due to Riverside's profusion of bungalow homes, Jacksonville has what is likely the largest number of such structures in the state' — with Craftsman, frame vernacular, Prairie, Colonial Revival and Tudor alongside them, while Avondale next door is more uniformly Mediterranean Revival. The American Planning Association named Riverside and Avondale among the top ten neighborhoods in the United States in 2010. Lots are narrow and deep city lots, commonly around 50 ft wide by 120–150 ft, frequently with a detached garage or rear alley. BACKYARDS ARE SMALL, enclosed, and deeply shaded — the usable turf area behind a Riverside bungalow is often 300–600 sq ft, a fraction of a Julington Creek yard. No HOAs; historic district review instead.
facts.who_lives_there: ZIP 32205 (Census Reporter / ACS): population 29,148 across 7.7 sq mi; median household income $64,789, about 80% of the metro and national figures; median home value $291,900; median age 37.9; 37.9% (±2.4) bachelor's or higher, above state and national rates; poverty 15.6% versus 12.5% nationally. ZIP 32204: population 9,151 across 2.7 sq mi; median household income $65,063 (±$15,288); median home value $375,000 (±$94,787), about 10% above the US median despite the lower income; median age 46.4; 42.4% (±7.4) bachelor's or higher; poverty 19.6%. Read honestly: Riverside is a TASTE market, not a money market — lower incomes than the Southside ZIPs, high educational attainment, high home value relative to income in 32204, an older and more established owner base in 32204 and a younger renter mix in 32205. It is also a cultural centre for Jacksonville's LGBTQ community and hosts the River City Pride parade. Adjacent Avondale and Ortega hold the real wealth: Ortega is a St. Johns River peninsula neighborhood listed by Worth magazine as the 46th wealthiest area in the country.
facts.golf: No course in Riverside, and the page should not claim one. The name to use is Timuquana Country Club, 4028 Timuquana Road in the adjacent Ortega neighborhood — founded 1921 with its charter approved in 1923, an original DONALD ROSS design later revised by Robert Trent Jones (1948), George Cobb (1957 and 1963), David W. Gordon (1968) and Bobby Weed (1996). It hosted the 2002 U.S. Senior Men's Amateur and the 2019 U.S. Women's Amateur Four-Ball, and it has hosted the PGA TOUR Champions Constellation FURYK & FRIENDS since 2021. That is the strongest golf name available on any page in this batch and it is roughly ten minutes from Five Points. Hyde Park Golf Club also sits just west in the Westside — HONEST GAP: I could not verify its details from a reliable source (the Wikipedia entry of that name is a Niagara Falls, NY club and the .com I reached is an Illinois club), so the client must verify before naming it. The realistic Riverside product is a COURTYARD-SCALE putting green: two cups, tight fringe, 200–400 sq ft, built between a 1920s garage and a live oak.
facts.commercial_targets: Five Points and King Street bars, restaurants, breweries and coffee shops with courtyards, side yards and rooftop patios — small, high-visibility, high-margin installs that photograph well and generate referral traffic; this is the best niche in Riverside and nobody is servicing it properly. The Cummer Museum's event lawn and garden-adjacent programming areas. Riverside High School and FSCJ Kent Campus grounds and athletic areas. Riverside Presbyterian Day School and other private schools in the district. The dense cluster of dog-friendly bars, breweries, groomers and pet boarding businesses — Riverside is Jacksonville's most dog-dense neighborhood by culture. Short-term rental and Airbnb-heavy blocks where absentee owners want a yard that needs zero maintenance between guests. Ascension St. Vincent's Riverside campus courtyards — NOTE: I did not verify its address or grounds, confirm before naming it.
facts.landmarks: Five Points and the King Street District — the neighborhood's two commercial hearts. Memorial Park on Riverside Avenue: 5.85 acres designed by the Olmsted Brothers with local architect Roy A. Benjamin, land acquired 1919, completed 1924 and dedicated on Christmas Day, honouring the 1,200 Floridians who died in World War I, with Charles Adrian Pillars' bronze 'Spiritualized Life' and two 48-inch bronze eagles added in 2011; listed on the National Register in 2017. The Cummer Museum of Art and Gardens on the riverfront — 1.45 acres of historic gardens comprising the English (originally Wisteria) Garden of 1910 with its 1922 wall garden and wisteria arbor, the Italian Garden designed by Ellen Biddle Shipman in 1931 with twin reflecting pools and a marble fountain, and the Olmsted Brothers garden with its neoclassical bronze Mercury — plus the 400-to-450-year-old Cummer Oak. Riverside Park. Willowbranch Park. Riverside High School. Florida State College at Jacksonville's Kent Campus. The River City Pride parade.

name: Lakeside

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH SHADE FAILURE UNDER LIVE OAKS, THEN THE PET CLUSTER. Lakeside is the mature, built-out, largely pre-HOA middle of Clay County: houses decades old, canopy grown in, and St. Augustine that has already lost the fight under it. Open the page with the homeowner who has re-sodded the same shaded patch three times — because that person exists in Lakeside far more than in new-build Oakleaf. Reinforce with two facts nobody else will have: the county's own code says solid sod belongs in swales and erosion areas (Sec. 18.5-53(4)(g)), and the county landscaping article does NOT reach a Lakeside back yard because Lakeside sits outside both the Branan Field Corridor and the Greater Lake Asbury District — so unlike Oakleaf, there is no county rule to satisfy, and unlike Oakleaf, many of these older plats have no HOA either. Then the commercial wedge that is unique to this CDP: CLAY HUMANE, POOCHIE'S PARK and POOCHIE'S GROOMING and PET SUPERMARKET are all inside Lakeside. Pet turf is the natural door-opener here, it produces visible reference installs, and it is a warmer, lower-friction sell than Oakleaf's architectural-review gauntlet or Fleming Island's country-club price point. Third: the Doctors Lake waterfront lots on the east side and the SJR State / Thrasher-Horne campus grounds. WHY DIFFERENT FROM NEXT DOOR: Bellair-Meadowbrook Terrace is denser, poorer and retail-driven; Oakleaf is new-build, HOA-governed and small-lot; Fleming Island is gated golf money. Lakeside is the old, shaded, unruly, institution-anchored middle — a college campus, a 1930s primate lab turned shopping plaza, three pet businesses and a lot of tired grass under oak trees.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: Lakeside is OUTSIDE both Clay County overlay districts — east of Little Black Creek (so outside the Branan Field Corridor, Sec. 18.5-52(22)) and north of Black Creek (so outside the Greater Lake Asbury District, Sec. 18.5-52(24)). Because Sec. 18.5-51 applies the landscaping article only to nonresidential paved-area landscaping outside those overlays (plus residential with over 4,500 sq ft of contiguous parking), the county's synthetic-turf clause at Sec. 18.5-53(4)(h) — 'Synthetic lawns: Synthetic or artificial turf shall not be used in lieu of plant requirements in this section' — DOES NOT REACH A LAKESIDE BACK YARD. That is a genuinely useful, checkable reassurance to put on the page. The real gatekeeper for residential work here is the individual subdivision HOA, and many older Lakeside plats have none. Statewide: Fla. Stat. 373.185 and 720.3075(4) prevent HOAs from banning Florida-Friendly Landscaping or imposing rules that conflict with a water shortage order — but artificial turf is not one of the UF/IFAS Florida-Friendly nine principles, so do not claim statutory protection for synthetic turf.
facts.water_and_rules: Clay County Utility Authority (CCUA). As of the 2026-09-07 check, CCUA is running 'Phase III Water Shortage Restrictions Now in Effect' under SJRWMD Phase III Extreme Water Shortage Order 2026-017: irrigation ONE DAY PER WEEK — odd or no address Saturday, even address Sunday, nonresidential Tuesday; never between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m.; maximum three-quarters inch and one hour per zone; applies to all sources including private wells. The normal (non-shortage) SJRWMD schedule is codified in Clay County Code Sec. 18.5-73 — Daylight Saving: odd Wed/Sat, even Thu/Sun, nonresidential Tue/Fri, never 10 a.m.-4 p.m.; Eastern Standard: one day only. Enforcement under Sec. 18.5-79: category 2 civil infraction for a first violation, category 10 for second and subsequent, up to $500 if contested and lost, each day a separate offense, and enforcement officials give no more than ONE written warning. CCUA offers NO landscape or irrigation rebate — its conservation page promotes reclaimed water and Florida-Friendly Landscaping only, and does not mention artificial turf. Artificial turf qualifies for nothing. Say that honestly and pivot to the arithmetic: an irrigation zone you no longer run at all.
facts.soil_and_yard: USDA Soil Data Access point query in the Lakeside core returns ORTEGA FINE SAND, 0 to 5 percent slopes — moderately well drained, minimum annual water table 130 cm (~51 inches), hydrologic group A. That is the BEST-DRAINING ground of the five places in this batch, and it matters technically in both directions: deep fast sand drains beautifully but wants proper compaction and a stable base or you get settling and seam movement. The rest of the CDP is far less forgiving: Leon fine sand (poorly drained, WT 31 cm, A/D), Sapelo fine sand (WT 7 cm, B/D), Pottsburg, Pelham, Mascotte, Boulogne, Lynn Haven, and Meggett fine sandy loam (C/D), with Pamlico muck, Maurepas muck and Rutlege-Osier complex (frequently flooded, very poorly drained) along the Doctors Lake tributaries. THE REAL YARD PROBLEM HERE IS SHADE, NOT WATER. Lakeside's housing is decades old on the old Yerkes-era and Kingsley Avenue tracts, under mature live oak canopy. St. Augustine thins and dies under that canopy, gets patchy, and gets re-sodded every few years. That is the classic turf-replacement trigger and it is more present in Lakeside than anywhere else in this batch. County code even reinforces the drainage story: Sec. 18.5-53(4)(g) requires that 'solid sod shall be used in swales or other areas subject to erosion.'
facts.housing_stock: 13.45 sq mi of land plus 2.19 sq mi of WATER (Census TIGERweb, GEOID 1238813, centroid 30.1356,-81.7674) — that water is real Doctors Lake frontage on the east side, and it is the second-largest water share of any place in this batch after Fleming Island. 12,633 housing units at the 2020 census with a low 5.9% vacancy; 51.6% married-couple households; 31.3% of households have children under 18. Population 30,943 (2010) → 31,275 (2020) → ~31,688 (2026 est): essentially flat, i.e. fully built out. This is mature, mid-century-to-1990s Clay County suburbia strung along Kingsley Avenue and Blanding Boulevard, with the Ridgewood neighbourhood on the west, Doctors Lake waterfront on the east, and the historic Yerkes/Foxwood tract in the middle. Lots are conventional suburban quarter-acre-ish with usable back yards — bigger than Oakleaf, smaller than Lake Asbury. HOA prevalence is patchy: much of Lakeside predates mandatory HOAs, so a meaningful share of these homes have no architectural review at all. HONEST GAP: I could not verify a CDP-level median year built or median home value from an authoritative source — city-data, Niche, BestPlaces and the Census API were all blocked or key-gated. Do not publish a specific 'median home value' figure without checking it. CRITICAL SEO NOTE: nobody in Lakeside says 'Lakeside.' Per Wikipedia's Orange Park article, ZIPs 32065 and 32073 carry 'Orange Park' as the city on every address in Lakeside, Bellair-Meadowbrook Terrace and Oakleaf Plantation. Optimise this page for 'Orange Park' plus the neighbourhood names (Ridgewood, Foxwood, Doctors Lake, Kingsley Avenue) as hard as for 'Lakeside.'
facts.who_lives_there: 2026 estimates: median household income $81,684; married-family median $104,696; per capita income $43,359; poverty 8.92%; median age 39.5 (21.4% under 18, 19.1% over 65 at the 2020 count). Race 2020: 71.3% White, 10.8% Black, 3.1% Asian, 10.3% two or more races, 11.6% Hispanic. Middle of the pack on money — well above Bellair-Meadowbrook Terrace ($59,388) and well below Oakleaf ($108,543) or Fleming Island ($116,611). Heavy NAS Jacksonville spillover: this is a classic Navy-adjacent bedroom community, which means a real rental/landlord segment as well as owner-occupiers, and a steady PCS turnover that cuts both ways for a capital improvement sale.
facts.golf: No course inside Lakeside CDP. The COUNTRY CLUB OF ORANGE PARK on Country Club Boulevard (OSM 30.1747,-81.7663) sits immediately on Lakeside's northern edge — TIGERweb puts the parcel inside Bellair-Meadowbrook Terrace CDP, but its membership catchment is squarely Lakeside/Orange Park. Across Doctors Lake to the southeast: EAGLE HARBOR GOLF CLUB, 2217 Eagle Harbor Parkway, Fleming Island — 18 holes, Clyde B. Johnston design, semi-private, in a 'forest of 60-foot pines.' Eagle Landing at Oakleaf Plantation (also Clyde Johnston) is about 6 miles west. So Lakeside is a golf-adjacent market rather than a golf market: sell backyard practice greens to Country Club of Orange Park and Eagle Harbor members, not fairway-frontage work.
facts.commercial_targets: All of the following were confirmed by Census TIGERweb point-in-polygon to lie inside Lakeside CDP: CLAY HUMANE, Filmore Street — the county animal shelter and clinic, the single best pet-turf flagship reference in Clay County. POOCHIE'S pet grooming AND POOCHIE'S PARK dog park, Fountain Drive — a grooming business and a dog park at the same address. PET SUPERMARKET, Blanding Boulevard. ST. JOHNS RIVER STATE COLLEGE Orange Park campus and the THRASHER-HORNE CENTER (campus grounds, entry beds, event lawn). ORANGE PARK HIGH SCHOOL, Kingsley Avenue. RIDGEVIEW HIGH SCHOOL, Madison Avenue, and RIDGEVIEW ELEMENTARY. LAKESIDE ELEMENTARY and LAKESIDE JUNIOR HIGH. MONTCLAIR ELEMENTARY. Saint Johns School, Clay Baptist Christian School, Orange Park Kindergarten and Andromeda Kindergarten and Day Care. Doctors Inlet Elementary School also falls inside Lakeside CDP. That is three pet businesses, a state college with a performing arts centre, two high schools and four daycares/private schools inside 13.45 square miles.
facts.landmarks: ST. JOHNS RIVER STATE COLLEGE ORANGE PARK CAMPUS on College Drive — the largest of SJR State's three campuses — and the THRASHER-HORNE CENTER for the performing arts on it. FOXWOOD CENTER, built on the site of the YERKES REGIONAL PRIMATE RESEARCH CENTER: founded 1930 by psychologist Robert Yerkes with Yale University and the Rockefeller Foundation on a 188-acre tract about a mile west of Orange Park, run by Emory from 1956, relocated to Atlanta in 1965 — the ORIGINAL LABORATORY BUILDINGS STILL STAND and now house the Orange Park Chamber of Commerce and The Granary organic food store. That is a landmark a local will absolutely recognise and no competitor's page will mention. Kingsley Avenue and Blanding Boulevard as the two spines. The Ridgewood neighbourhood. Doctors Lake and the Doctors Lake waterfront. Big Dawgs Family Sports Restaurant on Blanding.

https://sdmdataaccess.sc.egov.usda.gov/ (USDA Soil Data Access, survey area FL019)

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH TASTE AND DRAINAGE, IN THAT ORDER — "turf a 1925 neighborhood will accept, on a base that handles a low riverfront lot." San Marco is the only place in this batch with an active preservation society (since 1975), landmark commercial architecture, a 250-year-old celebrity oak with a 190-foot canopy, and blocks that grade down to the St. Johns. So the page must NOT lead with cost savings or with putting greens. It leads with two promises: (1) a product natural enough to sit behind a 1927 Mediterranean Revival house without reading as a sports surface, positioned in rear yards and courtyards rather than street-facing historic elevations; and (2) an ENGINEERED BASE — permeable aggregate, perforated drainage, positive fall away from a 100-year-old foundation — because the honest problem here is water, not mowing. Genuinely different from Miramar a mile south, where the same era of house sits on a plain unregulated plat with no review body and the enemy is shade alone; and completely different from San Jose, whose lead is a Donald Ross golf address. Secondary hook no competitor will use: as of the check date a Phase III order has cut irrigation to one day a week and banned decorative fountains — in the neighborhood whose emblem is a fountain.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: Duval is consolidated, so Jacksonville's single code governs and there is no separate San Marco municipality. But San Marco is the one place in this batch with a REAL non-governmental review culture: the San Marco Preservation Society has driven preservation and revitalization since 1975 and is an active voice on street-visible property. Treat it as a soft approval layer for front-yard and street-facing work even where no permit is triggered — say on the page that you keep artificial turf out of street-facing historic elevations, put it in rear and courtyard positions, and will work with an owner presenting to the Society. I could NOT reach Municode (403) to verify Jacksonville Chapter 656 Part 12 landscape provisions or any express artificial-turf clause — verify before publishing any code claim. Jessie Ball duPont Park carries a 1964 deed restriction that it be used "only for a public park" with the primary purpose of preserving the Treaty Oak — a good local illustration of how seriously this neighborhood takes trees. Jacksonville tree protection applies. HOAs are rare in historic San Marco proper; newer Southbank condo and apartment product does have associations.
facts.water_and_rules: Provider: JEA. Regulator: SJRWMD. Standard: two days/week under Daylight Saving Time, ONE day/week under Eastern Standard Time; odd or no address = Wednesday/Saturday, even = Thursday/Sunday, non-residential = Tuesday/Friday; not between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. AS OF 2026-09-07 A PHASE III EXTREME WATER SHORTAGE ORDER IS ACTIVE across parts of Duval and ten other counties: one irrigation day per week (odd = Saturday, even = Sunday, non-residential = Tuesday), NO irrigation 8 a.m.–6 p.m., maximum three-quarters of an inch and one hour per zone, DECORATIVE FOUNTAINS PROHIBITED, non-essential commercial water use suspended, street and pressure washing restricted. That fountain prohibition is a vivid San Marco detail — the Square's lion fountain is the neighborhood's own symbol. Exemptions: micro-irrigation and hand-held hose anytime. NO artificial-turf rebate is documented in SJRWMD material and JEA's conservation pages could not be retrieved (CAPTCHA) — make no rebate claim without checking with JEA directly.
facts.soil_and_yard: Two distinct yard problems; name both. (1) LOW-LYING RIVERFRONT DRAINAGE. San Marco's west edge is the St. Johns bank and the neighborhood grades down to it; the Preservation Society's own southern boundary, Greenridge Road, sits on a creek draining directly into the river. Low San Marco blocks are the classic Jacksonville standing-water yards — compacted 1920s fill over sand, poor percolation, moss and bare dirt where grass drowns. VERIFICATION NOTE: San Marco's riverfront blocks are widely reported locally to have flooded in Hurricane Irma (September 2017) with a record St. Johns crest, but I could NOT source that in this session (the Jacksonville Daily Record search returned no flooding coverage) — GET A LOCAL CITATION BEFORE PUTTING ANY FLOOD CLAIM ON THE PAGE. (2) CENTURY-OLD LIVE OAK SHADE. The identity tree is the Treaty Oak in Jessie Ball duPont Park — a southern live oak (Quercus virginiana) estimated at 250 years old, trunk over 25 ft in circumference, 70 ft tall, crown over 145 ft across shading a circle roughly 190 ft in diameter, possibly the oldest living thing in Jacksonville. That is the visual for the whole shade argument. Fourteen parks sit inside San Marco's boundaries, most under canopy. Installation implication: this is the page to talk about ENGINEERED BASE AND DRAINAGE — 4-inch permeable aggregate, perforated collection, positive fall away from a 1927 foundation — not about mowing savings.
facts.housing_stock: The core is a 1925 Telfair Stockton development laid out on 80 acres of the former Villa Alexandria estate, which "shattered local records by selling every lot within three hours." Named for Venice's Piazza San Marco and conceived in Italian Renaissance Revival, though the record is explicit that "few of the homes built there kept to the style, which was falling out of favor at the time" — so what you actually find is a DIVERSE 1920s–1930s mix: Mediterranean Revival, Tudor, Colonial Revival, Craftsman bungalows and 1930s brick, plus the 1935–1940 Colonial Manor sub-neighborhood (also Stockton, Whatley & Davin) and South Riverside. The commercial fabric is genuinely landmarked — the San Marco Building (Mediterranean Revival, 1927) and the San Marco Theatre (Art Deco, 1938). Boundaries per the San Marco Preservation Society: Interstate 95 north, Philips Highway east, Greenridge Road south, the St. Johns River west. It began as the independent city of South Jacksonville (incorporated 1907, boomed after the 1921 Acosta Bridge, annexed 1932). Lots range from tight bungalow parcels near the Square to deep riverfront estate lots on the west edge; backyards vary enormously, from 1,000 sq ft courtyards behind Square-adjacent homes to half-acre riverfront lawns. Newer high-density product exists on the edges (The Station at San Marco apartments; ongoing Southbank development). CHECK DATE 2026-09-07.
facts.who_lives_there: ZIP 32207 (ACS 2024 5-yr): ~37,000 residents over 11.4 sq mi (3,234/sq mi), median household income $65,234, per-capita $45,391, median age 40, 39.2% bachelor's or higher (well above state and national), 15.6% foreign-born, 13% poverty, 19.8-minute commute, 1,952 veterans (6.7%). The ZIP median badly understates San Marco proper — 32207 also contains lower-income Southbank and Philips Highway blocks; median home value across the ZIP is $307,200 while riverfront San Marco trades at multiples of that. The buyer is a downtown professional, a lawyer or Baptist Health physician, an architect, a preservation-minded restorer. The relevant psychographic is TASTE: this neighborhood has run a preservation society since 1975 and renovated its own fountain. They will pay for the right product and reject the wrong one on sight. This is the page where you show the highest-face-weight, most natural-looking turf you carry and talk about blade shape and thatch colour.
facts.golf: No golf course inside San Marco. Epping Forest Yacht & Country Club is the nearest club identity — Alfred I. duPont's 58-acre Christopher Point estate, a 15,000 sq ft, 25-room Harold Saxelbye Mediterranean Revival mansion on the National Register since 1973, bought by Gate Petroleum in 1984 and developed into a gated 90-home, 80-condo community — reached off San Jose Boulevard just south. San Jose Country Club (Donald Ross) is roughly 3–4 miles south. Timuquana Country Club sits across the river in Ortega. San Marco's golf sale is therefore the URBAN BACKYARD GREEN — a 150–350 sq ft green in a walled or hedged courtyard behind a 1920s house, often the only flat sunny patch on the lot, marketed as "practice at home, play at Epping Forest or San Jose." Small footprint, high $/sq ft, high design content.
facts.commercial_targets: Bishop Kenny High School, 1055 Kingman Avenue, 32207 — 55 riverfront acres, 1,308 students, William Johnston Stadium (football/track), John Baldwin Athletic Center, baseball stadium, softball field, six tennis courts, Roger Strickland Field House. The best institutional prospect in this batch's northern half. Episcopal School of Jacksonville, Munnerlyn Campus, 4455 Atlantic Boulevard, 32207 — roughly 995–1,200 students across about 56 acres, with a separate Knight Sports Campus on the Arlington River carrying lacrosse fields, USTA tennis courts, a cross-country trail, boathouse and field house. Julia Landon College Preparatory and Leadership Development School. Hendricks Avenue Elementary. San Marco Square restaurant patios and retail frontages — small, high-visibility jobs that photograph well and function as advertising. Baptist Medical Center Jacksonville on the Southbank (courtyards, healing gardens, rooftop terraces). The Southbank pipeline — The Station at San Marco apartments, the Haskell Southbank headquarters, Riverfront Plaza — amenity decks and dog runs. Fourteen public parks. Dog-friendly Square businesses feeding pet-turf work.
facts.landmarks: San Marco Square — the triangular commercial district with the renovated lion fountain, the single most recognisable address in the neighborhood. The San Marco Building (Mediterranean Revival, 1927). The San Marco Theatre (Art Deco, opened 1938) and Theatre Jacksonville. Balis Park, the pedestrian green expanded in the 2013 Square renovation. Jessie Ball duPont Park and the Treaty Oak, 7 acres on the south bank. The Southbank Riverwalk and Friendship Fountain Park. Alexandria Oaks Park (formerly FEC Park). Hendricks Avenue. The Acosta Bridge (1921) that made the neighborhood. Colonial Manor Park with its waterfowl and fountains. Underwood Jewelers on the Square (a $2.2 million renovation approved March 2026 — a live, current, checkable detail).

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH: the yard is bigger than you can still mow — low-maintenance turf for older owners on half-acre-plus lots, roughly half of them in manufactured homes. This is the demographic opposite of every coastal page the client will build, and pretending otherwise will waste his ad spend. The numbers force the lead: median age 52.9 (eighteen years older than Callahan), 80.6% owner-occupied, only about 4% of residents moved last year, 13.8% veterans, 47.9% mobile homes, median home value $253,000, 16.2% poverty. These are long-tenured, aging owners on land they have held for decades, on sandy flatwoods with a hardpan and a half-acre of sandspurs, pine straw and fire ants that they are still trying to mow in July. The page should sell defined, high-impact ZONES rather than whole-lot coverage: a clean turf pad in front of the skirting where the mower can no longer reach, a dog run beside the carport, a 400 sq ft grandkid play area, an RV-slab surround, a small chipping green for the retired golfer with no course within 30 minutes. That is a completely different proposition from Nassauville's riverfront acre-lot private green, Callahan's ball park and small-town backyards, Bryceville's forest-edge base engineering, and Yulee Heights's shade problem. STRATEGIC HONESTY FOR THE CLIENT: this is the one town in the batch where the $10-12/sq ft ambition will not land. Per capita income is $33,987 and 9.4% hold a bachelor's degree. Treat Nassau Village-Ratliff as a volume/referral page for small high-value zones and pet turf — its real asset is that almost nobody moves, so one good job on a county road compounds into neighbours for years.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: No municipality, no HOA, no CDD — this is unincorporated Nassau County and the properties are explicitly not part of planned developments. Nassau County LDC applies. The county provision worth knowing: LDC Appendix A, Article 37, § 37.05 (Landscaping) states 'Synthetic or artificial trees, shrubs, groundcovers or vines are not acceptable substitutes,' which prevents counting synthetic material toward required landscape material on plans that trigger landscaping review — commercial, multi-family, subdivision — but does not restrict a residential yard install. § 37.05's residential tree requirement (one tree per 3,000 sq ft for the first quarter acre, one per quarter acre thereafter, with existing canopy trees, sabal palms and pine trees counting) is trivially satisfied on these lots. State overlay: F.S. 125.572, created by Ch. 2025-140 / HB 683 effective July 1, 2025, bars counties from prohibiting compliant synthetic turf on single-family residential property of one acre or less once FDEP adopts standards — note that many parcels here EXCEED one acre and therefore fall outside that preemption, though nothing in the county code prohibits residential turf anyway. Confirm FDEP rulemaking status before publishing. Practical constraints on this ground are septic setbacks, well setbacks and manufactured-home installation/tie-down rules, not turf rules.
facts.water_and_rules: Mixed and address-specific: JEA serves parts of the Callahan/Bryceville corridor per the Nassau County Chamber resident guide, but at 323 people per square mile a large share of Nassau Village-Ratliff is on private wells and septic. That matters, because the SJRWMD Phase III Extreme Water Shortage Declaration in force across Nassau County since May 11, 2026 explicitly covers 'water supplied by public and private utilities, private wells and pumps, and ground or surface water sources.' Rules: one irrigation day per week, no watering 8 a.m.–6 p.m., maximum three-quarters of an inch and one hour per zone; odd or no street number = Saturday, even = Sunday, non-residential = Tuesday. New sod is allowed daily water for only 15 days, then 3 days/week for 30 days, then 2 days/week for 15 days. Reclaimed water is outside the one-day schedule but is not available here. Electricity is Florida Power & Light / Okefenokee REMC. No artificial turf rebate exists from any provider in this area — say so directly rather than hinting at one. UF/IFAS does not treat artificial turf as a Florida-Friendly product, so avoid FFL framing.
facts.soil_and_yard: Flat, sandy, low-density rural flatwoods across all 14.68 square miles. Soils are Leon fine sand and related spodosols: very deep, poorly to very poorly drained acid fine sand with a spodic (Bh) hardpan roughly 30-50 inches down, very rapid surface permeability over much slower subsurface, slopes 0-2%, seasonal high water table commonly 0.5-1.5 feet and in the wettest units 0-12 inches for extended periods. Drainage is roadside-ditch and swale, not piped. Yard realities that shape the job: manufactured homes sit on piers with skirting, so the ground plane around them is uneven, often under-drained, and prone to washing out at the skirting line; carport and RV slabs create runoff sheets; septic drainfields sit somewhere on every parcel and must be located before excavation; pine straw, sandspurs and fire ants are the constant complaints; and pine and scrub oak shade thins any turfgrass on the north sides. On half-acre-plus lots nobody attempts to irrigate the whole yard, so what actually exists is a mowed sand-and-weed mix, not a lawn.
facts.housing_stock: The defining statistic: 47.9% of occupied housing here is mobile/manufactured — more mobile homes than 98.9% of all neighbourhoods in America. This is a census-designated place with no municipal government, 14.68 square miles of land at roughly 30.5108N, -81.8088W (south of Callahan toward the Duval line, 32011 mailing address), holding 2,153 housing units at just 323 people per square mile. Owner-occupancy is 80.6% (some sources 86%), vacancy 6.3%. Lots are large and irregular: 'many homes are situated on half-acre to multi-acre lots, offering enough room for private gardens, workshops, RV parking, or even small livestock,' and the stock is explicitly not planned-development — 'properties here vary in size, layout, and style,' ranging from traditional ranch homes through manufactured houses to custom builds. Median owner-occupied home value is $253,000, roughly a quarter below the Jacksonville metro figure; mean mobile home prices ran about $209,774 in 2023. No HOA. Not new-build, not historic — this is decades of scattered rural self-development along county roads. Backyards are huge but mostly unimproved: pasture, pine, sand, RV pads and workshop aprons rather than designed outdoor rooms.
facts.who_lives_there: Older, settled, and far less affluent than the coastal service area — this is the demographic outlier of the batch and the client needs to know it before he builds a $12/sq ft page here. Population 4,737 (2020-2024 ACS; a 2025 estimate of 5,547 circulates, so cite one and stay consistent). Median age 52.9 — roughly 40% above regional and national medians, and eighteen years older than Callahan's 34.4.
