Pope Duval Park and Brandy Branch Trailhead Preserve. The town's short-lived municipal supermarket (2019–2024), opened after the last private grocer closed in 2018 — a detail every local knows.

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH THE PUTTING GREEN, AND LEAD WITH JIM FURYK. This is the one page in the batch that should not lead with water savings at all — it should lead with golf performance. Glen Kernan is the Jacksonville address where a 20-year member (Furyk) just redesigned the club's own course in 2024, where Tim Tebow and other pro athletes live, and where every home is at minimum 3,200 sq ft on a lot big enough for a genuine multi-tier practice green with real break, a chipping area and a bunker. The pitch is: the same short-game complex you use at the club, in your own backyard, at tour-realistic stimp — built on engineered contour, because Duval sand is dead flat and every roll has to be constructed. Photograph the undulation, quote green speeds, and name the course. That is a $12/sq ft conversation, not a $7 one. Second beat, and it is the practical differentiator: on a fairway lot, § 720.3045 does NOT protect you, because the statute excludes anything visible from the community golf course — so sell 'we prepare and submit your architectural review package' as part of the service. Compared with neighbours: Queen's Harbour is boats and bulkheads, Pablo Creek is Mayo physicians and shade, Deerwood is 65-year-old canopy over 1970s ranches. Glen Kernan is the only one where the buyer's motivation is their own golf game.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: City of Jacksonville consolidated code; no separate municipality. § 125.572, Fla. Stat. (HB 683 / Ch. 2025-140, effective 2025-07-01) preempts local bans on DEP-compliant synthetic turf for single-family lots of one acre or less — but note that some Glen Kernan estate lots may EXCEED one acre and fall outside that protection, and the DEP standards rule was still pending at the check date. The bigger issue here: § 720.3045, Fla. Stat. protects only turf not visible from the frontage, an adjacent parcel, an adjacent common area, or A COMMUNITY GOLF COURSE. In a community where 'most lots offer golf views', the statutory shield largely does not apply — a fairway-facing rear yard IS visible from the community golf course, so Glen Kernan's architectural review controls it. Combine that with a 24-hour guard gate and a club that just spent 2024 rebuilding its course and clubhouse, and ARB standards will be enforced tightly. HONEST GAP: the Glen Kernan ARB guidelines are not published publicly; get them from the association before quoting a fairway-lot job.
facts.water_and_rules: JEA, and under the same SJRWMD Phase III Extreme Water Shortage as all of Duval at the 2026-09-07 check: one irrigation day per week, none between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m., ¾ inch per zone and one hour per zone maximum, odd addresses Saturday / even Sunday / non-residential Tuesday. A relevant local nuance for a golf address: Jacksonville Today ran a reader question in April 2026 specifically on whether golf courses are restricted from watering during the drought — meaning the club's own maintenance water is under public scrutiny at the same moment its members are limited to one day a week at home. That is a conversation already happening inside this gate. HONEST GAP: no JEA or SJRWMD artificial-turf rebate found.
facts.soil_and_yard: Duval's Pomona-series poorly drained acidic sand with under 1.2% organic matter and a seasonally high water table; zone 9a/9b; essentially flat terrain, so any contour in a practice green has to be BUILT, not found. The community's own positioning is 'the natural beauty of Old Florida' — meaning heavy retained live oak, laurel oak and pine canopy on preserve lots, and dense shade where bentgrass-substitute putting surfaces are impossible to grow naturally but synthetic performs perfectly. Water features and lagoons through the property put a number of rear yards on a pond bank with drainage and edge-retention requirements. On golf-frontage lots, cart-path and fairway runoff crosses the property line.
facts.housing_stock: Approximately 350 custom-built estate homes on over 600 acres, developed from 1995 onward. Every residence is a minimum 3,200 sq ft, running to over 10,000 sq ft. Lots are large by Jacksonville gated-community standards, with most offering golf, water or private-preserve frontage. This is NOT production housing — it is one-off custom on generous homesites, and it is still not fully built out: The PARC Group markets remaining homesites from the high $900,000s and custom home-plus-homesite packages from $2.5 million. A townhome/villa enclave, Villini at Glen Kernan, sits inside the same footprint and gives the page a smaller-yard secondary product. HOA yes; NO CDD. 24-hour guard gate. Backyards are the important detail: on a 3,200–10,000 sq ft custom home on a golf/water/preserve lot, the rear yard is genuinely large enough for a multi-tier practice green with real undulation plus a chipping area and bunker — the job spec that carries $12/sq ft.
facts.who_lives_there: This is the professional-athlete address in Jacksonville. Community marketing and local coverage identify it as home to Tim Tebow and to current and former MLB, NFL and PGA TOUR players and coaches. Jim Furyk — 17 PGA TOUR wins — has been a Glen Kernan member for more than 20 years. Beyond the athletes: business owners and executives in the $2M+ custom-build bracket. ZIP-level income ($88,259 median for 32224) badly understates this community, because 32224 is diluted by the UNF student population on Kernan Blvd; use community pricing, not ZIP income, as the wealth signal on this page.
facts.golf: Glen Kernan Club — 18-hole championship course originally designed by ROBERT C. WALKER and built in 1999, then REIMAGINED IN 2024 under PGA TOUR veteran and long-time member JIM FURYK with his design team, in partnership with Hampton Golf. A clubhouse renovation of nearly $5 million went into review in 2024 (reported by the Jax Daily Record). Existing amenities: 20,000 sq ft clubhouse, lighted Hard-Tru tennis courts with a full-time pro, junior-Olympic saltwater pool, fitness centre, basketball and volleyball courts, a multi-purpose sports field, walking and biking trails, dog park and playground. Adjacent private golf: Jacksonville Golf & Country Club, Queen's Harbour (Mark McCumber), Windsor Parke Golf Club, Deerwood Country Club, and the Ponte Vedra/TPC Sawgrass cluster a short drive southeast.
facts.commercial_targets: Inside the gate: the club's practice facility and short-game area (freshly relevant post-2024 Furyk redesign), tee surrounds and cart-path edges, the multi-purpose sports field, dog park, playground, basketball and volleyball courts, and the pool-deck surround at the junior-Olympic saltwater pool — plus the clubhouse renovation project itself as a specification opportunity. Outside: University of North Florida athletics on Kernan Blvd (Hodges Stadium, Harmon Stadium, UNF Arena, and specifically the Hayt Golf Learning Center, which is a putting-surface prospect); Duval schools Kernan Trail Elementary, Kernan Middle and Sandalwood High; and the athlete-adjacent private training market that follows a community with this many pro sportspeople in it.
facts.landmarks: The gate is bounded by Hodges Boulevard on the east, Kernan Boulevard on the west and JTB (SR 202) on the south — the three roads every local uses for orientation. The 20,000 sq ft clubhouse and the Furyk-redesigned course itself. Villini at Glen Kernan (the villa enclave). Roughly 10 minutes to the Jacksonville beaches, 15 to downtown. University of North Florida sits directly across Kernan Blvd; Mayo Clinic Florida is on San Pablo Rd nearby; St. Johns Town Center is a short run west on JTB.

facts.strongest_angle: COMMERCIAL AND INSTITUTIONAL — NOT RESIDENTIAL. Every other page in this batch is written to a homeowner. Southside should not be. It is Jacksonville's office, retail, hospital, university and entertainment district, and the money here is spent by property managers, facilities directors, general contractors and club boards, not by someone standing in their backyard. Lead the page with commercial installs: multifamily and hotel dog parks and courtyards, office-park terraces and corporate putting greens, retail and restaurant patios, hospital healing gardens, gym and indoor sports flooring, golf practice facilities, and school and university athletic surfaces. Anchor it with names a facilities manager recognises — Topgolf on Brightman, the Hayt Golf Learning Center at UNF, St. Johns Town Center, Baptist South, Deerwood's redesign. Then use the residential neighborhoods (Baymeadows, Bartram Park, Mandarin, San Jose, Deerwood) purely as internal links so the pillar feeds the child pages rather than competing with them. Commercial work is also the fastest route from $7–8/sq ft to $10–12/sq ft, because commercial buyers price on spec compliance, warranty and installer credentials rather than on square-foot comparison shopping.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: Duval is a consolidated city-county: City of Jacksonville code governs the entire Southside with no separate municipal layer, which is a genuine simplification versus Clay, Nassau and St. Johns and worth stating on the pillar page. HONEST GAP: I could not verify whether COJ Chapter 656 zoning regulates artificial turf, impervious-surface percentages or landscape substitution — Municode returned 403 on every attempt — and this matters far more for commercial installs (where landscape buffer and pervious-area requirements bite) than for backyards. The client must confirm with COJ Planning & Development, and should treat 'we handle the code and the landscape-plan review' as a paid service line rather than a claim. Private rules layer on top: Simon Property Group standards at the Town Center, individual CDDs, and country club covenants.
facts.water_and_rules: JEA across the region. SJRWMD irrigation rule applies: Daylight Saving Time, up to two days a week — odd addresses Wednesday and Saturday, even addresses Thursday and Sunday, NONRESIDENTIAL Tuesday and Friday — before 10 a.m. or after 4 p.m. only; reclaimed water exempt unless locally restricted. The nonresidential Tuesday/Friday line matters most on THIS page, because Southside's audience is commercial property managers watering large ornamental and turf areas on a two-day-a-week ceiling. Winter EST schedule unverified (JEA page CAPTCHA-gated) — confirm before publishing. No artificial turf rebate found. Florida Statutes 373.185(3)(b) and 720.3075 protect Florida-Friendly Landscaping from local and HOA prohibition but do not cover artificial turf.
facts.soil_and_yard: Flatwoods sand over a shallow seasonal water table, with an extensive engineered stormwater pond network across every post-1990 development. Jacksonville sits about 3 ft above sea level, receives roughly 52 inches of rain a year concentrated May–September in brief intense downpours, and has sand-and-clay rather than limestone soils, so sinkholes are rare but surface ponding is chronic. Older Southside Estates and San Jose lots carry heavy mature canopy and root-compacted soil; Town Center-era sites are fill pads that settle. For commercial work the governing problems are compaction under high foot traffic, pond-edge grading and stormwater retention credit — not shade.
facts.housing_stock: Checked 2026-09-07. Southside is a REGION, not a neighborhood — east and south of the St. Johns River, north of Mandarin, spanning roughly zips 32216, 32217, 32224, 32246, 32256, 32257 and 32258. It contains Baymeadows, Bartram Park, Deerwood, Deercreek, Southpoint, Sunbeam, San Jose, the Town Center area and Southside Estates. Housing therefore spans the widest range in the batch: 1950s–60s concrete-block ranch on quarter-acre lots in Southside Estates; 1960s–70s San Jose (a historic suburban neighborhood with varied architecture); 1980s–2000s gated estate homes in Deerwood — 'the first gated community in Florida' — and Deercreek (roughly 750 homes east of Philips Highway); and 2000s–2020s apartments, townhomes and mixed-use around St. Johns Town Center. Southpoint is not residential at all: it is a commercial section of office centres and medical facilities. STRATEGIC NOTE for the client: a 'Southside' page will cannibalise its own child pages (Baymeadows, Bartram Park, Mandarin, San Marco) if written as another neighborhood page. It should be built as the regional PILLAR — the hub that links down to every Southside neighborhood page — and it should own the commercial keyword set the neighborhood pages do not.
facts.who_lives_there: Spans the full range. ZIP 32256 (Baymeadows/Deerwood/Southpoint): population 58,192, median household income $73,570, median home value $382,500, median age 34.4, 52.8% bachelor's or higher, 24.6% one-year mobility. ZIP 32258 (Bartram Park/south Mandarin): population 40,408, median household income $102,204, median home value $370,700, median age 36.2, 47% bachelor's or higher. Together this is where Jacksonville's corporate white-collar workforce lives, works and shops — young, highly educated, high-churn, and concentrated around the JTB / I-295 employment and retail spine. The Deerwood and Deercreek gated communities hold the region's genuine high-net-worth residential pockets.
facts.golf: Deerwood Country Club, 10239 Golf Club Drive, Jacksonville FL 32256 — founded 1960, original George Cobb design, hosted the Greater Jacksonville Open in years between 1967 and 1976 per the club, currently in a full Erik Larsen redesign to roughly 7,350 yards completing 2027 with a new par-3 short course opening mid-2026. Deercreek Country Club — gated, 700+ homes, driving range, tennis, pickleball. Jacksonville Golf & Country Club, 3985 Hunt Club Road, 32224 — private, member-owned. Windsor Parke Golf Club, 13823 Sutton Park Drive, 32224 — public, 'Jacksonville's home for public golf.' Topgolf, 10531 Brightman Blvd, 32246 — the single most obvious commercial synthetic-turf prospect on the entire map. UNF's Hayt Golf Learning Center on the university campus. This is the densest concentration of named golf facilities in the client's whole service area outside Ponte Vedra.
facts.commercial_targets: This is the whole point of the page. Topgolf, 10531 Brightman Blvd — hitting bays, target greens, patio areas. UNF athletics: Hodges Stadium, Harmon Stadium, UNF Arena surrounds and above all the Hayt Golf Learning Center, an existing golf-practice facility that is a natural synthetic-green prospect. St. Johns Town Center — Simon-managed common areas, tenant patios, the Nordstrom/Dillard's/Target/Dick's anchor frontages, and the outdoor event lawn. Baptist Medical Center South courtyards and healing gardens. Deerwood Country Club (mid-redesign through 2027, new par-3 course mid-2026) and Deercreek Country Club. Corporate campus courtyards and rooftop terraces throughout Southpoint and Deerwood Park. The Foundry Commercial industrial redevelopment sites (403,000 sq ft of spec warehouse). Hotel pool decks and courtyards along JTB. Indoor sports and training facilities along Philips Highway. Daycares and pet resorts region-wide.
facts.landmarks: St. Johns Town Center, 4663 River City Drive — opened March 18, 2005, 51.2 acres, 1,391,569 sq ft of leasable space, anchored by Nordstrom, Dillard's, Target and a flagship Dick's Sporting Goods, owned 50% and managed by Simon Property Group, with the region's only Gucci, Louis Vuitton and Tiffany & Co. Topgolf at 10531 Brightman Blvd. IKEA and Sprouts Farmers Market nearby. University of North Florida — 1,300-acre campus inside a nature preserve, roughly 16,400 students, NCAA Division I Ospreys in the ASUN Conference with 17 varsity sports; UNF Arena (6,300 capacity), Harmon Stadium (baseball), Hodges Stadium (soccer and track), Hayt Golf Learning Center, miles of nature trails. Baptist Medical Center South, 14550 Old St. Augustine Road. Deerwood and Deercreek country clubs. J. Turner Butler Boulevard and the I-295 East Beltway. Southpoint office district.

facts.strongest_angle: GOLF-COMMUNITY CREDIBILITY PLUS AGING ASSOCIATION COMMON AREAS. Baymeadows is the one page where the client can name real clubs and real members: 'we build practice greens for people who play Deerwood and Deercreek.' These customers know what a green should roll like, they will ask about stimp and grain, and they will pay $10–12/sq ft for a green that reads true — which is precisely the price move the client wants. Deerwood's active Larsen redesign and its new par-3 short course opening mid-2026 give the page a live, timely hook nobody else has. The second half of the page is the opposite of new-build turf marketing: a 1968-founded suburb whose condo and townhome associations are now replacing forty-year-old shaded courtyards, entry medians and pool decks where grass has not grown in a decade. That common-area, board-approved, spec-driven work is a completely different sale from Bartram Park's brand-new apartment dog parks, from Julington Creek's private acreage, and from Riverside's one-off historic craftsmanship jobs.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: Duval consolidated city-county, so City of Jacksonville code applies with no separate municipal layer. I could NOT verify whether COJ Chapter 656 addresses artificial turf — Municode returned 403 repeatedly — so no permit claims should be published without a call to COJ Planning & Development. The governing rules in practice are private: condominium association documents and country club community covenants. Deercreek's HOA (DCCOA) controls common areas separately from the country club; Deerwood is a gated community with its own standards. Because synthetic turf is outside the Florida-Friendly Landscaping statutory protection, these associations can and do set standards — pile height, colour, infill, edge detail. The commercial play is to get specified BY the association, not to fight it.
facts.water_and_rules: JEA water and sewer. SJRWMD irrigation rule: Daylight Saving Time, up to two days per week — odd addresses Wednesday and Saturday, even addresses Thursday and Sunday, nonresidential Tuesday and Friday — before 10 a.m. or after 4 p.m. only; reclaimed water exempt unless locally restricted. Winter Eastern Standard Time schedule unverified (JEA's own page is CAPTCHA-gated); confirm by phone. No turf rebate found. As everywhere in this batch, Florida Statutes 373.185(3)(b) and 720.3075 protect Florida-Friendly Landscaping from local and HOA prohibition but do NOT cover artificial turf, so condo and country-club associations here can restrict it — which matters more in Baymeadows than anywhere, because so much of the ground is association-controlled common area rather than private yard.
facts.soil_and_yard: Flatwoods sand over a shallow seasonal water table, with the specific complication of a 40-to-50-year-old suburb: heavy mature canopy over the original single-family streets, so the classic 'grass will not grow under the oak' failure is well advanced; compacted, root-bound soil from decades of foot and mower traffic; and irrigation systems installed in the 1970s and 80s that leak, run dry zones and are expensive to rezone. Jacksonville averages about 52 inches of rain a year concentrated May–September, at roughly 3 ft above sea level on sand-and-clay soils. Condo and townhome courtyards are small, hard-shaded by two-story buildings, and get zero direct sun — the single most reliable synthetic-turf conversion in Florida.
facts.housing_stock: Checked 2026-09-07. Baymeadows developed around a private golf community that opened in 1968, and the neighborhood's DNA is still that of a late-1960s-through-1990s golf suburb. Zip 32256, centred on Baymeadows Road and Baymeadows Road East. Housing splits three ways: (1) 1970s–1990s detached single family on the original golf-era streets — ranch and two-story, lots typically 0.2–0.3 acre, now under 40–50 years of mature tree canopy; (2) a very large 1970s–1980s condominium and townhome stock with small private patios and extensive shared common ground; (3) a heavy apartment inventory, still growing — The Vale at Baymeadows, 276 units on Baymeadows Road East (formerly Courtney Meadows), sold for $42 million in April 2026. To the immediate east, in the same ZIP, sit the estate-scale gated country club communities: Deerwood (described as the first gated community in Florida) and Deercreek (a gated country club community of roughly 750 homes east of Philips Highway). Not new-build, not historic — this is the middle-aged suburb of the batch, and the aging is exactly the opportunity.
facts.who_lives_there: ZIP 32256 (Census Reporter / ACS): population 58,192 across 61.4 sq mi; median household income $73,570 (±$5,226) — notably LOWER than 32258's $102,204, because the apartment stock pulls it down; median home value $382,500 (±$19,295), about 10% above state and national; median age 34.4, well below Florida's 42.6; 52.8% (±2.3) hold a bachelor's degree or higher, the highest educational attainment in this batch; 24.6% one-year mobility rate, a strikingly high churn figure that confirms the renter-heavy character. The barbell is the story: the same ZIP contains the $42M apartment complex and Deerwood Country Club estate homes. Two completely different customers, one page — write for the estate owner and the condo association board, not the renter.
facts.golf: This is the golf ZIP of the batch and the page should lead with it. Deerwood Country Club, 10239 Golf Club Drive, Jacksonville FL 32256 — established 1960, original course by George Cobb, the club's own site states it hosted the Greater Jacksonville Open across multiple years between 1967 and 1976, and it is currently in a comprehensive Erik Larsen redesign to roughly 7,350 yards due for completion in 2027, with a NEW PAR-3 SHORT COURSE opening mid-2026 plus tennis, pickleball, fitness, spa and aquatics. Deercreek Country Club — gated, private roads, 700+ homes around the course, with tennis, driving range, pool, pickleball and playground, HOA common areas managed by the DCCOA and golf by the club. Nearby in 32224: Jacksonville Golf & Country Club, 3985 Hunt Club Road (private, member-owned, ten minutes from the beaches) and Windsor Parke Golf Club, 13823 Sutton Park Drive (public). HONEST GAP: I could not verify the current status or fate of the original Baymeadows Golf Club course itself — the club that opened in 1968 — and the client should phone-check it before naming it on the page.
facts.commercial_targets: Deerwood Country Club — actively spending, mid-redesign through 2027 with a new par-3 short course opening mid-2026; a live prospect for practice greens, tee-line surrounds, clubhouse lawn and nursery turf. Deercreek Country Club common areas, driving range surrounds, pickleball and playground zones (DCCOA-managed). The very large 1970s–1990s condominium and townhome associations along Baymeadows Road — tired pool decks, entry medians and courtyards being re-landscaped, which is the most under-served synthetic turf market in Jacksonville. Corporate office park courtyards and rooftop terraces at Southpoint and Deerwood Park. Daycares, veterinary clinics and pet boarding along Baymeadows Road. Deerwood Village retail patios.
facts.landmarks: Baymeadows Road and Baymeadows Road East. Deerwood Country Club at 10239 Golf Club Drive (with the Erik Larsen redesign and 2026 par-3 course under way). Deercreek Country Club, gated, east of Philips Highway. Deerwood Village shopping centre, where the first Jacksonville Potbelly Sandwich Works opened in May 2026. The former AT&T American Transtech campus, subject of a roughly $2 million demolition to clear the site for two speculative warehouses totalling 403,000 sq ft under Foundry Commercial — a visible, checkable sign of the neighborhood's office-to-industrial turn. The Vale at Baymeadows, 276 units, sold $42M April 2026. Southpoint and Deerwood Park office concentrations just north.

facts.strongest_angle: BIG, SHADY, SOGGY, UNREGULATED BACKYARDS. This is the only place in the batch where the yard is simultaneously large, heavily wooded, chronically wet, and frequently free of any HOA architectural review. Lead with the two-part failure the homeowner has already lived: 'your St. Augustine died under the oaks, and the low corner by the creek has never dried out.' Then lead the offer with what the acreage makes possible — a real practice green with genuine approach length, a bunker, and a chipping fringe, plus engineered drainage under the whole thing. This is the page where the client earns $10–12/sq ft, because the job is big, technically hard, and the customer has $100k+ household income and a $370k+ house on water. It reads nothing like Bartram Park next door, where the pitch is a tiny fenced dog yard and an ARC form, and nothing like Riverside, where the pitch is a 400-square-foot courtyard.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: Duval County is a consolidated city-county, so there is no separate municipal government here: City of Jacksonville rules apply directly. I could NOT verify whether Jacksonville's Chapter 656 zoning code addresses artificial turf — Municode returned 403 on every attempt — so the client must confirm with COJ Planning & Development before making any 'no permit needed' claim on the site. Practically, the differentiator on this page is the ABSENCE of restriction: many of the older Duval-side streets have no HOA and no architectural review committee, so the homeowner can simply proceed. Say that plainly. Where a newer subdivision HOA does exist, remember that Florida's Florida-Friendly Landscaping protections do not extend to synthetic turf, so the HOA can lawfully say no.
facts.water_and_rules: JEA (Jacksonville Electric Authority) supplies water and sewer on the Duval side; larger acreage parcels near Hood Landing may still be on private wells and septic. Irrigation is governed by the St. Johns River Water Management District rule, which applies to well and utility water alike: during Daylight Saving Time, up to two days a week — odd-numbered addresses Wednesday and Saturday, even-numbered addresses Thursday and Sunday, nonresidential Tuesday and Friday — and only before 10 a.m. or after 4 p.m. Reclaimed water is exempt unless locally restricted. NOTE: I could not verify JEA's own published page (it is CAPTCHA-gated) or the Eastern Standard Time winter schedule; cite SJRWMD, not JEA, and have the client confirm the winter days by phone before publishing. No turf-specific rebate found. IMPORTANT and load-bearing across all five pages: Florida Statute 373.185(3)(b) bars local ordinances from prohibiting Florida-Friendly Landscaping and 720.3075 bars HOA documents from doing the same — BUT artificial turf is NOT inside the statutory definition of Florida-Friendly Landscaping. Do not let the client claim state law protects turf installs. It does not.
facts.soil_and_yard: Sand over a seasonally shallow water table. This is the wettest ground in the batch: the neighborhood sits at the confluence of Julington Creek, Durbin Creek, Big Davis Creek and Cormorant Branch, all draining to the St. Johns, and the 2,031-acre Julington-Durbin Preserve (Duval County, managed by SJRWMD) is the undeveloped wetland peninsula immediately south. Creek-adjacent lots carry organic muck, seasonal standing water and tidal influence. Jacksonville averages roughly 52 inches of rain a year, concentrated May–September in short intense downpours, and sits at about 3 ft above sea level with sand-and-clay rather than limestone soils. Heavy live oak and pine canopy over most of the older lots means dense shade plus leaf and acorn litter. The technical sell here is drainage engineering — deep base, aggressive slope, and a French-drain tie-in — not water conservation.
facts.housing_stock: Checked 2026-09-07. CRITICAL DISAMBIGUATION the client's competitors get wrong: 'Julington Creek Plantation' is a St. Johns County CDD community in Fruit Cove (32259). The DUVAL side is different — it is the southern tail of Mandarin on the north bank of the creek, zip 32258, along Hood Landing Road, Julington Creek Road, Cormorant Branch, Mandarin Road south end and the bottom of San Jose Blvd. Housing here is predominantly 1970s–1990s custom and semi-custom detached homes on large wooded lots (commonly 0.3 acre to 1+ acre, with true acreage parcels near the water), plus creekfront homes with private docks. Not new-build, not tract. Backyards are the largest in this batch by a wide margin — deep, mature, tree-covered, and often running down to water. HOA prevalence is LOW to moderate: many of these streets predate the CDD era entirely and have no architectural review at all, which is the opposite of Bartram Park two miles east. Newer 1990s–2000s infill subdivisions do carry conventional HOAs.
facts.who_lives_there: ZIP 32258 (Census Reporter / ACS): population 40,408; median household income $102,204 (±$11,612), about 1.3x the Jacksonville metro figure and ~25% above the national median; median home value $370,700 (±$13,603); median age 36.2; 47% (±3.9) hold a bachelor's degree or higher, ~1.3x the metro rate; veteran share 11.6% (±2.1) versus 6.2% nationally — an unusually high military/ex-military concentration (NAS Jacksonville, Mayport). Caveat stated honestly: 32258 is a large ZIP that also contains Bartram Park and much of south Mandarin, so these figures are the aggregate, not a neighborhood-level read. The Duval creekside streets specifically skew older, wealthier and more land-rich than the ZIP average; the ZIP's median is pulled down by Bartram Park apartments.
facts.golf: There is no golf course inside the Duval-side neighborhood, and the page should not pretend otherwise. Adjacent, across the county line: Julington Creek Golf Club (inside Julington Creek Plantation, St. Johns County), Cimarrone Golf Club and St. Johns Golf & Country Club. Nearest Duval private clubs are Deerwood Country Club (10239 Golf Club Drive, 32256 — George Cobb 1960 design, mid-redesign by Erik Larsen through 2027) and Deercreek Country Club, both ~15 minutes north. The realistic golf revenue here is BACKYARD PUTTING GREENS, and unlike anywhere else in this batch these yards are big enough for a genuine multi-hole practice complex with 30–60 ft approach shots, a chipping fringe and a bunker — not a 12x15 postage stamp. Sell length.
facts.commercial_targets: Clark's Fish Camp (waterfront deck and outdoor seating). Julington Creek Fish Camp and Marina. Mandarin-corridor veterinary clinics, groomers and boarding kennels along San Jose Blvd. Mandarin High School and Greenland Pines Elementary athletic areas. Boat and marina businesses along Hood Landing Road. Waterfront event venues. This is the thinnest commercial market of the five — be honest with the client that Julington Creek Duval is a residential-only page and the commercial pitch belongs on the Southside and Bartram Park pages.
facts.landmarks: Clark's Fish Camp on Hood Landing Road — the local institution, and the single most recognisable name in the neighborhood. Julington Creek Fish Camp and Marina on San Jose Blvd. Hood Landing public kayak launch. Tommy Hazouri Sr. Park boat ramp. Julington-Durbin Creek Preserve (2,031 acres, three marked hiking trails, horseback riding and cycling, SJRWMD-managed) on the peninsula where the two creeks meet. The Bartram Canoe Trail runs from Durbin Creek to Julington Creek. Harriet Beecher Stowe wrote about visiting the creek in her 1873 memoir Palmetto Leaves — a genuinely local, checkable literary hook nobody else will use. Mandarin Park.

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH SMALL-FORMAT, HIGH-MARGIN WORK — COURTYARDS, DOG RUNS AND PRACTICE GREENS — NOT WHOLE BACK YARDS. This corridor is young (median age 33.6), highly educated (57% degreed), well paid (median household income $88,259) and extremely transient (a quarter of residents moved in the last year). A large share live in condos, townhomes and apartments, and a third rent. That combination kills the standard 'transform your back yard forever' pitch and creates a different, better-margin one: a 300–600 sq ft courtyard or pool-deck install, a balcony or rooftop terrace, a small dog run for a renter-heavy dog-heavy population, and — because Windsor Parke is in the same ZIP and TPC Sawgrass is 15 minutes away — a compact 2–3 hole practice green for a golfer with no room for a real one. The second, larger opportunity is B2B: multi-family and condo association common areas, which the 2025 state preemption does NOT cover, so they are won on maintenance economics and board persuasion rather than on a statute. Explicitly different from Ponte Vedra Beach next door (estate-scale championship greens) and from Oceanway (family drainage jobs on big flat lots). RECOMMENDATION: because the boundary and the neighbourhood identity could not be verified, consider publishing this as a Beach Boulevard / 32224–32250 corridor page rather than a 'Beach Haven' town page, or folding it into a beaches-corridor page.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: Duval/Jacksonville has no artificial-turf ordinance, and since 19 May 2026 could not enforce a ban on a compliant install on a single-family lot ≤1 acre anyway (s. 125.572 F.S. / DEP Rule 62-308.100). But that preemption explicitly excludes condominiums, duplexes, parks, athletic fields and commercial property — and it does not touch HOA or deed restrictions. In a corridor this heavily attached and rental, the decision-maker is usually a condo board or a property manager, not a homeowner and not the city. Practical consequence for the page: sell to boards and managers with a maintenance-cost and liability argument, and keep DEP-compliance documentation (permeable subgrade, natural silica/shell infill, no PFAS or heavy metals, no change to stormwater) ready as reassurance even where the rule does not legally apply.
facts.water_and_rules: JEA water/sewer. SJRWMD rules; as of 2026 the Phase III Extreme Water Shortage order applies to all of Duval — one irrigation day per week, none between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m., odd/no address Saturday, even Sunday, nonresidential Tuesday, one hour and ¾ inch per zone. No artificial-turf rebate from JEA or the City. Coastal-specific rule points from DEP Rule 62-308.100: turf must be installed landward of any dune system and must not replace existing dune vegetation, and must sit at least 10 ft back from any natural or man-made waterbody (measured from ordinary/mean high water) unless there is a seawall or bulkhead — relevant on Intracoastal-side and lagoon lots. Also note the preemption is single-family only, so it gives no leverage at all with the condo and townhome associations that make up much of this corridor.
facts.soil_and_yard: Coastal sand ridge and relict dune sand rather than inland flatwoods — fast-draining, nutrient-poor, with a shallow water table close to the Intracoastal and salt spray in the mix. St. Augustine here is thin and needs constant water and feeding, and one day a week of irrigation under Phase III will not carry it through a Northeast Florida summer. Yards on the 1990s–2000s single-family stock are small and mostly sunny; heavy live-oak shade is confined to the older pockets. A lot of the addressable square footage is not lawn at all — it is courtyards, pool decks, side yards, balconies and shared common areas.
facts.housing_stock: HONEST CAVEAT FIRST — this is by far the thinnest place in the batch and the research does not support a village-style page. 'Beach Haven' has no Wikipedia entry, no verifiable neighbourhood association, no OpenStreetMap place node and no 'Beach Haven' street in Duval County (Overpass returns only a private cul-de-sac, Beach Haven Place, at 30.2486, -81.5185 near JTB/Kernan). It functions as a real-estate-portal region name. zipdatamaps places it across ZIP codes 32224 and 32250 — i.e. the Beach Boulevard corridor between the Intracoastal Waterway and Jacksonville Beach. Sources disagree wildly because each portal draws a different polygon: NeighborhoodScout gives a $530,208 median value in 32224; realtor.com gives a $295,000 median list price; proximitii claims $463,485 and 21,843 residents. Anchor on ACS ZIP data, not the portals. What is consistent: this is NOT a single-era neighbourhood. BestNeighborhood.org puts the average home built around 1998 with pockets 80+ years old; NeighborhoodScout describes the stock as "medium sized (three or four bedroom) to small (studio to two bedroom) single-family homes and apartment complexes/high-rise apartments" at a 2.3% vacancy rate; homes.com describes "a mix of newly-constructed homes and properties built more than 50 years ago." So: 1990s–2000s single-family on modest lots, plus a very large share of condo, townhome and apartment product along Beach Blvd, Kernan and Hodges. Renters are roughly 35%.
facts.who_lives_there: Young, high-earning, high-turnover professionals. ZIP 32224 (Census Reporter ACS): population 42,092, median household income $88,259, per-capita income $50,984, median home value $458,100, median age 33.6, 97% high-school and 57% bachelor's degree attainment, 15.1% foreign-born, poverty 10.9%, average commute 22.2 minutes — and 24.5% of residents moved within the past year, about double the national rate, because the University of North Florida is inside this ZIP. NeighborhoodScout adds that 61.9% of the working population is in executive, management and professional occupations, and that 3.1% of households are same-sex couples, well above the national average.
facts.golf: The golf-rich half of the batch. Windsor Parke Golf Club, 13823 Sutton Park Drive, Jacksonville 32224 — public, 18 holes, in the same ZIP. Jacksonville Beach Golf Club (municipal). Queen's Harbour Yacht & Country Club, Queens Harbor Blvd, 32225. Jacksonville Golf & Country Club. Glen Kernan Golf & Country Club. Atlantic Beach Country Club. Deerwood Country Club, Golf Club Drive, 32256. And 15 minutes south: Ponte Vedra Inn & Club, Marsh Landing Country Club and TPC Sawgrass. High golf density, but the customers here mostly live in small-lot or attached homes — which points at practice greens and short-game areas, not 3,000 sq ft installs.
facts.commercial_targets: Pet Doctors of America, Beach Blvd, 32250. Banfield Pet Hospital. Schools: San Pablo Elementary, Chets Creek Elementary, Kernan Trail Elementary, Kernan Middle, Alimacani Elementary, Duncan U. Fletcher High and Middle, Jacksonville Beach Elementary, plus private/parochial — Beaches Chapel School, Discovery Montessori School, Seabreeze School, St. Paul's by the Sea Episcopal Day School, The Foundation Academy. UNF athletics facilities (Hodges Stadium complex, soccer and softball). A Social Affair Dance Studio, Beach Blvd, 32224. Windsor Parke Golf Club practice areas. Above all: the condominium, townhome and apartment associations along Beach Blvd, Kernan and Hodges — pool decks, courtyards, dog-relief areas and entry medians.
facts.landmarks: University of North Florida — 1,300-acre campus at I-295 and J. Turner Butler Blvd, ~16,400 students, UNF Arena (6,300 seats) and Hodges Stadium. The Beach Boulevard corridor and Intracoastal Waterway bridges. Duncan U. Fletcher High School and Fletcher Middle in Neptune Beach. Jacksonville Beach. Windsor Parke and Sutton Park. Kernan Blvd and Hodges Blvd.

facts.strongest_angle: Lead with the absentee owner. 44.2% of Butler Beach's housing units sat vacant at the 2020 census — this is a second-home and vacation-rental coast where the owner is usually somewhere else. The page should open on the yard that looks identical in August and in February with nobody there: no lawn service invoice arriving all winter, no dead St. Augustine patch greeting a guest who is about to leave a review, no watering-day compliance problem while you are in Ohio, and — under the Phase III ban on establishment watering for new sod — no legal way for the competing solution (re-sod it) to even work right now. Pair that with the 43.3%-over-65 resident who is done with a mower and would rather have a two-hole putting green. That is a completely different page from every neighbor: St. Augustine Beach next door is an incorporated city with its own code, Jacksonville Beach is high-income volume and municipal golf, and Atlantic Beach is a written city turf spec. Butler Beach's page is about the yard that maintains itself while the owner is 900 miles away, sold to a retiree-and-investor market with a real but modest $81K median income — so price it on durability and unattended performance, not on luxury finish.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: The most useful structural fact about Butler Beach: it is a census-designated place with NO municipal government. There is no city building department, no city turf ordinance, no municipal impervious cap. The St. Johns County Land Development Code and county permitting apply, full stop. That is a genuine competitive point against St. Augustine Beach immediately north, which IS an incorporated city with its own code, and against the three Duval beach cities. Private restrictions — condo docs and subdivision covenants — are the real gate here, and Florida law limits an HOA's ability to outright ban artificial turf (secondary-source characterization; verify the current statute text before putting it on the page as a legal claim).
facts.water_and_rules: Provider: St. Johns County Utility Department (potable and reclaimed). Under the SJRWMD Phase III Extreme Water Shortage Declaration issued/effective mid-May 2026 (May 11 per St. Johns County, May 13 per the District's own release), covering Clay, Duval, Flagler, Nassau, Putnam and St. Johns counties: landscape irrigation limited to ONE day per week, never between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m., max 3/4 inch and one hour per zone. Residential odd addresses Saturday, even addresses Sunday, non-residential Tuesday. Restrictions apply to private wells and pumps too, not just utility water. Crucially, irrigation restrictions on NEW plantings including sod were tightened under Phase III — so a homeowner replacing a dead lawn cannot legally water it in. Micro-irrigation/drip and hand-held hoses are exempt. Enforcement via the SJC Connect app or Code Enforcement, (904) 209-0734 / codenf@sjcfl.us. No rebate program is listed on the county's water page, and nothing indicates artificial turf qualifies for one — do not claim a rebate. Statewide, FS 125.572 (Ch. 2025-140) directs FDEP to adopt minimum synthetic turf standards for single-family lots of 1 acre or less and preempts inconsistent local rules once adopted.
facts.soil_and_yard: Relict barrier-island dune sand on Anastasia Island — the CDP is a 2.66 sq mi strip with the Atlantic on one side and the Matanzas River on the other. Fast infiltration along the dune ridge, but low interior and riverside parcels sit close to the water table. Constant salt wind and thin topsoil make St. Augustine grass expensive to hold. Less live-oak canopy than the Duval beach towns. (Barrier-island geology and salt exposure are inferred from the confirmed geography rather than from a soil survey — worth a spot-check before the page states it as fact.)
facts.housing_stock: 1950s–1980s low-slung concrete-block and frame beach cottages, later ocean-side stilt/piling construction, plus condos and duplexes and scattered 2000s+ infill, on the A1A grid between the Atlantic and the Matanzas River. 4,530 housing units across a 2.66 sq mi CDP. The headline number: 44.2% of those units were VACANT at the 2020 census — that is seasonal/second-home/vacation-rental vacancy, not distress. Median house/condo value ~$551,966 (2024 est), mean detached ~$815,019, mean townhouse/attached ~$534,540, median gross rent $1,872. Lots are modest island parcels; backyards small to medium, and oceanfront parcels often have no true backyard at all. Not new-build suburbia and not a historic district — it is a mid-century barrier-island beach subdivision that has been steadily reinvested in. HOA coverage is patchy because this is unincorporated county subdivision land; condo/association documents matter more here than single-family HOA covenants.
facts.who_lives_there: Median age 62.5 — far older than the Duval beaches. 43.3% aged 65 or over, only 9.2% under 18. 92.4% White, 100% classified urban. Median household income ~$81,285 (2024 est), per capita ~$59,712, poverty 10.1%. Population 4,978 at the 2020 census (4,951 in 2010) — essentially flat. Most residents own. Practically: retirees and second-home owners plus a large short-term-rental investor cohort. Materially lower income than Atlantic/Neptune/Jacksonville Beach, so this page should sell durability and absence-proofing, not luxury.
facts.golf: Honest answer: this is the weakest field for Butler Beach and the page should NOT lead with golf. There is no course inside the CDP and no on-course golf community. Golf options are in the wider St. Augustine / Anastasia Island market, several miles north or across the Matanzas. Do not name a 'Butler Beach golf course' — there isn't one. The residual golf angle is demographic, not geographic: a community that is 43.3% over 65 is the single best backyard putting-green demographic in the batch, because these are the people who actually play. Sell the practice green to the retiree, not to the neighborhood.
facts.commercial_targets: St. Johns County School District schools serving the CDP: W.D. Hartley Elementary, Gamble Rogers Middle School, Pedro Menendez High School. Vacation-rental management companies along A1A South (the highest-value target given 44.2% vacancy). Condo and homeowner association common areas — pool decks, entry medians, clubhouse surrounds. Frank B. Butler County Park is county-owned (St. Johns County Parks & Recreation procurement). Note: there is no walkable commercial district here comparable to Beaches Town Center, so restaurant-patio and boutique work is thin — the commercial money is rental managers and associations.
facts.landmarks: Frank B. Butler County Park — oceanfront access via the Mary Street beach ramp ($10 parking) with free parking on Gloria Avenue, plus a riverside park on the Matanzas; restrooms, showers, grills, picnic pavilions, seasonal lifeguards, leashed dogs allowed. A1A South. Roughly 8 miles south of St. Augustine's historic district, sitting between St. Augustine Beach to the north and Crescent Beach to the south. The civil-rights history is checkable and locally respected: Frank B. Butler (1885–1973), a Lincolnville grocer and real-estate investor, began buying Anastasia Island oceanfront in 1927 and platted the Butler's Beach subdivision in 1947 — the only beach open to Black Floridians between Jacksonville and Daytona, with a resort, bathhouse, inn and casino. The land passed to St. Johns County in 1980 on condition it carry his name.

facts.strongest_angle: Smallest yards, biggest money — lead with the small-yard premium job. Neptune Beach carries roughly the same household income as Jacksonville Beach ($119,294 vs $115,825) and the highest median property value of the five ($670,900), on 2.34 sq mi — the smallest land base in the batch — where the typical backyard is a shaded 30x40 patch under live oaks that St. Augustine grass has already lost. The page should say plainly: your yard is too small and too shaded to grow grass, and it is also too small for the square-footage discount every other installer is quoting you. Then sell the finish: 800–2,000 sq ft, shade-proof, dog-proof, installed in a day, every seam visible from the back door because the whole yard is visible from the back door. This is exactly where $10–12/sq ft is defensible — small jobs where the customer is buying craftsmanship, not acreage, and where a 73% owner-occupancy rate with almost no HOA layer means one person decides. Deliberately different from the neighbors: Jacksonville Beach leads on municipal golf and job-type variety; Atlantic Beach leads on the city's written turf spec and larger Selva Marina lots; Butler Beach leads on absentee owners. Neptune's lead is that it is small, shaded, wealthy and unregulated — a fast, high-margin, high-craft install with no committee to satisfy.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: Neptune Beach incorporated on August 11, 1931 after seceding from Jacksonville Beach over a tax dispute — residents felt underserved while paying equal taxes — and it resisted the 1968 Duval consolidation alongside Jacksonville Beach, Atlantic Beach and Baldwin. So it has its own city code and building department, even though residents vote in Jacksonville's mayoral election and are represented on the Jacksonville city council. Honest gap: I could not confirm a Neptune Beach synthetic-turf ordinance or a specific impervious/lot-coverage limit from public sources — verify with the city at (904) 270-2400 before the page makes a code claim. Note the contrast worth using in copy: Atlantic Beach immediately north publishes a detailed turf specification; Neptune Beach does not appear to, so the compliance burden is lighter here. HOAs are largely ABSENT — this is old platted city grid, not covenant subdivision, so there is usually no architectural review committee standing between the homeowner and the decision.
facts.water_and_rules: The City of Neptune Beach runs its OWN water utility — three groundwater wells drawing from the Floridan Aquifer, serving roughly 7,270 people. Not JEA, not Jacksonville Beach. Utility billing at 116 First Street, (904) 270-2400; water and wastewater treatment at 2010 Forest Avenue. The provider being municipal does not exempt anyone: the SJRWMD Phase III Extreme Water Shortage (mid-May 2026, covering Duval) applies to all sources including private wells and pumps — one irrigation day per week, never 8 a.m.–6 p.m., odd addresses Saturday, even Sunday, non-residential Tuesday, 3/4 inch and one hour per zone maximum, with tightened limits on watering in new plantings and sod. No rebate identified for artificial turf.
facts.soil_and_yard: San Pablo Island sand. The decisive yard condition here is SHADE: mature live oaks and cabbage palms canopy the old cottage streets, and a large share of Neptune Beach backyards sit in dense, year-round shade where St. Augustine grass thins out and never comes back. Combine that with lot sizes that concentrate all foot traffic, dog traffic and kid traffic into a small area, and you get the textbook turf case — small, shaded, over-trafficked, permanently bare. About 52 inches of rain a year regionally, and low interior lots near the Intracoastal side hold water. (Canopy and soil character inferred from the town's confirmed age, density and barrier-island setting.)
facts.housing_stock: 1930s–1950s summer cottages originally built by Jacksonville families as beach getaways, plus 1950s–70s ranches, all on very small platted lots. 3,500 housing units, only 7.5% vacant (homeowner vacancy 1.0%, rental 5.8%) — the opposite of Butler Beach; people actually live here year-round. 73.1% owner-occupied. Median property value $670,900 (2024) — the HIGHEST of the five, on the SMALLEST land base. The city has just 2.34 sq mi of land (6.85 sq mi total, the rest water), making it the smallest of the Jacksonville Beaches communities. The practical consequence for turf: backyards are genuinely small — a large share of buildable area is house, driveway and setback — and the ongoing scrape-and-rebuild pressure makes them smaller still, because new construction maxes out the envelope. Not new-build suburbia, not a formal historic district: an old, dense, walkable city grid.
facts.who_lives_there: Median household income $119,294 (Data USA; Wikipedia cites $109,375 — use the range, not a single figure). Poverty just 3.07% — the lowest in this batch. 91.6% White, 5.6% Hispanic. Population 7,217 at the 2020 census, drifting down slightly since (about 6,984 by 2023) — the smallest of the beaches. 73.1% homeownership. These are established, settled owners in a walk-everywhere town, not transients and not a rental market. Decisions are made by the homeowner alone, which shortens the sales cycle considerably compared with HOA-governed towns.
facts.golf: Be straight about this on the page: there is no golf course and no golf community in Neptune Beach. The city has 2.34 sq mi of land — there is no room for one. The nearest named courses are Atlantic Beach Country Club immediately north on Selva Marina Drive and the municipal Jacksonville Beach Golf Club immediately south. Do not build this page on golf. Most Neptune backyards cannot hold a real multi-hole green; the honest, sellable version is a compact 2–3 hole chipping and putting setup that fits an 800–1,500 sq ft yard — which is a legitimate premium product, just not the page's lead.
facts.commercial_targets: Beaches Town Center storefronts, brick courtyards and outdoor seating — small-footprint, extremely high-visibility jobs in a pedestrian district, ideal portfolio pieces. The two oceanfront hotels at the Town Center. Restaurant patios and dog-friendly outdoor seating (Pete's, Ragtime, Sliders, Poe's, Coop 303) in a town with heavy dog traffic. Neptune Beach operates its own elementary and middle schools — a direct municipal procurement path for play areas and field work. A Jacksonville Public Library branch. Pet businesses and groomers serving a dense, walkable, dog-heavy population. Surf and paddle shops with small outdoor display areas.
facts.landmarks: Beaches Town Center, where Atlantic Boulevard meets the ocean — Atlantic Blvd is literally the Neptune Beach / Atlantic Beach line, and the district is shared between the two cities. Pete's Bar, a Neptune Beach institution since 1933, reputedly holding Duval County's first liquor license. Ragtime Tavern, Sliders Oyster Bar, North Beach Fish Camp, Lemon Bar, Poe's Tavern, Coop 303, Southern Grounds. The BookMark (independent bookstore), Aqua East Surf Shop, Jax Surf and Paddle, Drift Boutique, Milo Fashion. The town was named 'Neptune' by land dealer Eugene Gilbert in 1885; the name stuck when resident Dan G. Wheeler built a private train station near his home in 1922. (I could not confirm Jarboe Park from the sources checked — verify before naming it.)
